## Package com.pantrixui.components.container.card

### CardVariant

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.card.CardVariant`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class CardVariant
```

How a `PantrixCard` stands off what it sits on.

Entries:

- `Elevated`: Lifted off the page by a shadow, on the surface colour. The default. On iOS the preset has no shadow, and the surface colour alone sets the card apart.
- `Filled`: Tinted rather than lifted, in the neutral role's container: for a card on a surface that is already raised.
- `Outlined`: Edged by a hairline in the divider colour: for dense lists of cards, where many shadows become noise.

Documented on: [Card](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/card.md)

### PantrixCard

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.card.PantrixCard`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCard(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: CardVariant = CardVariant.Elevated,
    onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: CardStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(CardStyle, style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: CardColors? = null,
    contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(PantrixTheme.spacing.lg),
    header: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    media: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    footer: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A container for one subject: a header, a body and actions on a surface of their own, with media edge to edge above them.

Given `onClick`, the whole card is one button. That is the accessible way to build a card that opens something: a screen reader announces one target, with the card's text or its `contentDescription`, rather than leaving the user to find which of the card's children is the real link. A button in the `footer` keeps its own press.

On the theme's surface, where an elevated and an outlined card stand, the card gives what it holds no colour: each child draws in its own default, a text in `textPrimary`. A `CardVariant.Filled` card, and one given a role's colour as its fill, gives the colour that reads on that fill. A card that cannot be pressed, one with `onClick` and `enabled` false, gives its content the disabled colour instead, so its text and icons say that it cannot; a child that sets a colour of its own keeps it.

A card is as wide as its widest part, whether or not it has a footer. Given a width, usually with `fillMaxWidth()`, its media spans it and its footer reaches its end edge. Given a height, as the cards of a row are given the height of the tallest with `fillMaxHeight()`, its body fills it: the footer stands at the card's foot, and a child of the body given `Modifier.weight(1f)` takes the room between, with what follows it at the bottom.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the card's modifier.
- `variant: CardVariant`: how the card stands off what it sits on: its fill, its shadow and its edge.
- `onClick: (() -> Unit)?`: when given, the whole card becomes one button, and a click is reported as a `Card` event that carries the variant.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a card with `onClick` can be pressed. A card without one ignores it.
- `style: CardStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform. A card's corners and depth are not scaled by the density.
- `shape: Shape`: the card's corners: by default the resolved style's. Given here, it wins over `style`'s.
- `colors: CardColors?`: this card's own colours: the ones it sets, with the variant's for the rest.
- `contentPadding: PaddingValues`: the room around the header, the body and the footer. The media takes none.
- `header: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: drawn above the body: usually the card's title.
- `media: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: drawn edge to edge above the padded content, because a picture inset by the card's padding reads as a mistake.
- `footer: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: the card's actions in a row at the end edge, the main one last: closest to the thumb on a phone, and where the eye finishes on a wide card. In a card taller than what it holds, they stand at its foot.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the card. For a card with `onClick`, name what it opens.
- `tagKey: String?`: the card's automation key: the card is `Card_<tagKey>`.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the card's interactions, hoisted. The card keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit`: the card's body, in a column whose children stand `spacing.sm` apart. A child given a weight takes the room a card's height leaves.

Documented on: [Card](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/card.md)

### PantrixCardSkeleton

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.card.PantrixCardSkeleton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCardSkeleton(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: CardVariant = CardVariant.Elevated,
    style: CardStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(CardStyle, style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: CardColors? = null,
    skeletonColors: SkeletonColors? = null,
    contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(PantrixTheme.spacing.lg),
    showHeader: Boolean = true,
    lines: Int = 3,
    footerButtons: Int = 0,
    mediaHeight: Dp? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = PantrixTheme.strings.loading,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A `PantrixCard` whose content has not arrived: the card's own surface, with bars where its header, its body and its actions will be.

It is built from the card's own shape, fill, shadow, padding and spacing rather than drawn to look like one, so the frame the data arrives in is already there. Its bars take the room of what they stand for: the header's of a line of the theme's title, the body's of `lines` lines of text in the type a `PantrixText` has by itself, the theme's label, the footer's of medium buttons. A card with that content is as tall as its skeleton, and nothing below it moves when the data arrives. The skeleton cannot know what a card holds: match `showHeader`, `lines`, `footerButtons` and `mediaHeight` to the card it replaces.

It is announced once, for the whole card. A dozen bars that each said they were loading would make a loading list unusable with a screen reader. It fills the width it is given: a bar has no width of its own.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the skeleton's modifier.
- `variant: CardVariant`: the variant of the card it replaces: the same fill, shadow and edge.
- `style: CardStyle?`: this call's own `CardStyle`: over every enclosing one and under the density. The footer's bars keep the theme's button shape.
- `shape: Shape`: the card's corners: by default the resolved style's. Given here, it wins over `style`'s.
- `colors: CardColors?`: the colours of the card it replaces, where that card has its own: the same fill and edge.
- `skeletonColors: SkeletonColors?`: the bars' own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `contentPadding: PaddingValues`: the room around the bars, as around a card's content.
- `showHeader: Boolean`: whether a bar stands in for the header: a line of the theme's title.
- `lines: Int`: how many lines of text the bars stand in for, in the type a `PantrixText` has by itself.
- `footerButtons: Int`: how many buttons the footer's bars stand in for.
- `mediaHeight: Dp?`: the height of the media the card will show above its content, or null for a card without any.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the whole skeleton, or null inside something that already says it is loading.
- `tagKey: String?`: the skeleton's automation key: it is `CardSkeleton_<tagKey>`, and its bars have no tags of their own. Without one it has no tag.

### PantrixListDetailScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.listdetail.PantrixListDetailScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixListDetailScaffold(
    state: ListDetailState,
    list: @Composable ListDetailScope.() -> Unit,
    detail: @Composable ListDetailScope.(key: String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    emptyDetail: (@Composable ListDetailScope.() -> Unit)? = null,

```

A list and the detail of the item opened in it: side by side where the room has space for both, the detail in the list's place where it has not, and an extra pane beside the detail, or over it in a side sheet of the scaffold's.

- **How many panes.** The scaffold counts its own room, not the window's: one pane in a Compact or Medium room, two from Expanded on, three from Large on where an `extra` pane is given. A fold that divides the room upright, a foldable held like a book, makes two panes at any width, and the list and the detail meet at the fold.

- **One pane.** No item open shows the list; `ListDetailState.select` opens the detail in its place, sliding in from the end. Back, Escape and the edge swipe of iOS call `ListDetailState.back`: the detail slides away, following a back gesture's progress as the finger moves, and the list comes back. Of several scaffolds on one screen, back closes the detail opened last. A keyboard's focus goes with the pane shown: into the detail an item opened from the list, and back to that item. While the detail slides it is drawn on the theme's background, so that it covers the list under it.

- **Two panes.** The list is the style's `listWidth` wide at the start, the detail takes the rest past the gap, and back is the app's: the scaffold leaves it alone. With no item open the detail pane shows `emptyDetail`.

- **Resizable.** With `resizable` a handle stands in the gap: a drag, the arrow keys and a screen reader's adjusting make the list wider and narrower, between the style's `minListWidth` and where the detail would be narrower than `minDetailWidth`. A pointer over it is one that resizes (`PantrixPointerIcons.ResizeHorizontal`). The width is kept in `ListDetailState.listWidth`. A fold places the panes itself, and there is no handle then.

- **Extra pane.** `ListDetailState.showExtra` shows `extra` beside the detail where there is room for three panes. Elsewhere it slides in from the end over the detail, in a side sheet drawn in the scaffold's own room: under `extraTitle` and a close button, over a scrim that a press closes, as back and Escape do. A keyboard's focus moves into it and stays there until it closes. In both places it is given a bounded height and scrolls what it holds itself, and it is one composition: what it remembers is kept as the room changes from one to the other.

- **Each pane a window.** What a pane holds is told the pane as its window: `PantrixTheme.window`, its classes and `PantrixTheme.layout` answer for the pane's room, so that a list in a narrow pane lays itself out as on a phone. The posture stays the window's, and a fold is found where it crosses a pane.

- **Screen reader.** Each pane is read as one group. `listTitle`, `detailTitle` and `extraTitle` name the panes as they come into view, which TalkBack says on Android; Compose does not tell VoiceOver a pane's name.

- **Kept state.** The list and the detail stay where they are in the composition as the room changes between one pane and two: a list's scroll and a detail's text are kept. A pane that is not shown is not placed, so a keyboard and a screen reader skip it.

- **Reduced motion.** The detail appears and leaves at once.

- **Reading direction.** The list is at the start, on the right where the language is read from right to left, and the detail slides in from the left there.

- **Automation.** The scaffold is tagged `ListDetailScaffold_<tagKey>`, its panes `ListDetailList_<tagKey>`, `ListDetailDetail_<tagKey>` and `ListDetailExtra_<tagKey>`, the handle `ListDetailHandle_<tagKey>`, and the side sheet's scrim and close button `ListDetailScrim_<tagKey>` and `ListDetailClose_<tagKey>`.

The scaffold takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: `Modifier.fillMaxSize()` on a screen.

Parameters:

- `state: ListDetailState`: what is open: `rememberListDetailState` keeps it across a change of configuration.
- `list: @Composable ListDetailScope.() -> Unit`: the list. It opens an item with `ListDetailState.select`.
- `detail: @Composable ListDetailScope.(key: String) -> Unit`: the detail of the item whose key it is given. A new key composes it anew.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the room the panes have.
- `emptyDetail: (@Composable ListDetailScope.() -> Unit)?`: shown in the detail pane beside the list while no item is open: "Choose a message". Nothing is shown there without it.
- `extra: (@Composable ListDetailScope.(key: String) -> Unit)?`: a third pane for the open item, beside its detail: the contact's history, a file's properties. Shown once `ListDetailState.showExtra` is called.
- `listTitle: String?`: what the list is called, for a screen reader as it comes into view: "Inbox".
- `detailTitle: ((key: String) -> String)?`: what the detail of the item whose key it is given is called, for a screen reader as it comes into view: the message's subject.
- `extraTitle: String?`: what the extra pane is called: the title of the side sheet it is shown in over the detail, and for a screen reader as it comes into view.
- `resizable: Boolean`: whether a handle between the list and the detail makes the list wider and narrower.
- `style: ListDetailScaffoldStyle?`: the scaffold's widths, on top of the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the key of the scaffold's automation tags.

Documented on: [List and detail](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-list-detail.md)

### ListDetailScaffoldStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.listdetail.ListDetailScaffoldStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ListDetailScaffoldStyle(
    public val listWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val minListWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val minDetailWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val extraWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleTarget: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ListDetailScaffoldStyle>
```

`PantrixListDetailScaffold`'s geometry: how wide the list and the extra pane are beside the detail, how narrow a drag of the handle may make the list and the detail, and the handle itself.

The gap between the panes follows density, as the layout's gutter it is by default does; the widths and the handle do not. The panes' colours are not part of the style: each pane is drawn by the app, on what it puts in it.

Parameters:

- `listWidth: Dp`: How wide the list is beside the detail until its handle is dragged: 360dp, a phone's width.
- `minListWidth: Dp`: The narrowest a drag of the handle makes the list.
- `minDetailWidth: Dp`: The narrowest the detail is let be beside the list: a drag of the handle stops where the detail would be narrower, and so does a list width set on the state.
- `extraWidth: Dp`: How wide the extra pane is beside the detail, where there is room for three panes.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the panes. Unspecified in the presets: the layout's gutter, `PantrixTheme.layout.gutter`, which grows with the window. A brand whose panes meet edge to edge, with a line of their own between them, gives 0dp.
- `handleWidth: Dp`: The mark a resizable list's handle draws in the gap: a short upright bar.
- `handleHeight: Dp`: How tall the handle's upright bar is: `handleWidth` is how thick it is.
- `handleTarget: Dp`: How wide the strip is that a finger or a pointer catches the handle by, centred on the gap and over the panes' edges where the gap is narrower: each platform's smallest touch target under a finger, a narrow strip under a pointer.

Documented on: [List and detail](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-list-detail.md)

### ListDetailState

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.listdetail.ListDetailState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ListDetailState(initialSelectedKey: String? = null)
```

What a `PantrixListDetailScaffold` shows: which item of the list is open, whether its extra pane is shown, and how wide the list was dragged. An app reads it, changes it, and keeps it across a change of configuration and a process's death: `rememberListDetailState` saves it.

```kotlin
val inbox = rememberListDetailState()
PantrixListDetailScaffold(
    state = inbox,
    list = { Messages(onOpen = { id -> inbox.select(id) }) },
    detail = { id -> Message(id) }
)
```

An item is named by a key the app gives it: a string, the same in every language, that can be saved.

Parameters:

- `initialSelectedKey: String?`: the item open at first, or none.

Members:

- `selectedKey: String?`: The key of the item open in the detail pane, or null while none is.
- `isExtraVisible: Boolean`: Whether the extra pane is shown, the one beside the detail. A scaffold given no extra pane shows none whatever this says.
- `listWidth: Dp`: How wide the list was made by its handle, or `Dp.Unspecified` while it is as wide as the scaffold's style says. Kept with the rest of the state, and set by an app that remembers a reader's width itself.
- `fun select(key: String)`: Opens the item `key` in the detail pane: in one pane at a time, the detail takes the list's place.
- `fun back()`: Goes back to the list: closes the detail and the extra pane, and no item is open. What back, Escape and the edge swipe of iOS do while the scaffold shows one pane at a time.
- `fun showExtra()`: Shows the extra pane: beside the detail where there is room for three panes, in a side sheet elsewhere.
- `fun hideExtra()`: Hides the extra pane.

On the type:

- `ListDetailState.Saver: Saver<ListDetailState, *>`: What `rememberListDetailState` saves a state with.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.container.page

### PageAction

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.page.PageAction`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PageAction(
    public val key: String,
    public val label: String,
    public val icon: ImageVector? = null,
    public val primary: Boolean = false,
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
    public val destructive: Boolean = false,
    public val tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Something a page can do, shown at its top: export, filter, a new order.

A page lays its actions out by the room it has. In a wide one each is a button with its `label`, the `primary` one filled; in a narrow one each is its `icon`, with its label as what a screen reader and a tooltip say. What has no room, and in a narrow page what has no icon, is in a menu behind a "…" button, in the order the actions are given: the first one given is the last to fold away.

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What the page's `onAction` reports when the action is pressed. It is the same in every language, and the same action has the same key wherever it is shown.
- `label: String`: What the action is called: the button's text, and its name for a screen reader.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: What stands for the action where there is room for its icon alone, and before its label in the menu; null for an action that is only ever written, and in a narrow page is in the menu.
- `primary: Boolean`: Whether this is what the page is mostly for: a filled button in a wide page. One action of a page is primary at most.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the action can be pressed now. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled text's colour.
- `destructive: Boolean`: Whether the action deletes or undoes something that cannot be had back: drawn in the danger colour.
- `tagKey: String?`: The action's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: the action is `Action_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a page that has a key, as `PageScaffold_orders.Action_export`.

Documented on: [Page Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/page-scaffold.md)

### PageTitlePlacement

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.page.PageTitlePlacement`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class PageTitlePlacement
```

Where a `PantrixPageScaffold` writes its title, its subtitle and its actions.

Entries:

- `Bar`: In the page's top bar, whatever its width.
- `Adaptive`: In the top bar while the page is narrower than Expanded, and from Expanded on as a heading at the top of its content, in a large type, with no bar: the way a page of an app's admin reads on a desktop.

```kotlin
enum class PageWidth
```

How wide a `PantrixPageScaffold`'s content is.

Entries:

- `Full`: As wide as the page, the default: a page of cards, a table or a dashboard uses all the room there is.

What scrolls in a `PantrixPageScaffold`.

Entries:


What a `PantrixPageScaffold`'s content is given: a column to lay itself out in, and the room it is to keep.

Members:

With `PageScroll.None` it is the page's margins at the sides, its room above and below, and the room of a bar along the bottom, which a list scrolls its last rows clear of with its own `contentPadding`.

Documented on: [Page Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/page-scaffold.md)

### PantrixPageScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.page.PantrixPageScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixPageScaffold(
    title: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    subtitle: String? = null,
    onBack: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    actions: List<PageAction> = emptyList(),
    onAction: (key: String) -> Unit = {},
    trailing: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    header: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    stickyHeader: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    titlePlacement: PageTitlePlacement = PageTitlePlacement.Bar,
    largeTitle: Boolean = false,
    width: PageWidth = PageWidth.Full,
    scroll: PageScroll = PageScroll.Page,
    padding: PaddingValues = LocalPantrixScaffoldPadding.current,
    style: PageScaffoldStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable PageScaffoldScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A screen inside an app's shell: its title and what it can do at its top, and under them what it shows, kept clear of the shell's bars, of the keyboard and of the window's edges. An app lays its shell out once with a `PantrixScaffold`, its navigation along the bottom of a narrow window and down the side of a wide one, and each of its screens with this.

- **The bar.** The page draws its own `PantrixTopBar`, the scaffold none: as one page slides over another, the title goes with its page. The bar has the page's `title` and `subtitle`, a back button where `onBack` is given, and the `actions`. Its title starts where the content does, at the page's margin. Where the content is scrolled under it the bar draws a line along its bottom edge.

- **The title in a wide page.** With `PageTitlePlacement.Adaptive`, from Expanded on, the page has no bar: its title is a heading at the top of its content, in a large type, the subtitle under it and the actions after it as buttons with their labels, and it scrolls with the content. Narrower, it is in the bar. The page goes by its own width, not the window's, as a scaffold does: a page in a part of a window lays itself out for the room it has.

- **A large title.** With `largeTitle`, the bar's title stands under it in a large type, and goes up into the bar as the content scrolls, on every platform.

- **Header.** `header` stands under the title and over the content, and scrolls with them: a breadcrumb, a line of what the page is for, a notice. `stickyHeader` stands under the bar and stays there: tabs, a search, filters. The line of a scrolled page is then under the sticky header.

- **Actions.** `actions` are laid out by the room: in a wide page each a button with its label, the primary one filled; in a Compact one each its icon, its label in a tooltip and for a screen reader. What there is no room for, and in a Compact page what has no icon, is in a menu behind a "…" button, in the order given. `onAction` is told the key of the one pressed. `trailing` stands after them all the time: the app's own buttons, an account.

- **Scroll.** With `PageScroll.Page` the heading, the header and the content scroll together. With `PageScroll.None` the content fills the room under the bar and scrolls itself, a table or a map, and is given the room to keep as `contentPadding`; the bar's line and a large title follow its scroll. A list's page is a `PantrixLazyPageScaffold`.

- **Width.** With `PageWidth.Full`, the default, what the page shows takes the page's width, in a wide window too. With `PageWidth.Content` it is no wider than the theme's content width, `PantrixTheme.layout.maxContentWidth`, and stands at the start, under the title: a page that is read. A narrower form inside it takes the layout's columns.

- **Room.** The page keeps clear of what `padding` says, the enclosing `PantrixScaffold`'s by default: its bars and the window's insets, the bar's room at the top and a bar's along the bottom. At its sides it keeps the theme's page margin, which grows with the window's class, and above and below its content the style's room. What it holds is handed none of the scaffold's padding: a page inside it keeps clear of none of it again.

- **Keyboard and focus.** The page ends above the keyboard, and a field that takes the focus near the bottom is brought up into view over a bar along the bottom, not behind it. The page does not jump as the keyboard shows.

- **The window's title.** The page names the window after itself while it is shown: the browser's tab on the web, the title bar on the desktop (`PantrixWindowTitle`). An app writes its own name after it with `LocalPantrixWindowTitleFormat`. A page inside another page's content, as an example of one is, leaves the window's title to the page it stands in.

- **Screen reader.** The title is the page's heading, and the page's name as it comes into view, which TalkBack says on Android; Compose does not tell VoiceOver a pane's name.

- **Reported shown.** A page with a `tagKey` reports a `show` event to the theme's analytics each time it comes into the composition: an app counts its screens' views by it. On Android an activity built anew, as on a turn of the device, comes into the composition again. The title is never in the event.

- **Automation.** The page is tagged `PageScaffold_<tagKey>`, its bar `TopBar_<tagKey>`, an action `PageScaffold_<tagKey>.Action_<key>` and the "…" button `PageScaffold_<tagKey>.More_actions`, whose menu is `Menu_<tagKey>_actions`. What the app puts in the page, its header, its sticky header, its content and `trailing`, stands in `TestScope(tagKey)`: a button tagged `save` there is `orders.Button_save`, and an event it reports is on the screen `orders`. While one page gives way to another, and while a back gesture is held, the two pages stand together: a button both show, as one in every page's `trailing`, is tagged twice unless each page has a `tagKey` of its own.

- **Reading direction.** The page is laid out from the start: on the right where the language is read from right to left.

The page takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: a scaffold's content, or `Modifier.fillMaxSize()`.

Parameters:

- `title: String`: what the page is called: in its bar or its heading, its name for a screen reader, and the window's.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the page's modifier.
- `subtitle: String?`: a line under the title, a count or a state, or null for none.
- `onBack: (() -> Unit)?`: where the page goes back to, as its bar's back button; null where there is nowhere to go back to. The system's back, a gesture or a key, is the app's navigation's to hear.
- `actions: List<PageAction>`: what the page can do, the most used first: laid out by the room, the rest in a menu. Each has a key of its own among them.
- `onAction: (key: String) -> Unit`: told the key of the action pressed.
- `trailing: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands after the actions all the time, in a row: the app's own buttons.
- `header: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands under the title and over the content, and scrolls with them.
- `stickyHeader: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands under the bar and stays there as the page scrolls.
- `titlePlacement: PageTitlePlacement`: whether the title is in the bar at every width, or in the content of a wide page.
- `largeTitle: Boolean`: whether the bar's title stands in a large type under it, and goes up into it as the page scrolls.
- `width: PageWidth`: how wide what the page shows is: the page's, or the theme's content width.
- `scroll: PageScroll`: whether the page scrolls, or its content scrolls itself.
- `padding: PaddingValues`: what the page keeps clear of at its edges: the enclosing scaffold's padding by default.
- `style: PageScaffoldStyle?`: the page's geometry, over the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the page's automation key, the same in every language: what the page and its parts are tagged by, the TestScope of what it holds, and the page its `show` event is of.
- `content: @Composable PageScaffoldScope.() -> Unit`: what the page shows, in a column; with `PageScroll.None` it is given the room to keep as `PageScaffoldScope.contentPadding`.

Documented on: [Page Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/page-scaffold.md)

A `PantrixPageScaffold` whose content is a list: its rows are composed as they come into view, and its heading and its header are the list's first rows, which scroll with it. Everything else is the page's: the bar, the actions, the sticky header, the room it keeps, the keyboard, the window's title, the event and the tags.

Parameters:

- `title: String`: what the page is called: in its bar or its heading, its name for a screen reader, and the window's.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the page's modifier.
- `subtitle: String?`: a line under the title, a count or a state, or null for none.
- `onBack: (() -> Unit)?`: where the page goes back to, as its bar's back button; null where there is nowhere to go back to.
- `actions: List<PageAction>`: what the page can do, the most used first: laid out by the room, the rest in a menu.
- `onAction: (key: String) -> Unit`: told the key of the action pressed.
- `trailing: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands after the actions all the time, in a row: the app's own buttons.
- `header: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands under the title as the list's first row, and scrolls with it.
- `stickyHeader: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands under the bar and stays there as the list scrolls.
- `titlePlacement: PageTitlePlacement`: whether the title is in the bar at every width, or in the content of a wide page.
- `largeTitle: Boolean`: whether the bar's title stands in a large type under it, and goes up into it as the list scrolls.
- `width: PageWidth`: how wide the rows are: the page's, or the theme's content width, from the start. The list scrolls across the page's whole width either way.
- `state: LazyListState`: the list's scroll: kept with `rememberLazyListState`, and read for where the list is.
- `verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical`: how the rows stand along the list: one under another by default.
- `padding: PaddingValues`: what the page keeps clear of at its edges: the enclosing scaffold's padding by default.
- `style: PageScaffoldStyle?`: the page's geometry, over the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the page's automation key, as `PantrixPageScaffold`'s.

### PageScaffoldStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.page.PageScaffoldStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PageScaffoldStyle(
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sectionGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val actionGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val topBar: TopBarStyle? = null
) : PantrixStyle<PageScaffoldStyle>
```

`PantrixPageScaffold`'s geometry: the room around what a page holds and between its parts.

The room at a page's sides is the theme's page margin, `PantrixTheme.layout.margin`, which grows with the window's class, unless `horizontalPadding` sets one: the bar's title starts where the content does, at that room. The rooms follow the density. A page's colours are the theme's: its background, and the bar's surface.

Parameters:

- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the page's sides and what it holds, past the scaffold's padding: unspecified, the theme's page margin, unless it is set.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: The room above what the page holds and below it: 16dp on Android and iOS, 24dp on desktop and the web.
- `sectionGap: Dp`: The room between the page's heading, its header and its content: 16dp on Android and iOS, 24dp on desktop and the web.
- `actionGap: Dp`: The room between two of the page's actions, and between them and what stands beside them: 8dp.
- `topBar: TopBarStyle?`: The page's bar's own geometry, over the theme's. The bar's title starts at `horizontalPadding` unless this sets where.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.container.scaffold

### ScaffoldNavigationPlacement

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.scaffold.ScaffoldNavigationPlacement`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ScaffoldNavigationPlacement
```

Where a `PantrixScaffold` with adaptive navigation puts it.

Entries:

- `Bottom`: Along the bottom edge, below the content: a navigation bar. Where the scaffold is narrow, and on a foldable held like a laptop on a table.
- `Start`: Along the start edge, the scaffold's full height: a navigation rail or a sidebar. The right edge in a right-to-left layout.
- `VerticalBar`: Upright, at the bottom of the system's vertical bar: the column the iPhone Duo's outer screen keeps along its side for its status bar and an app's bars. A navigation bar drawn as `NavigationBarOrientation.Vertical`. Where the window has such a column, stands upright and has no fold across it, and the scaffold reaches the column, whatever the scaffold's width.


The padding the enclosing `PantrixScaffold` gives its content, as its `content` is handed it: what keeps a screen clear of the bars and the insets. A screen deep inside the scaffold, a `PantrixPageScaffold` among them, reads it here rather than being handed it down. Zero outside a scaffold.

### PantrixScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.scaffold.PantrixScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixScaffold(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    topBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)? = null,
    bottomBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)? = null,
    sideBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)? = null,
    snackbars: PantrixSnackbarState? = null,
    snackbarHost: @Composable () -> Unit = { if (snackbars != null) PantrixSnackbarHost(snackbars) },
    containerColor: Color = PantrixTheme.colors.background,
    contentColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    windowInsets: WindowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.union(WindowInsets.displayCutout),
    content: @Composable (padding: PaddingValues) -> Unit
)
```

The layout of a screen: a top bar, a bottom bar and a side bar around the content, and the app's snackbars over the content.

The side bar runs the scaffold's full height along the start edge, the right edge in a right-to-left layout, and the top bar and the bottom bar span the rest. The content fills that rest too, under the bars, so a list scrolls beneath them: pass `content`'s padding to the list as its content padding. The scaffold draws `containerColor` edge to edge, behind the window's system bars.

**Insets.** Each slot is given, as padding, the insets of the window edges it touches: the side bar its start, top and bottom insets; the top bar its top inset and the bottom bar its bottom inset, each with the end inset, and the start inset too when there is no side bar. A bar that pads its content by them draws its background behind the system bar and keeps its content in the safe area. A bar can apply the insets itself instead, with `Modifier.windowInsetsPadding`: the scaffold consumes the insets of the edges a slot does not touch, so the bar gets only its own. The `content`'s padding is each bar's height, or the inset of an edge without a bar, whichever is larger. Insets a parent has already consumed, with `consumeWindowInsets` or a `windowInsetsPadding`, are left out. The scaffold does not consume them for its content, as Material's does not: content that holds another scaffold, a snackbar host or anything else that pads by the window's insets consumes what it is given, with `Modifier.padding(padding).consumeWindowInsets(padding)`, or those insets are added again inside it.

**Snackbars.** Given `snackbars`, the scaffold shows them in a `PantrixSnackbarHost` over the content and inside the padding the content is given: between the bars, beside the side bar and clear of the window's insets. It also provides them to everything inside it as `LocalPantrixSnackbars`, so a screen shows a snackbar without the state being passed down to it. `snackbarHost` puts the app's own host in that place instead.

**Colour.** On the theme's own grounds, its background, which is the default, and its surface, the scaffold provides no content colour: there each component draws in its own default, text in `textPrimary` and a spinner in the brand's colour. On a role's fill it provides the colour paired with that fill.

**In the system's vertical bar.** Where the window has a column along its side for bars that stand upright, as the iPhone Duo's outer screen has from iOS 27.1 on, and the scaffold reaches it, a `PantrixTopBar` inside the scaffold hands its back button and its actions over: they stand in the column under the status bar, one above another, as UIKit puts a navigation bar's buttons there, and the top bar keeps its title. The content keeps clear of the column by its inset. Of two scaffolds one inside the other, the outer one holds the column. The scaffold holds it only in a window that stands upright with no fold across it, the outer screen as it is held: the inner screen and either screen on its side keep a column too, and there the scaffold leaves the status bar alone in it.

**Order.** A keyboard user moves, and a screen reader reads, from the side bar to the top bar, the buttons in the vertical bar, the content, the bottom bar and the snackbars. The bars and the snackbars are drawn over the content.

**Focus.** A list that scrolls beneath a bar brings what takes the focus to its own edge, and that edge is behind the bar. The list's content says what it keeps free at its ends with `Modifier.scrollPadding`, on a column's content or on each item of a lazy list, and what takes the focus is shown between the bars (docs/guide/scroll-padding/SCROLL_PADDING_GUIDE.md).

The scaffold fills a bounded space, usually the window: a scrolling parent has no height to give it.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the scaffold's modifier. The scaffold fills the space it is given.
- `topBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)?`: the bar above the content, given the insets of the edges it touches.
- `bottomBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)?`: the bar below the content, given the insets of the edges it touches.
- `sideBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)?`: the bar along the start edge, the scaffold's full height, given the insets of the edges it touches.
- `snackbars: PantrixSnackbarState?`: the app's snackbars: shown over the content, and provided to everything inside as `LocalPantrixSnackbars`. Without them, a scaffold shows no snackbars of its own and keeps the `LocalPantrixSnackbars` of the layout around it.
- `snackbarHost: @Composable () -> Unit`: what shows the snackbars over the content: by default a `PantrixSnackbarHost` of `snackbars`.
- `containerColor: Color`: drawn behind everything, the window's system bars included.
- `contentColor: Color`: the colour of text and icons that set none. By default the one paired with `containerColor` when that is a role's fill, and none on the theme's background, on its surface or on a colour the theme does not know: pass one with such a colour when the components' own defaults do not read on it.
- `windowInsets: WindowInsets`: the insets the scaffold hands to its slots and keeps the content and the snackbars clear of, by default the system bars and the display cutout; any a parent has already consumed are left out. The keyboard is not among them: a screen with text fields adds `Modifier.consumeWindowInsets(padding).imePadding()` to its content.
- `content: @Composable (padding: PaddingValues) -> Unit`: the screen, given the padding that keeps it clear of the bars and the insets.

Documented on: [Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/scaffold.md)

### PantrixScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.scaffold.PantrixScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixScaffold(
    navigation: @Composable (placement: ScaffoldNavigationPlacement, insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    topBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)? = null,
    snackbars: PantrixSnackbarState? = null,
    snackbarHost: @Composable () -> Unit = { if (snackbars != null) PantrixSnackbarHost(snackbars) },
    containerColor: Color = PantrixTheme.colors.background,
    contentColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    windowInsets: WindowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.union(WindowInsets.displayCutout),
    style: ScaffoldStyle? = null,
    content: @Composable (padding: PaddingValues) -> Unit
)
```

The layout of a screen whose navigation moves with its width: along the bottom edge while the scaffold is narrower than `ScaffoldStyle.sideNavigationMinWidth`, 600dp by default, and along the start edge from that width on.

`navigation` is told where it is, so it can draw the same destinations as a navigation bar at the bottom and as a rail or a sidebar at the start. At the start it runs the scaffold's full height and `topBar` spans the rest; at the bottom it spans the width below the content. The width is the scaffold's own, not the window's, so a scaffold in part of a window decides by the space it has. The navigation stays one composition as it moves, and so does the content: what they remember, a selection or a scroll position, is still there after the window is resized, and what they save comes back where a turned device builds the screen anew.

**On a table.** A foldable held half open with its fold lying across, like a laptop on a table, keeps the navigation along the bottom edge whatever the width: the lower half is where the hands are, and a column along the start edge would run across the fold. The posture is the window's, `PantrixTheme.window`. A scaffold short enough to fit in one half of that window is taken to be a pane there, and follows its width.

**In the system's vertical bar.** Where the window has a column along its side for bars that stand upright, as the iPhone Duo's outer screen has from iOS 27.1 on, stands upright with no fold across it, and the scaffold reaches the column, the navigation stands at the bottom of that column whatever the width: `navigation` is told `ScaffoldNavigationPlacement.VerticalBar` and draws an upright navigation bar there, as UIKit puts a tab bar. It is given no insets: the column's place for bars is clear of the status bar and the home indicator. A top bar's buttons stand at the column's top, as in the `PantrixScaffold` with separate bars.

Insets, snackbars, colour and order work as in the `PantrixScaffold` with separate bars: the navigation is given the insets of the edges it touches where it is, and is read and reached where it is, first at the start and after the content at the bottom and in the vertical bar.

Parameters:

- `navigation: @Composable (placement: ScaffoldNavigationPlacement, insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit`: the app's destinations, given where they are and the insets of the edges they touch there.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the scaffold's modifier. The scaffold fills the space it is given.
- `topBar: (@Composable (insets: PaddingValues) -> Unit)?`: the bar above the content, given the insets of the edges it touches.
- `snackbars: PantrixSnackbarState?`: the app's snackbars: shown over the content, and provided to everything inside as `LocalPantrixSnackbars`. Without them, a scaffold shows no snackbars of its own and keeps the `LocalPantrixSnackbars` of the layout around it.
- `snackbarHost: @Composable () -> Unit`: what shows the snackbars over the content: by default a `PantrixSnackbarHost` of `snackbars`.
- `containerColor: Color`: drawn behind everything, the window's system bars included.
- `contentColor: Color`: the colour of text and icons that set none. By default the one paired with `containerColor` when that is a role's fill, and none on the theme's background, on its surface or on a colour the theme does not know.
- `windowInsets: WindowInsets`: the insets the scaffold hands to its slots and keeps the content and the snackbars clear of, by default the system bars and the display cutout, without the keyboard; any a parent has already consumed are left out.
- `style: ScaffoldStyle?`: this call's own style, which says from what width the navigation moves to the start edge: over every enclosing one. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `content: @Composable (padding: PaddingValues) -> Unit`: the screen, given the padding that keeps it clear of the bars and the insets.

Documented on: [Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/scaffold.md)

### ScaffoldStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.scaffold.ScaffoldStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ScaffoldStyle(
    public val sideNavigationMinWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ScaffoldStyle>
```

`PantrixScaffold`'s one decision of its own: how wide it has to be before its adaptive navigation moves from the bottom edge to the start edge.

The scaffold measures its own width, not the window's, so a scaffold in one pane of a wider window decides by the space it has. The width does not follow the density. On a foldable held like a laptop on a table the navigation stays along the bottom edge at any width: that is the window's posture, not a style. A scaffold's colours are not part of its style: its container is `background` by default, and its insets come from the window.

Parameters:

- `sideNavigationMinWidth: Dp`: The narrowest a scaffold is when its adaptive navigation sits along the start edge; a narrower scaffold puts it along the bottom edge. 600dp on every platform, the width at which Material 3 moves navigation from a bar to a rail.

Documented on: [Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/scaffold.md)

### PantrixShowcaseScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.PantrixShowcaseScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixShowcaseScaffold(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    showcase: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    showcaseBackground: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    title: String? = null,
    topBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    header: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    footer: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    bottomBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    backdrop: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    showcaseSide: ShowcaseSide = ShowcaseSide.Start,
    showcaseFrom: WindowWidthClass = WindowWidthClass.Expanded,
    frame: ShowcaseFrame = ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive,
    formLayout: ShowcaseFormLayout = ShowcaseFormLayout.Centered,
    scrim: ShowcaseScrim = ShowcaseScrim.None,
    windowInsets: WindowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.union(WindowInsets.displayCutout),
    colors: ShowcaseScaffoldColors? = null,
    style: ShowcaseScaffoldStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A screen that stands outside the app's shell: sign in, sign up, a password reset, an invitation, a welcome, a page not found. A showcase stands on one side, a picture, a quote or slides, and the form on the other; in a narrow room only the form is left.

- **Showcase.** `showcase` stands beside the form once the scaffold is as wide as `showcaseFrom`, Expanded by default, on the side `showcaseSide` says. Narrower, it is not composed at all: its slides do not turn and its pictures are not loaded. The scaffold goes by its own width, not the window's. `showcaseBackground` fills the showcase to its edges, a picture or a gradient, under the system's bars, while what `showcase` holds keeps clear of them; `scrim` shades the background under what is written on it. The showcase is drawn in its own colours.

- **Form.** `content` is the form, no wider than the style's form width, in the middle of its side. `header` stands above it, a heading, and `footer` under it, a way to sign up instead. `formLayout` puts the header, the form and the footer together in the middle of the side's height, or apart: the header at the top and the footer at the foot.

- **Bars.** `topBar` is a row across the top of the form's side, a logo at its start and a language at its end; `bottomBar` is a row across its foot, a line of copyright. They stay where they are as the form scrolls between them. Where the showcase is not shown, a line parts each bar from the form; a bar with nothing in it takes no room. The bars and the form's parts are each told whether the showcase is shown, so that the logo the showcase carries in a wide window can stand in the top bar of a narrow one.

- **Frame.** With `ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive`, from the Large class on, the scaffold is a card in the middle of the window, no wider and no taller than its style says, on its `backdrop`; a card with no showcase is the form's width and as tall as what it holds. Narrower, and with `ShowcaseFrame.Edge` at every width, it reaches the window's edges.

- **Folds.** Where a fold upright divides the room, a device held like a book, the showcase is in one half and the form in the other, and they meet at the fold. A fold across the room, a device on a table, leaves only the form.

- **Room.** The scaffold keeps clear of the system's bars and the display's cut-out itself, as `windowInsets` says: it stands outside the app's shell, where nothing else does. Only the form's side scrolls; it ends above the keyboard, and a field that takes the focus is brought into view.

- **What it remembers.** The form and the showcase are each composed in one place whatever the layout: what they remember, a typed address or a slide's place, stays as the room changes, a phone turned on its side or a window widened into a card. A showcase a narrow room hides forgets, as it is not composed there.

- **The window's title.** With a `title`, the scaffold names the window after the screen while it is shown: the browser's tab on the web, the title bar on the desktop. The title is not drawn: the form has its own heading. A scaffold inside a page's content, as an example of one is, leaves the window's title to the page.

- **Screen reader and focus.** The form is read first, and takes the focus first, wherever the showcase stands; the showcase is read after it, as one group. The title is the screen's name as it comes into view, which TalkBack says on Android.

- **Reported shown.** A scaffold with a `tagKey` reports a `show` event to the theme's analytics each time it comes into the composition.

- **Automation.** The scaffold is tagged `ShowcaseScaffold_<tagKey>`, its sides `ShowcaseScaffold_<tagKey>.Pane_form` and `ShowcaseScaffold_<tagKey>.Pane_showcase`. What the app puts in it stands in `TestScope(tagKey)`: a button tagged `sign_in` there is `sign_in.Button_sign_in` on a scaffold keyed `sign_in`.

- **Reading direction.** The start and the end are the language's: `ShowcaseSide.Start` is on the right where the language is read from right to left.

The scaffold takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: the window, or `Modifier.fillMaxSize()`.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the scaffold's modifier.
- `showcase: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands beside the form in a wide room: a quote, a picture's caption, slides. Null for a screen with only its form.
- `showcaseBackground: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)?`: what fills the showcase to its edges, under what it holds: a picture or a gradient.
- `title: String?`: the screen's name: the window's title, and the screen's for a screen reader. Not drawn.
- `topBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)?`: the row across the top of the form's side: a logo, a language, a way back.
- `header: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands above the form: a heading.
- `footer: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands under the form: another way in, as signing up instead.
- `bottomBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)?`: the row across the foot of the form's side: a line of copyright, the terms.
- `backdrop: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)?`: what the card stands on in a wide window, with `ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive`: a picture or a gradient.
- `showcaseSide: ShowcaseSide`: which side the showcase stands on: the start or the end.
- `showcaseFrom: WindowWidthClass`: the narrowest class of width the showcase is shown in.
- `frame: ShowcaseFrame`: whether the scaffold is a card on its backdrop in a wide window, or reaches the window's edges.
- `formLayout: ShowcaseFormLayout`: whether the header, the form and the footer stand together or apart.
- `scrim: ShowcaseScrim`: what shades the showcase's background, so that what is written on it reads.
- `windowInsets: WindowInsets`: what the scaffold keeps clear of: the system's bars and the display's cut-out by default.
- `colors: ShowcaseScaffoldColors?`: what the scaffold is painted with, over the theme's.
- `style: ShowcaseScaffoldStyle?`: the scaffold's geometry, over the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the screen's automation key, the same in every language: what the scaffold and its sides are tagged by, the TestScope of what it holds, and the screen its `show` event is of.
- `content: @Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit`: the form, in a column.

Documented on: [Showcase Scaffold](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/showcase-scaffold.md)

### ShowcaseScaffoldStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseScaffoldStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ShowcaseScaffoldStyle(
    public val showcaseShare: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val formMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val formPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sectionGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val showcasePadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val showcaseInset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val showcaseShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val cardMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val cardMaxHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val cardMargin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val cardShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val cardElevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ShowcaseScaffoldStyle>
```

`PantrixShowcaseScaffold`'s geometry: how the room is shared between the showcase and the form, how wide the form is, the rooms inside each side, and the card it stands as in a wide window.

The rooms follow the density; the widths, the corners and the shadow do not. Its colours are not part of its style: they are `ShowcaseScaffoldColors`.

Parameters:

- `showcaseShare: Float`: How much of the room the showcase takes beside the form, more than nought and less than one: half on every platform. A fold that divides the room shares it instead.
- `formMaxWidth: Dp`: How wide the form, its header and its footer are at the most, in the middle of their side: 440dp.
- `formPadding: Dp`: The room between the edges of the form's side and what it holds: 24dp on Android and iOS, 40dp on desktop and the web.
- `sectionGap: Dp`: The room between the header, the form and the footer: 24dp on Android and iOS, 32dp on desktop and the web.
- `showcasePadding: Dp`: The room between the edges of the showcase and what it holds: 24dp on Android and iOS, 40dp on desktop and the web. The showcase's background runs to its edges.
- `showcaseInset: Dp`: The room around the showcase, inside its side, where it stands as a panel of its own: none on every platform, so that it reaches its side's edges.
- `showcaseShape: ShapeSpec`: The showcase's corners where it is inset: large on every platform. Not inset, it has the corners of what it stands in.
- `cardMaxWidth: Dp`: How wide the card the scaffold stands as in a wide window is at the most: 1120dp.
- `cardMaxHeight: Dp`: How tall that card is at the most: 760dp. A card with no showcase is as tall as its form.
- `cardMargin: Dp`: The room between that card and the window's edges, past the system's bars: 32dp.
- `cardShape: ShapeSpec`: That card's corners: large on every platform.
- `cardElevation: Dp`: The shadow under that card: 2dp on Android, none on iOS, 1dp on desktop and the web.
- `barPadding: Dp`: The room above and below what a bar of the form's side holds: 12dp on Android and iOS, 16dp on desktop and the web.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.container.supportingpane

### SupportingPanePresentation

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.supportingpane.SupportingPanePresentation`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SupportingPanePresentation
```

How a `PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold` shows its supporting pane where there is no room beside the main content.

Entries:

- `Sheet`: In a sheet the scaffold draws over the main content, under the supporting pane's title and a close button: from the bottom in a Compact room, where a drag of its handle pulls it closed, and from the end in a wider one.
- `Pane`: In the main content's place, sliding in from the end over it: back brings the main content back, and the supporting pane's own bar has a back button that calls `SupportingPaneState.hide`.

Documented on: [Supporting pane](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-supporting-pane.md)

### SupportingPanePlace

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.supportingpane.SupportingPanePlace`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SupportingPanePlace
```

Where a `PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold`'s supporting pane is, as the scaffold's room stands.

Entries:

- `Sheet`: Over the main content, in the scaffold's sheet under its title and close button: it draws no header itself.
- `InPlaceOfMain`: In the main content's place: its own bar has a back button that calls `SupportingPaneState.hide`.

Documented on: [Supporting pane](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-supporting-pane.md)

### PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.supportingpane.PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold(
    state: SupportingPaneState,
    main: @Composable SupportingPaneScope.() -> Unit,
    supporting: @Composable SupportingPaneScope.() -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    mainTitle: String? = null,
    supportingTitle: String? = null,
    presentation: SupportingPanePresentation = SupportingPanePresentation.Sheet,
    resizable: Boolean = false,
    style: SupportingPaneScaffoldStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A screen's main content and a pane that supports it: a document and its comments, a chart and its filters, a map and its results. Side by side where the room has space for both; over the main content, or in its place, where it has not.

- **Beside.** The scaffold counts its own room, not the window's: from Expanded on, and where the main content keeps the style's `minMainWidth`, the supporting pane is the style's `supportingWidth` wide at the end, the main content takes the rest past the gap, and back is the app's. The supporting pane stands there from the start; `SupportingPaneState.hide` puts it away, and the main content takes the whole room.

- **Narrow room.** Where there is no room beside, the supporting pane is closed until `SupportingPaneState.show`. With `SupportingPanePresentation.Sheet` it opens in a sheet drawn in the scaffold's own room, over a scrim that a press closes: from the bottom in a Compact room, where a drag of its handle pulls it closed, and from the end in a wider one, under `supportingTitle` and a close button. A keyboard's focus moves into it and stays there until it closes. With `SupportingPanePresentation.Pane` it slides in from the end in the main content's place, following a back gesture's progress as the finger moves. Back, Escape and the edge swipe of iOS close it in both.

- **The room changes.** A window made narrower does not open the supporting pane over the main content; a supporting pane open over it stays in view, beside, as the window is made wider.

- **Resizable.** With `resizable` a handle stands in the gap: a drag, the arrow keys and a screen reader's adjusting make the supporting pane wider and narrower, between the style's `minSupportingWidth` and where the main content would be narrower than `minMainWidth`. A pointer over it is one that resizes (`PantrixPointerIcons.ResizeHorizontal`). The width is kept in `SupportingPaneState.supportingWidth`.

- **Folds.** A foldable held like a book shows both at any width, meeting at the fold; one laid on a table shows the main content above the fold and the supporting pane below it. A fold places the panes itself, and there is no handle then.

- **Each pane a window.** What a pane holds is told the pane as its window: `PantrixTheme.window`, its classes and `PantrixTheme.layout` answer for the pane's room. The posture stays the window's.

- **Screen reader.** Each pane is read as one group. `mainTitle` and `supportingTitle` name the panes as they come into view, which TalkBack says on Android; Compose does not tell VoiceOver a pane's name. The scrim is not read: the sheet's close button closes it.

- **Kept state.** Both panes stay where they are in the composition as the room changes, and the supporting pane while it is hidden: what they remember is kept. A pane that is not shown is not placed, so a keyboard and a screen reader skip it.

- **Reduced motion.** The supporting pane appears and leaves at once.

- **Reading direction.** The supporting pane is at the end, on the left where the language is read from right to left, and slides in from the left there.

- **Automation.** The scaffold is tagged `SupportingPaneScaffold_<tagKey>`, its panes `SupportingPaneMain_<tagKey>` and `SupportingPaneSupporting_<tagKey>`, the handle `SupportingPaneHandle_<tagKey>`, and the sheet's scrim and close button `SupportingPaneScrim_<tagKey>` and `SupportingPaneClose_<tagKey>`.

The scaffold takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: `Modifier.fillMaxSize()` on a screen.

Parameters:

- `state: SupportingPaneState`: whether the supporting pane is shown, and its width: `rememberSupportingPaneState` keeps it across a change of configuration.
- `main: @Composable SupportingPaneScope.() -> Unit`: the screen's main content.
- `supporting: @Composable SupportingPaneScope.() -> Unit`: what supports it.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the room the panes have.
- `mainTitle: String?`: what the main content is called, for a screen reader as it comes into view: "Report".
- `supportingTitle: String?`: what the supporting pane is called: the title of the sheet it is shown in, and for a screen reader as it comes into view: "Comments".
- `presentation: SupportingPanePresentation`: how the supporting pane is shown where there is no room beside the main content.
- `resizable: Boolean`: whether a handle between the main content and the supporting pane makes the supporting pane wider and narrower.
- `style: SupportingPaneScaffoldStyle?`: the scaffold's widths, on top of the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the key of the scaffold's automation tags.

Documented on: [Supporting pane](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-supporting-pane.md)

### SupportingPaneScaffoldStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.supportingpane.SupportingPaneScaffoldStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SupportingPaneScaffoldStyle(
    public val supportingWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val minSupportingWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val minMainWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleTarget: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<SupportingPaneScaffoldStyle>
```

`PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold`'s geometry: how wide the supporting pane is beside the main content, how narrow a drag of the handle may make it and the main content, and the handle itself.

The gap between the panes follows density, as the layout's gutter it is by default does; the widths and the handle do not. The panes' colours are not part of the style: each pane is drawn by the app, on what it puts in it. Where the supporting pane is shown in a sheet, the sheet's own style draws it.

Parameters:

- `supportingWidth: Dp`: How wide the supporting pane is beside the main content until its handle is dragged, and the side sheet it is shown in where there is no room beside: 360dp, a phone's width.
- `minSupportingWidth: Dp`: The narrowest a drag of the handle makes the supporting pane.
- `minMainWidth: Dp`: The narrowest the main content is let be beside the supporting pane: a drag of the handle stops where it would be narrower, and a room too narrow for both at their narrowest shows the supporting pane over the main content.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the panes. Unspecified in the presets: the layout's gutter, `PantrixTheme.layout.gutter`, which grows with the window. A brand whose panes meet edge to edge, with a line of their own between them, gives 0dp.
- `handleWidth: Dp`: The mark a resizable supporting pane's handle draws in the gap: a short upright bar.
- `handleHeight: Dp`: How tall the handle's upright bar is: `handleWidth` is how thick it is.
- `handleTarget: Dp`: How wide the strip is that a finger or a pointer catches the handle by, centred on the gap and over the panes' edges where the gap is narrower: each platform's smallest touch target under a finger, a narrow strip under a pointer.

Documented on: [Supporting pane](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-supporting-pane.md)

### SupportingPaneState

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.supportingpane.SupportingPaneState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SupportingPaneState(initiallyShownBeside: Boolean = true)
```

What a `PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold` shows: whether its supporting pane stands beside the main content, whether it is open over the main content where there is no room beside it, and how wide it was dragged. An app reads it, changes it, and keeps it across a change of configuration and a process's death: `rememberSupportingPaneState` saves it.

```kotlin
val comments = rememberSupportingPaneState()
PantrixSupportingPaneScaffold(
    state = comments,
    main = { Document(onComments = { comments.show() }) },
    supporting = { Comments() }
)
```

The two are kept apart. Where the room has space for both, the supporting pane stands beside the main content from the start, until `hide` puts it away. Where it has not, the supporting pane is closed until `show` opens it. So a window made narrower does not open a sheet over the main content by itself, and a supporting pane open over the main content stays in view, beside it, as the window is made wider.

Parameters:

- `initiallyShownBeside: Boolean`: whether the supporting pane stands beside the main content at first, where there is room for both.

Members:

- `isShownBeside: Boolean`: Whether the supporting pane stands beside the main content where the room has space for both.
- `isOpenOver: Boolean`: Whether the supporting pane is open where there is no room beside the main content: in a sheet over it, or in its place, as the scaffold's presentation says. Closed at first.
- `supportingWidth: Dp`: How wide the supporting pane was made by its handle beside the main content, or `Dp.Unspecified` while it is as wide as the scaffold's style says. Kept with the rest of the state, and set by an app that remembers a reader's width itself.
- `isShown: Boolean`: Whether the supporting pane is in view as the scaffold's room stands: beside the main content, or over it. Before the scaffold has laid out its room, whether it is to be in view wherever the room puts it.
- `fun show()`: Shows the supporting pane: beside the main content where there is room, over it where there is not. Called before the scaffold has laid out its room, as at a screen's start, it shows the pane wherever the room puts it.
- `fun hide()`: Hides the supporting pane: beside the main content where there is room, and closes it over the main content where there is not. What back, Escape and the edge swipe of iOS do while it is open over the main content. Called before the scaffold has laid out its room, it hides the pane wherever the room puts it.

On the type:

- `SupportingPaneState.Saver: Saver<SupportingPaneState, *>`: What `rememberSupportingPaneState` saves a state with.

Documented on: [Supporting pane](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-supporting-pane.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.container.tab

### TabBadge

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabBadge`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TabBadge(
    public val contentDescription: String?,
    public val count: Int? = null,
    public val tone: BadgeTone = BadgeTone.Danger,
    public val colors: BadgeColors? = null
)
```

A badge on a tab of `PantrixTabs`: a count, or a dot where there is nothing to count.

The badge comes after the tab's label, and takes its room from the label where the tab is narrow: a long label is cut, and the badge is whole. It is a `PantrixBadge`, as large as that is and in its colours, on a tab of any state.

A screen reader hears `contentDescription` after the tab's label, as a part of the tab: "Inbox, 3 unread". A number alone would say nothing of what it counts, so the badge is silent without one, which is right only where the label says it already. It has no default for that reason: null is a decision.

Parameters:

- `contentDescription: String?`: What a screen reader says of the badge, after the tab's label, or null to say nothing.
- `count: Int?`: The number to show, or null for a dot. It is capped as a badge's is: `99+`.
- `tone: BadgeTone`: The colour role the badge is filled from.
- `colors: BadgeColors?`: The badge's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

Documented on: [Tabs](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tabs.md)
