### PantrixTabs

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTabs(
    tabs: List<TabItem>,
    selectedIndex: Int,
    onSelect: (index: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    scrollable: Boolean = false,
    style: TabsStyle? = null,
    colors: TabsColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A row of tabs that switches between views of the same content: one is selected, and a mark slides to the one selected next.

What marks the selected tab is the style's `TabsStyle.indicator`: a line under it, a line over it, a pill behind it, or its colour alone. The mark is where its tab is. It follows the tab when the row changes size, and slides only when the selection changes: at once under reduced motion.

The row is one stop for Tab, on the selected tab, as the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern has it. The arrow keys select the next or the previous tab, the other way round in a right-to-left layout, and Home and End the first and the last; a tab that is disabled is skipped. While a tab has the focus, the focus goes with the selection, whoever makes it: a key, a press, or the app, as when a pager is swiped to the next view. A press on a tab asks for it, and the focus goes to the row's one stop, the selected tab, where a press can take the focus. For a screen reader each tab is a tab that says whether it is selected, in one group.

A tab may carry a badge after its label, a count or a dot: `TabItem.badge`. A screen reader hears the badge's description after the label, as a part of the tab.

With `scrollable`, each tab is as wide as its label and the row scrolls sideways. It opens on the selected tab, and brings the one selected next to its middle, so that the tabs on both sides of it can be seen and pressed.

A tab is at least as tall as the platform's touch target, whatever the style's height and the density say. The row has no fill of its own: it sits on the page or on a surface, and its labels read on both. The tabs are only the row: the view that `selectedIndex` stands for is the app's, below it.

Parameters:

- `tabs: List<TabItem>`: the tabs, in order.
- `selectedIndex: Int`: the selected tab's index. Outside `tabs`, no tab is selected and no mark is drawn.
- `onSelect: (index: Int) -> Unit`: called with the index of the tab the user chose, by a press or by the keys, whether or not it is selected already. The row selects nothing by itself: a tab is selected when `selectedIndex` says so.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier. The row fills the width it is given.
- `scrollable: Boolean`: false shares the row's width between the tabs. True makes each as wide as its label, at least the style's `minTabWidth`, in a row that scrolls sideways and keeps the selected tab in its middle.
- `style: TabsStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TabsColors?`: this row's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled tab keeps the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the row's automation key: the row is `Tabs_<tagKey>`, and its tabs are named inside it, `Tabs_<tagKey>.Tab_<key>`, so that two rows with the same tabs are told apart. A selection is reported as a `Tabs` event that carries the tab's index and whether a press or a key chose it, and never its label.

Documented on: [Tabs](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tabs.md)

### TabIndicator

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabIndicator`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class TabIndicator
```

How `PantrixTabs` marks the selected tab.

Entries:

- `Underline`: A line along the selected tab's bottom edge, over the hairline under the row. The default on every platform.
- `Top`: The same line along the tab's top edge, for a row that sits below what it switches.
- `Pill`: A pill in the primary role's container behind the selected tab, inset by the style's `indicatorPadding`. A row of pills draws no hairline: it is a control of its own, not a heading over the content.
- `None`: No indicator: the selected tab is marked by its colour alone.

Documented on: [Tabs](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tabs.md)

### TabsStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabsStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TabsStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val indicatorHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val minTabWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val edgePadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val indicator: TabIndicator? = null,
    public val indicatorPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<TabsStyle>
```

`PantrixTabs`' geometry, and how it marks the selected tab.

Fixed tabs share the row's width. Scrollable tabs are as wide as their labels, at least `minTabWidth`, with `edgePadding` before the first and after the last. The air follows the density: `height`, `horizontalPadding`, `edgePadding`, `iconGap` and `indicatorPadding`. The indicator's thickness, the icon's size and the least a tab is wide do not. The tabs' colours are not part of the style: they come from the theme, and from `TabsColors` where a row has its own.

Android follows Material 3's primary tabs, with the icon before the label. iOS has no tab row of its own, since a segmented control does that job there, which `TabIndicator.Pill` draws; its values and the desktop's are Pantrix's own.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: The least a tab is tall: 48dp on Android, 44dp on iOS, 40dp on desktop and the web. A tab is never shorter than the platform's touch target, whatever this says.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: Inside a tab, before its icon or label and after its label.
- `indicatorHeight: Dp`: How thick a `TabIndicator.Underline` or a `TabIndicator.Top` line is.
- `minTabWidth: Dp`: The least a scrollable tab is wide.
- `edgePadding: Dp`: Before the first scrollable tab and after the last.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The size of a tab's icon.
- `iconGap: Dp`: Between a tab's icon and its label, and between its label and its badge.
- `indicator: TabIndicator?`: What marks the selected tab.
- `indicatorPadding: Dp`: Between a `TabIndicator.Pill` and the edges of the tab it marks.

Documented on: [Tabs](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tabs.md)

### TabsColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabsColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class TabsColors(
    public val selectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val unselectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val indicator: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val divider: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What `PantrixTabs` is painted with, for a row that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```kotlin
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = views,
    selectedIndex = view,
    onSelect = { view = it },
    colors = TabsColors(selectedContent = brand, indicator = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of tabs that can be selected. A disabled tab is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given here.

Parameters:

- `selectedContent: Color`: The label and the icon of the selected tab. The theme's `primary`, and on a pill the primary role's `onContainer`, the colour paired with the pill's fill. A pill given an `indicator` that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it; for one no role has, give this with it.
- `unselectedContent: Color`: The label and the icon of the other tabs. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `indicator: Color`: What marks the selected tab: the line under or over it, or the pill behind it. The theme's `primary`, and for a pill the primary role's `container`.
- `divider: Color`: The hairline under the row, which a row of pills does not draw. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. A row of tabs has no fill of its own: on a fill, where that line would not read, a share of what is written there.

```kotlin
interface TabletopScope
```

Documented on: [Tabletop](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-tabletop.md)

### PantrixTabletopLayout

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tabletop.PantrixTabletopLayout`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTabletopLayout(
    content: @Composable TabletopScope.() -> Unit,
    controls: @Composable TabletopScope.() -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    flatControls: TabletopControls = TabletopControls.Below,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Content that is looked at and the controls that are touched, laid out for how a foldable is held: on a table, half open with the fold lying across, the content fills the half above the fold and the controls the half below, where the hands are; held like a book, the two stand at each side of the fold; and on a screen that does not fold, the controls are below the content or over it, as `flatControls` says. A video and its player's buttons, a video call and its buttons, a camera's view and its shutter.

- **Its own room.** The layout looks for the fold where it crosses its own room, not the window: a layout that lies wholly on one side of the fold is laid out flat.

- **The fold's strip.** On a table and like a book, nothing is laid on the strip the fold keeps clear, and a strip in the middle of the room leaves both halves as large as each other.

- **Kept state.** The two parts stay where they are in the composition as the posture changes, at once and with no motion: a video goes on playing, and what the controls remember is kept.

- **Each part a window.** What a part holds is told the part's room as its window: `PantrixTheme.window`, its classes and `PantrixTheme.layout` answer for the part. The posture stays the window's.

- **Screen reader.** Each part is read as one group, the content first and the controls after it.

- **Reading direction.** Held like a book, the content is at the start of the fold: on the right where the language is read from right to left.

- **Automation.** The layout is tagged `TabletopLayout_<tagKey>`, its parts `TabletopContent_<tagKey>` and `TabletopControls_<tagKey>`.

The layout takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: `Modifier.fillMaxSize()` on a screen.

Parameters:

- `content: @Composable TabletopScope.() -> Unit`: what is looked at: a video, the people of a call, a camera's view.
- `controls: @Composable TabletopScope.() -> Unit`: what is touched: a player's buttons and its progress, a call's buttons, a shutter.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the room the two parts have.
- `flatControls: TabletopControls`: where the controls are while no fold divides the room.
- `tagKey: String?`: the key of the layout's automation tags.

Documented on: [Tabletop](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-tabletop.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar

### PantrixTopBarState

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBarState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PantrixTopBarState(collapsedFraction: Float = 0f)
```

How far a `PantrixTopBar` with a collapsing title has collapsed, and the scroll that collapses it.

A bar given a state is `TopBarStyle.expandedHeight` tall, with its title in a large type in a band under the navigation icon and the actions. As the content under it scrolls up the band closes, the title comes into the row, and the bar is `TopBarStyle.height` tall. The content hands the bar its scroll with `topBarScroll`: the bar collapses before the content moves, and opens again only once the content is back at its top, so the large title does not come back in the middle of a list. A finger that leaves the bar between its two heights is followed by the bar going on to the nearer, and a mouse wheel by the bar going on the way the wheel was last turned.

The state is the app's, as a scroll state is: keep it with `rememberPantrixTopBarState`, which survives a configuration change, and read `collapsedFraction` for anything else that follows the bar.

Parameters:

- `collapsedFraction: Float`: how far the bar is collapsed to begin with: 0, all open, unless it is told.

Members:

- `collapsedFraction: Float`: 0 while the bar is all open, 1 once it has collapsed. Set, it is kept between the two: set to 0, as a screen that has just gone back to its top does, it opens the bar.

On the type:

- `PantrixTopBarState.Saver: Saver<PantrixTopBarState, Float>`: Keeps how far the bar had collapsed across a configuration change.

Documented on: [Top Bar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/top-bar.md)

### PantrixTopBar

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTopBar(
    title: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    subtitle: String? = null,
    titleStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    subtitleStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    navigationIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    scrolled: Boolean = false,
    state: PantrixTopBarState? = null,
    style: TopBarStyle? = null,
    colors: TopBarColors? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

The bar at the top of a screen: the screen's title, with a navigation icon before it and actions after it.

Where the title stands follows the platform (`TopBarStyle.titleAlignment`): at the start on Android, the desktop and the web, in the middle of the bar on iOS. A title in the middle is in the middle of the bar, whatever is beside it, while it fits there; one too wide for that moves over, away from the wider side. Neither kind runs under the navigation icon or the actions: a title that is too long for the room between them is cut short, and so is the `subtitle` under it. The title is the screen's heading for a screen reader.

The bar is as wide as what holds it, and as tall as its style says under the `insets` it keeps clear. It is taller only where what it holds needs it, as a title in a larger type does: the title's lines keep a little clear of its top and its bottom.

```kotlin
val list = rememberLazyListState()
PantrixScaffold(
    topBar = { insets ->
        PantrixTopBar(
            title = stringResource(Res.string.conversation),
            navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = onBack, tagKey = "back") },
            scrolled = list.canScrollBackward,
            insets = insets,
            tagKey = "conversation"
        )
    }
) { padding -> Messages(list, padding) }
```

With a `state` the bar has a collapsing title. It starts `TopBarStyle.expandedHeight` tall, with the title in a large type, and the subtitle under it, in a band of their own under the navigation icon and the actions, at the bar's start on every platform. As the content under the bar scrolls up the band closes and the bar comes down to `TopBarStyle.height`, the title in the row coming in as the one in the band goes. The content hands the bar its scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll(state)`. A screen reader reads the title in the row, which is there all the time, and never meets the title twice.

A screen reader and the Tab key go through the bar in the order it reads: the navigation icon, the title and the subtitle under it, the actions.

**In the system's vertical bar.** Inside a `PantrixScaffold` that holds the column the iPhone Duo's outer screen keeps along its side, the bar hands its navigation icon and its actions over to it: they stand at the column's top, under the status bar, the navigation icon in a capsule of the bar's fill and the actions one above another in another, as UIKit puts a navigation bar's buttons there. The bar keeps its title, which then has the bar's width. Of two bars handing buttons over at once, as while one page slides over another, the column shows the one that came last.

Parameters:

- `title: String`: the screen's name, on one line.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the bar's modifier.
- `subtitle: String?`: a line under the title in a smaller type, a count or a state, or null for none.
- `titleStyle: TextStyle`: the type the title is set in, in the row: the theme's `title` unless given. A larger one makes the bar as tall as its line needs. Its colour is the bar's unless the style has one of its own. The large title of a collapsing bar is the theme's `headline`, whatever this is.
- `subtitleStyle: TextStyle`: the type the subtitle is set in, in the row and in a collapsing bar's band: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Its colour is the bar's unless the style has one of its own.
- `navigationIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the title: a `PantrixBackButton`, or a button that opens a drawer. Null for none, and the title then starts at the bar's own inset.
- `actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands after the title, in a row: icon buttons for what the screen can do, the most used first. A button draws in its own colours, the brand's unless it is given others: on a bar with a fill of its own, give each the colour that reads there.
- `scrolled: Boolean`: whether a line is drawn along the bar's bottom edge, to part it from what is scrolled under it: pass whether the content can scroll back, as `listState.canScrollBackward`. The line is inside the bar's height, and nothing moves as it comes and goes.
- `state: PantrixTopBarState?`: gives the bar a collapsing title: kept with `rememberPantrixTopBarState`, and handed the content's scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll`. Null is a bar of one height.
- `style: TopBarStyle?`: this bar's own geometry, which a `PantrixBackButton` in `navigationIcon` draws with too. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TopBarColors?`: this bar's own colours, or null for the theme's: its `surface`, with the title in `textPrimary` and the subtitle in `textSecondary`.
- `insets: PaddingValues`: the room the bar keeps clear at its edges, the status bar's and a cutout's, as a `PantrixScaffold` hands its top bar. The bar's fill runs behind them.
- `tagKey: String?`: the bar's automation key, the same in every language: the bar is tagged `TopBar_<tagKey>`, and the large title of a collapsing one `TopBar_<tagKey>.Title_large`.

Documented on: [Top Bar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/top-bar.md)

### PantrixBackButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixBackButton(
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A button that goes back to the screen before, for a `PantrixTopBar`'s navigation icon: an icon button a screen reader calls "Back" in the theme's language.

It draws the platform's own icon (`TopBarStyle.backIcon`): an arrow on Android, the desktop and the web, a chevron on iOS. Both turn round in a right-to-left layout. In a top bar's `navigationIcon` it takes the style that bar was given.

It is a `PantrixIconButton`, and on the theme's grounds it is drawn as one: in the brand's colour. On a fill, and in a bar that was given a colour for what it holds, it is drawn in that colour. It is tagged `IconButton_<tagKey>` and reports an `IconButton` `click`.

Parameters:

- `onClick: () -> Unit`: called at a press: go back to the screen before.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the button's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the button can be pressed.
- `tagKey: String?`: the button's automation key, the same in every language.

### TopBarStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TopBarStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val expandedHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val titleInset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val titleGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val titleAlignment: TopBarTitleAlignment? = null,
    public val backIcon: BackButtonIcon? = null
) : PantrixStyle<TopBarStyle>
```

`PantrixTopBar`'s geometry, and the icon `PantrixBackButton` draws.

`titleInset` keeps the title clear of an edge that has nothing beside it; next to a navigation icon or the actions the title is `titleGap` away from them. The bar is taller than `height` only where what it holds needs it. The heights and the room in the bar follow the density; where the title stands and which icon goes back do not. A top bar's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `TopBarColors` where a bar has its own.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: How tall the bar is, under the insets it keeps clear: 54dp on Android and iOS, 56dp on desktop and the web.
- `expandedHeight: Dp`: How tall a bar with a collapsing title is before it collapses: `height`, and under it the band that holds the title in a large type. 106dp on Android and iOS, 104dp on desktop and the web: a band of 52dp, and of 48dp on desktop and the web. A band is taller only where its lines need it, and a style that sets this no higher than `height` has no band: its bar is of one height, with a state or without.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the bar's edges and the navigation icon and the actions: 8dp.
- `titleInset: Dp`: How far the title stands from the bar's start edge where there is no navigation icon, and from its end edge where there are no actions: 16dp. The title is never nearer an edge than `horizontalPadding`.
- `titleGap: Dp`: The room between the navigation icon and the title, and between the title and the actions: 8dp.
- `titleAlignment: TopBarTitleAlignment?`: Where the title stands: in the middle on iOS, at the start elsewhere.
- `backIcon: BackButtonIcon?`: What a `PantrixBackButton` draws: a chevron on iOS, an arrow elsewhere.

Documented on: [Top Bar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/top-bar.md)

### TopBarColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class TopBarColors(
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val divider: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixTopBar` is painted with, for a bar that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
// A bar in the brand's own colour, written in what the theme pairs with it.
PantrixTopBar(title = title, colors = TopBarColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what the bar holds, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The bar's fill, which runs behind the insets the bar keeps clear. The theme's `surface`.
- `content: Color`: The title, the subtitle, and the icons of the navigation icon and the actions that give no colour of their own. On the theme's own fill the title is the theme's `textPrimary`, the subtitle its `textSecondary`, and an icon its own default.
- `divider: Color`: The line along the bar's bottom edge while content is scrolled under it. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

Documented on: [Top Bar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/top-bar.md)

### PantrixTwoPane

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.twopane.PantrixTwoPane`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTwoPane(
    first: @Composable () -> Unit,
    second: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: TwoPaneOrientation = TwoPaneOrientation.SideBySide,
    firstSize: PaneSize = PaneSize.Fraction(0.5f),
    gap: Dp = PantrixTheme.layout.gutter,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Two panes in one room: beside each other or one above the other, split at the window's fold where one divides the room.

- **Where they meet.** A fold that divides the room the way the panes stand, upright for panes beside each other and lying across for panes one above the other, is where they meet: each pane is on one side of it, and the strip the system asks to keep clear around it, the fold's `clearance`, is the gap. Elsewhere `firstSize` says how much the first pane takes and `gap` stands between them.

- **Which fold.** The fold is the window's where it crosses this room, so a pair of panes in part of a window splits at the fold only where the fold runs through it. A foldable held like a book splits panes beside each other; one on a table, panes one above the other.

- **Reading direction.** Beside each other, the first pane is at the start: on the right where the language is read from right to left. A fold stays where it is on the screen, and the first pane is on its start side.

- **Room.** The panes take the whole room across: beside each other, as tall as the room, or as tall as the taller of them where the room's height is not bounded. Along the split the room is to be bounded.

- **Both, always.** The two panes are always shown. A layout that shows one where there is no room for two asks the window first: `PantrixTheme.window.paneCount()`.

- **Automation.** The pair is tagged `TwoPane_<tagKey>`.

Parameters:

- `first: @Composable () -> Unit`: the first pane: at the start beside the second, or above it.
- `second: @Composable () -> Unit`: the second pane.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the room the two panes have.
- `orientation: TwoPaneOrientation`: which way the panes stand.
- `firstSize: PaneSize`: how much the first pane takes where no fold divides the room: half by default.
- `gap: Dp`: the room between the panes where no fold divides it: the layout's gutter by default.
- `tagKey: String?`: the key of the pair's automation tag.

Documented on: [Two panes](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/adaptive-two-pane.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.data.carousel

### PantrixCarousel

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.carousel.PantrixCarousel`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCarousel(
    pageCount: Int,
    currentPage: Int,
    onPageChange: (page: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    swipeEnabled: Boolean = true,
    loop: Boolean = false,
    autoAdvanceMillis: Int = 0,
    style: CarouselStyle? = null,
    colors: CarouselColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    page: @Composable (index: Int) -> Unit
)
```

Slides one beside another, one of them on screen: pictures, cards, the steps of an introduction. A swipe turns them; what is under them says where the carousel is, and turns them for a reader with no finger on the screen.

Which slide is on screen is the screen's state: the carousel shows `currentPage` and goes to another when that changes, turning there, or at once where the theme's motion is reduced. A swipe turns the slides by itself and tells `onPageChange` where it ended; a press on a button or a dot, and an arrow key, ask `onPageChange` for a slide and turn nothing by themselves. A caller that keeps a slide the reader swiped away from is asked once, and the carousel stays where the reader left it until `currentPage` changes. The carousel keeps no slide of its own beyond that: one that comes back to the screen is on `currentPage`.

Under the slides a dot stands for each of them; a style counts the slides instead, or shows nothing. With a pointer, a press on a dot asks for its slide. Under a finger a dot is too small a thing to touch, and the dots are one thing to press, as large as the platform's touch target: a press before their middle asks for the slide before, and one after it for the slide after. Where the reader has no touch, two buttons turn the slides back and on: a press while the carousel is turning goes on from the slide it is heading for, so two quick presses turn two slides. The slides take the keyboard's focus as one stop: the arrow keys turn them, mirrored where the reading runs from the right, and Home and End go to the first and the last. A button at the end it turns to cannot be pressed, and the focus it had goes to the slides; so does the focus of what is in a slide that an arrow turns away. Of what is in the slides, Tab stops at what is in the one on screen alone.

With `loop` the slides go round: the last goes on to the first and the first back to the last, by a swipe, a button or an arrow, and neither button is ever at an end.

With `autoAdvanceMillis` the carousel turns by itself: so long after it came to a slide, it asks `onPageChange` for the slide after, and for the first after the last. It waits while the reader holds a slide, while a pointer is over the carousel and while the keyboard's focus is in it. Beside the dots it has a button that stops it and lets it turn again, and that button is the reader's last word: stopped, the carousel turns only when it is turned, and let to turn again it does so with the focus on that button. Where the theme's motion is reduced the carousel does not turn by itself at all, and has no such button.

A screen reader is told the carousel's name, where it is given one, and where the carousel is whenever that changes, as "Slide 2 of 5" in the theme's language; a carousel that is turning by itself does not break in at every turn, and where it is can be read when the reader asks. On iOS the carousel is a group without a name: a screen reader there reads a group's own name after what the group holds.

The slides are as tall as the carousel is told to be, less what is under them, and a slide lower than that stands at their top. Told nothing, as on a page that scrolls, the carousel is as tall as the slide on screen, and on the way from a slide to a taller or a lower one as tall as the way between the two is far gone. A slide is as wide as the carousel, less the style's `peek` at each side. A style puts the dots and the buttons over the slides instead, as on a gallery of pictures, where they take no room of their own.

Parameters:

- `pageCount: Int`: how many slides there are.
- `currentPage: Int`: the slide on screen, counted from zero, as a pager's is. One past either end is the nearest slide. A `PantrixPagination` counts its pages from one, as it writes them: its page is this and one.
- `onPageChange: (page: Int) -> Unit`: told the slide a swipe ended on, and the slide a button, a dot or a key asks for, or the carousel itself when it turns by itself.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the carousel: the slides and what is under them.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what the carousel holds, for a screen reader: "Featured products".
- `swipeEnabled: Boolean`: whether a swipe turns the slides. An introduction that goes on by its own button turns it off.
- `loop: Boolean`: whether the slides go round, the last on to the first. A carousel of one slide has nowhere to go.
- `autoAdvanceMillis: Int`: how long the carousel stays on a slide before it turns to the next by itself, or 0, the default, for a carousel that is turned by its reader alone. Long enough to read a slide in: five seconds or more.
- `style: CarouselStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: CarouselColors?`: this call's own colours for what is under the slides. Only the ones it sets change.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the carousel's tag is `Carousel_<tagKey>`, and its parts are named inside it: `Carousel_<tagKey>.Slides_view`, which takes the keyboard's focus, `.Page_<index>`, `.Control_previous`, `.Control_next`, `.Control_pause` and `.Indicator_position`. Where the slides go round and a slide's neighbours show, a carousel of two slides has the same slide at both sides, twice under one tag.
- `page: @Composable (index: Int) -> Unit`: a slide, by its index.

What a `PantrixCarousel` is painted with under its slides, for a carousel that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's. The slides are the caller's own.

A carousel has no fill of its own and stands on what is behind it. On a fill, which says what is written on it, the current dot and the buttons are written in that, and the other dots in a share of it: the brand's colour and the theme's border are colours for the theme's own grounds. So is the theme's disabled colour: a button at the end it would turn past is drawn in that on the theme's grounds, and in a share of the buttons' colour on a fill and where the buttons are given a colour.

Over the slides, where a style puts them, the dots and the buttons do have a fill of their own, `overlay`, and are written in what reads on it, as on any other fill.

- `indicator: Color`: The dot of the current slide. The primary role's `color`.
- `indicatorTrack: Color`: The dots of the other slides. The theme's `borderStrong`, which is told from a ground as a control's own mark is.
- `control: Color`: The buttons. The theme's `onSurface`, an icon's colour.
- `overlay: Color`: The fill behind the dots and behind each button where they stand over the slides. The theme's `onSurface`, the tone opposite the theme's grounds, thinned so that the slide shows through it. One of the theme's role colours given here brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is written on it.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock

### PantrixCodeBlock

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.PantrixCodeBlock`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCodeBlock(
    code: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    tokens: List<CodeToken> = emptyList(),
    title: String? = null,
    language: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    lineNumbers: Boolean = false,
    firstLineNumber: Int = 1,
    softWrap: Boolean = false,
    selectable: Boolean = true,
    copyable: Boolean = true,
    onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null,
    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    style: CodeBlockStyle? = null,
    colors: CodeBlockColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    leading: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null
)
```

Code set out to be read: in the theme's code type, a line to a line, each run of it in the colour of what it is, and ready to be copied.

The block does not know the language it shows. What colours the code are the `tokens` its caller gives: the runs of the text and what each is, as whatever read the code found them. Code given none is written in one colour.

A header stands over the code while there is something to say in it: a `title`, which is a file's name most often, the `language`, an `icon`, what the screen puts in `trailing`. The button that copies stands at its end; a block that has nothing else to put there has no header, and the button stands in a strip of its own over the code. That button copies all of the code, whatever part of it is on the screen, and shows a tick for a moment after. What is on the screen can be selected too, and copied a part at a time.

A line too long for the block is not broken: the code scrolls sideways, under line numbers that stay where they are. A line of code broken where the room ends loses what its indent says. With `softWrap` a line goes on under itself all the same, for a narrow screen where the words matter more than the columns.

The block fills the width it is given. Given a height, it scrolls inside it under a header that stays, and only the lines on the screen are built. With no height, in a page that scrolls, it is as tall as its lines where it has no more than three hundred; longer code is no taller there than the window, and scrolls in it. Where it scrolls, a bar at its edge shows how far, and a mouse can drag it.

Where a pointer leads and there is something to scroll, the lines are a stop for Tab: with the focus on them the arrow keys scroll by a line and, sideways, by a step; Page Up and Page Down by a screen of lines; Home and End go to the first line and to the last. A screen reader reads the code a line at a time, and passes the line numbers.

Code is written from left to right in every language, and so are its lines here. The header is laid out as the app is.

```kotlin
PantrixCodeBlock(code = snippet, language = "Kotlin", tagKey = "usage")
```

Parameters:

- `code: String`: the code. Its lines end at a line feed, at a carriage return, or at the two together, and the break that ends the text starts no line.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the block's modifier. A height given here is the room the code scrolls in.
- `tokens: List<CodeToken>`: the runs of `code` that have a colour, placed by the letters of the whole text. None by default.
- `title: String?`: what the header says first: a file's name, or what the code is. A title too long for the header is cut short.
- `language: String?`: the language's name, written after the title in the header, as it is to be read: `Kotlin`, `TS`. The block keeps no list of languages.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: an icon before the title.
- `lineNumbers: Boolean`: whether each line carries its number before the code.
- `firstLineNumber: Int`: the number of the first line. A part taken out of a file starts where it started there.
- `softWrap: Boolean`: whether a line too long for the block goes on under itself. By default no line does, and the code scrolls sideways.
- `selectable: Boolean`: whether the code can be selected, by a pointer drawn over it or a finger held on it, and copied by the system's own means. What is copied so is what the lines on the screen show, without their numbers and without what is said about them. Code that scrolls in its own height has built the lines on its screen and no others, and "select all" there selects those. The button copies all of it.
- `copyable: Boolean`: whether the block has the button that copies the code.
- `onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)?`: called after that button was pressed, with whether the code got to the clipboard: a screen that says so in its own way listens here. The button itself shows a tick for a moment and tells a screen reader, unless the system shows every copy itself (`PantrixClipboard.traits`): there nothing more is needed.
- `trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the screen puts at the header's end, before the button that copies: a count, a button of its own. It is drawn in the block's text colour.
- `style: CodeBlockStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: CodeBlockColors?`: this block's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the block's automation key: the block is `CodeBlock_<tagKey>`, a line of it `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Line_<number>`, the message under a line `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Note_<number>`, the lines' window where a keyboard scrolls it `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Lines_window`, and the button that copies `CodeBlock_<tagKey>.Button_copy`. A press on that button is reported as a `CodeBlock` `copy` event with whether the code got there. Nothing of the code is reported.
- `leading: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what the screen puts at the header's start, before the icon and the title, written in the header's colour: the tabs of one file in two forms, as a page of documentation shows a setup for two repositories.
- `textStyle: TextStyle?`: what the code is set in: the theme's `code` where it is not given, a smaller one on a phone's page.

Documented on: [Code Block](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/code-block.md)

### PantrixCodeBlock

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.PantrixCodeBlock`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCodeBlock(
    lines: List<CodeLine>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    title: String? = null,
    language: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    lineNumbers: Boolean = false,
    firstLineNumber: Int = 1,
    softWrap: Boolean = false,
    selectable: Boolean = true,
    copyable: Boolean = true,
    onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null,
    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    style: CodeBlockStyle? = null,
    colors: CodeBlockColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    leading: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null
)
```

`PantrixCodeBlock` given its lines one by one, each with what is said about it: a band behind a line that is to be looked at, the lines that were added and taken out, a finding with its message under the line it is about.

`codeLines` makes the lines of a text, to be marked from there.

```kotlin
val lines = remember(source, finding) {
    codeLines(source).mapIndexed { index, line ->
        if (index == finding.line) line.copy(mark = CodeMark(CodeTone.Danger, message = finding.message)) else line
    }
}
PantrixCodeBlock(lines = lines, title = "AuthRepository.kt", lineNumbers = true, tagKey = "review")
```

A line with a mark is drawn on the soft fill of its tone's role, and written in the one colour the theme pairs with that fill; a bar in the role's colour runs down its left edge. A mark's message stands under its line, after the tone's icon, in the app's own reading direction, and does not scroll sideways with the code.

Parameters:

- `lines: List<CodeLine>`: the lines, in their order. The button copies their texts, a line to a line.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the block's modifier. A height given here is the room the code scrolls in.
- `title: String?`: what the header says first: a file's name, or what the code is.
- `language: String?`: the language's name, written after the title in the header, as it is to be read.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: an icon before the title.
- `lineNumbers: Boolean`: whether each line carries its number before the code.
- `firstLineNumber: Int`: the number of the first line. A part taken out of a file starts where it started there.
- `softWrap: Boolean`: whether a line too long for the block goes on under itself.
- `selectable: Boolean`: whether the code can be selected and copied by the system's own means.
- `copyable: Boolean`: whether the block has the button that copies the code.
- `onCopy: ((copied: Boolean) -> Unit)?`: called after that button was pressed, with whether the code got to the clipboard.
- `trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the screen puts at the header's end, before the button that copies.
- `style: CodeBlockStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: CodeBlockColors?`: this block's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the block's automation key, as the other overload has it.
- `leading: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what the screen puts at the header's start, before the icon and the title: the tabs of a file in two forms, written in the header's colour.
- `textStyle: TextStyle?`: what the code is set in: the theme's `code` where it is not given.

### CodeBlockStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.CodeBlockStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class CodeBlockStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val linePadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val headerHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gutterGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val borderWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val headerLineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val headerHorizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<CodeBlockStyle>
```

`PantrixCodeBlock`'s geometry: the room around its lines, its header, the room before the code where the lines are numbered, and the edge.

The lines stand close, as lines of code do: nothing in them is pressed, and they need no room for a finger. A line of the theme's code type is 20dp tall; Android leaves 2dp over and under its words, iOS 1dp, and the desktop and the web none.

The corners are the card's on each platform: medium on Android, large on iOS, small on desktop and the web.

The paddings, the header's height and the gap follow the density, since they are the room around the words. The icons' size, the widths of the edge and of a mark's bar, and the shape do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The corners of the block: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the block's sides and what it holds: the header's words, the lines, a message under a line. A mark's band is drawn across it, to the sides.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: The room over the first line and under the last, and under a message. A message has half of it over its words.
- `linePadding: Dp`: The room over and under the words of each line.
- `headerHeight: Dp`: The least the header is tall. It grows with what stands in it. A block that has nothing in its header but the button that copies has no header: the button's strip is as tall as the button.
- `gutterGap: Dp`: Between the line numbers and the code, where the lines are numbered.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The width and height of the header's icon, of the icon of the button that copies, and of the one before a message.
- `borderWidth: Dp`: The width of the edge around the block, and of the line under its header where `headerLineWidth` is not set. Zero draws none.
- `barWidth: Dp`: The width of the bar down the left edge of a line with a mark. Zero draws none.
- `headerLineWidth: Dp`: The width of the line under the header: `borderWidth` where it is not set, so that a block without an edge can still have its header ruled off. Zero draws none.
- `headerHorizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the block's sides and what its header holds: `horizontalPadding` where it is not set. Tabs at the header's start stand nearer the side than the lines do.

### CodeBlockColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.CodeBlockColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class CodeBlockColors(
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val text: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val comment: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val keyword: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val type: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val string: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val number: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val punctuation: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val annotation: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val lineNumber: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val border: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixCodeBlock` is painted with, for a block that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
// No fill and no edge of its own, in a card that has both:
PantrixCodeBlock(
    code = snippet,
    colors = CodeBlockColors(container = Color.Transparent, border = Color.Transparent)
)
```

On the theme's own grounds each kind of token has a colour of its own, from the theme's roles. On another fill those colours are not known to read. A `container` that is one of the theme's role colours, and a transparent one on a fill that gives what stands on it a colour, write all the code in the one colour that reads there; a fill the theme does not have writes it in the theme's text colour. Each colour given here is used wherever the block stands.

A line with a mark is drawn on the soft fill of its tone's role, and all of it is written in the one colour the theme pairs with that fill, as a toned row of a table is: the colours of the kinds are for the theme's grounds, and are not known to read on a role's fill. A comment is still slanted there.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The fill behind the header and the lines: the theme's `surface`. `Color.Transparent` leaves what is behind the block to show.
- `text: Color`: What no token colours, and the header's title. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `comment: Color`: A comment, which is slanted too. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `keyword: Color`: A word of the language. The theme's primary role.
- `type: Color`: The name of a type. The theme's info role.
- `string: Color`: A string. The theme's success role.
- `number: Color`: A number. The theme's warning role.
- `punctuation: Color`: Brackets, commas and semicolons. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `annotation: Color`: A name that says something about what follows it. The theme's danger role.
- `lineNumber: Color`: The line numbers, the header's language and its icon, the icon of the button that copies, and the scroll bars. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `border: Color`: The edge around the block and the line under its header. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds, and on a fill, where that line would not read, a share of what is written there.

### CodeTokenKind

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.CodeTokenKind`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class CodeTokenKind
```

What a run of code is, which is what it is coloured by.

There are as many kinds as the theme has colours to tell them apart with: a kind that could only be drawn as its neighbour is would say that two different things are one. A reader of a language that knows more folds the rest in: an operator is `Punctuation`, a property is `Plain`, an escape inside a string is a part of the `StringLiteral`.

Entries:

- `Plain`: What no other kind claims: names, the room between words. A token of it takes a colour off what is under it.
- `Comment`: A comment. It is slanted as well as coloured.
- `Keyword`: A word of the language: `fun`, `val`, `return`.
- `Type`: The name of a type.
- `StringLiteral`: A string or a character, with its quotes.
- `Number`: A number.
- `Punctuation`: Brackets, commas, semicolons: what holds the code together and says nothing itself.
- `Annotation`: A name that says something about what follows it: `@Composable`, `@Override`, a decorator, an attribute.

Documented on: [Code Block](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/code-block.md)

### CodeToken

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.CodeToken`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class CodeToken(
    public val start: Int,
    public val end: Int,
    public val kind: CodeTokenKind
)
```

One coloured run of a text of code: the letters from `start` up to `end`, and what they are.

Its place counts the letters of the text it is given with: of the whole text for `codeLines`, which then cuts a run that goes over several lines into one for each, and of the line itself for a `CodeLine`. Where two runs lie over the same letters the later one colours them. What reaches past the text's end is cut there, and a run that holds nothing colours nothing.

Parameters:

- `start: Int`: The place of the run's first letter, counted from nought.
- `end: Int`: The place after its last letter.
- `kind: CodeTokenKind`: What the run is.

Documented on: [Code Block](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/code-block.md)

### CodeTone

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.CodeTone`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class CodeTone
```

What a mark on a line of code means: the role of the theme its band and its bar are drawn in.

A tint says nothing to someone who cannot see it. What a mark means stands in its message, as words.

Entries:

- `Primary`: The brand's colour: the line someone was sent to, the one a step of a guide is about.
- `Info`: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.
- `Success`: Something that is well: a line that was added, a check that passed.
- `Warning`: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.
- `Danger`: Something that is wrong: a finding, a failure, a line that was taken out.
- `Neutral`: Set apart without a judgement in it.

Documented on: [Code Block](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/code-block.md)

### CodeMark

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.CodeMark`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class CodeMark(
    public val tone: CodeTone,
    public val message: String? = null,
    public val source: String? = null
)
```

What is said about a line of code: a band behind the line in the soft fill of the `tone`'s role, a bar down its left edge in the role's colour and, with a `message`, the message under the line.

```kotlin
// The line someone was sent to:
CodeMark(CodeTone.Primary)
// A finding, with what reported it:
CodeMark(CodeTone.Danger, message = "This may be null here.", source = "kotlin:S2259")
```

Parameters:

- `tone: CodeTone`: What the mark means.
- `message: String?`: What is written under the line, in the app's own words and in its reading direction. A screen reader comes to it after the line. Nothing by default: the band alone.
- `source: String?`: What said so, at the message's end: a rule's name, a check's. It is written only with a message.

```kotlin
data class CodeLine(
```

One line of a `PantrixCodeBlock`: what it says, how it is coloured, and what is said about it.

What is said about a line is carried by the line and not kept beside the lines under its number: a number can name a line the block does not have.

Parameters:

### codeLines

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.codeblock.codeLines`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
fun codeLines(
    code: String,
    tokens: List<CodeToken> = emptyList()
): List<CodeLine>
```

The lines of `code`, each with the runs of `tokens` that lie on it: what the `PantrixCodeBlock` that takes a text is given, and where a screen starts that marks some of the lines itself.

```kotlin
val lines = remember(source) {
    codeLines(source, kotlinTokens(source)).mapIndexed { index, line ->
        if (index == failed) line.copy(mark = CodeMark(CodeTone.Danger, message = why)) else line
    }
}
PantrixCodeBlock(lines = lines, lineNumbers = true)
```

A line ends at a line feed, at a carriage return, or at the two together. The break that ends the text ends its last line and starts no other: a file that ends as files do has no empty line after it. A text of nothing is one empty line.

Returns the lines in the text's order, without what ends them.

Parameters:

- `code: String`: the text.
- `tokens: List<CodeToken>`: the runs of `code` that have a colour, placed by the letters of the whole text. A run that goes over a line's end, as a comment of several lines does, is cut into one for each line.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.data.datatable

### PantrixDataTable

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.datatable.PantrixDataTable`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixDataTable(
    rows: List<T>,
    columns: List<DataTableColumn<T>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    rowKey: ((row: T) -> String)? = null,
    rowLabel: ((row: T) -> String)? = null,
    rowEnabled: ((row: T) -> Boolean)? = null,
    rowTone: ((row: T) -> DataTableTone?)? = null,
    sort: List<DataTableSort> = emptyList(),
    onSortChange: ((List<DataTableSort>) -> Unit)? = null,
    multiSort: Boolean = false,
    selected: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    onSelectionChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null,
    selection: DataTableSelection = DataTableSelection.Multiple,
    expanded: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null,
    expansion: DataTableExpansion = DataTableExpansion.Multiple,
    rowDetail: (@Composable (row: T) -> Unit)? = null,
    onRowClick: ((row: T) -> Unit)? = null,
    loading: Boolean = false,
    loadingRows: Int = 5,
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    toolbar: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    listContent: (@Composable (row: T) -> Unit)? = null,
    variant: DataTableVariant = DataTableVariant.Plain,
    striped: Boolean = false,
    layout: DataTableLayout = DataTableLayout.Auto,
    headerTextStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold),
    state: DataTableState = rememberDataTableState(),
    style: DataTableStyle? = null,
    colors: DataTableColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Rows of records in columns: a header that orders them, boxes that choose them, rows that open, columns that stay in place while the others scroll, and a list of records where there is no room for a table.

```kotlin
var sort by remember { mutableStateOf(listOf(DataTableSort("total", descending = true))) }
var chosen by remember { mutableStateOf(emptySet<String>()) }
val columns = remember {
    listOf(
        DataTableColumn.text<Order>(key = "customer", header = customer, sortable = true) { it.customer },
        DataTableColumn.text(key = "total", header = total, alignment = Alignment.End, sortable = true) { it.total }
    )
}
PantrixDataTable(
    rows = remember(orders, sort) { orders.sortedWith(sort.comparator(columns)) },
    columns = columns,
    rowKey = { it.id },
    sort = sort,
    onSortChange = { sort = it },
    selected = chosen,
    onSelectionChange = { chosen = it },
    tagKey = "orders"
)
```

**The rows are the caller's.** The table shows `rows` in the order they are given and changes nothing by itself: a press on a header asks for an order with `onSortChange`, a box for a choice with `onSelectionChange`, a chevron for a row to be opened with `onExpandedChange`. That is what lets one table show rows a screen holds and orders itself, with comparator, and rows a server orders and sends a page at a time. The rows given are the page: the box in the header chooses those, and keeps what was chosen on other pages.

**Columns.** A `DataTableColumn` says how wide it is, or shares what is left. Where the columns do not fit at their least widths the table scrolls sideways: by a drag, by a wheel, by the bar under the rows where a pointer leads, and by the keyboard, which brings the cell with the focus into view. A column pinned to an edge stays there while the others pass under it. The end of a resizable column's header is dragged with a pointer, and moved with the arrow keys once Tab has come to it. Which columns there are, and in which order, is the list itself: a screen that lets its reader hide a column or move one gives the table another list.

**Height.** A table told no height is as tall as its rows and builds them all: that is for a page of rows, in a screen that scrolls, and its header goes up with the page as the rows do. A table told a height keeps its header in place, scrolls its rows under it and builds only the ones in view, so that it holds thousands: a table whose header is to stay is told a height. A height it may not pass is a height too: a table laid straight in a window, with nothing around it that scrolls, is no taller than the window, and one that shares a column with other things is given `Modifier.weight`, as a lazy list is.

**State.** Where the rows are scrolled to, how far the columns are and the widths they were dragged to are kept in a `DataTableState`, which a screen holds itself to read them, to keep them and to scroll to a column.

**Narrow.** A table of `DataTableLayout.Auto` narrower than the style's `compactWidth` is a list of records: each row a block, a column's name before each of its values. The boxes, the chevrons and the order stay: the names of the columns that sort stand in a strip over the list, each the button it is in the header. Where the names do not fit, the strip scrolls sideways, fades towards the end it goes on past, and shows the name of the column the records are ordered by. A column that is not in the list has no name there.

**Keyboard and screen readers.** Tab goes through the headers that sort, the boxes, the chevrons, the rows that can be pressed and whatever the cells hold, and the arrow keys move the focus to the nearest of them that way. A cell that holds nothing to press is no stop: this is a table to read and to act on, and not a grid of cells to walk. Where a pointer leads, the rows' window is a stop itself while the table scrolls, so that a table of plain values is scrolled by the keyboard too: by the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End. A header says that it is one, as a heading, and how its column is ordered; a box says which row it chooses where `rowLabel` names the rows, and a cell which row and column it is in.

Parameters:

- `rows: List<T>`: the rows, in the order they are shown.
- `columns: List<DataTableColumn<T>>`: the columns, in the order they are shown. No two of them have one key. Keep the list in a `remember`: a table given its columns anew at every composition lays every row out again.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the table's modifier. The table is as wide as the room it is given.
- `rowKey: ((row: T) -> String)?`: what tells a row from the others, the same while the row is the same: what `selected` and `expanded` hold, and the row's automation key. Rows that are chosen or opened need one. Without it a row is known by its place.
- `rowLabel: ((row: T) -> String)?`: what a screen reader calls a row by: `Select Ada Lovelace` in place of twenty boxes that all say `Select row`.
- `rowEnabled: ((row: T) -> Boolean)?`: whether a row can be chosen and pressed. One that cannot is drawn fainter, its box is closed, and the box in the header neither chooses it nor lets it go. Its chevron opens it all the same, and what its cells hold stays the caller's to close. A table whose every row is closed is given `{ false }`.
- `rowTone: ((row: T) -> DataTableTone?)?`: what a row means, or null for a row like the others: the row lies on the soft fill of the tone's role, over any stripe, and what it shows is written in the colour the theme pairs with that fill.
- `sort: List<DataTableSort>`: the order the rows are in: the columns it goes by, the first one first. It is drawn in the headers.
- `onSortChange: ((List<DataTableSort>) -> Unit)?`: called with the order a press on a sortable column's header asks for: smallest first, then largest first, then no order. Null leaves the headers as names.
- `multiSort: Boolean`: whether a press adds its column to the order, to settle the rows the columns before it hold equal, in place of ordering by that column alone.
- `selected: Set<String>`: the keys of the rows that are chosen.
- `onSelectionChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)?`: called with the keys that are to be chosen after a box was pressed. Null leaves the table without boxes.
- `selection: DataTableSelection`: whether many rows are chosen or one.
- `expanded: Set<String>`: the keys of the rows that are open.
- `onExpandedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)?`: called with the keys that are to be open after a chevron was pressed. Null leaves the rows without chevrons: the rows named in `expanded` are open all the same.
- `expansion: DataTableExpansion`: whether many rows are open at a time or one. Where it is one, a chevron that opens a row asks for that row alone, and the row that was open closes; the rows named in `expanded` are open as they are given.
- `rowDetail: (@Composable (row: T) -> Unit)?`: what an open row shows under itself, as wide as the table.
- `onRowClick: ((row: T) -> Unit)?`: called with a row that was pressed. It makes every row a button.
- `loading: Boolean`: whether the rows are still on their way: blocks stand in their place, in the table's columns.
- `loadingRows: Int`: how many rows of blocks stand there.
- `empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what a table without rows shows in their place, in place of the theme's words for it.
- `toolbar: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands over the header inside the table's edge: a title, a search field, what is done with the chosen rows.
- `footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands under the rows inside the table's edge: a `PantrixPagination`, a count.
- `listContent: (@Composable (row: T) -> Unit)?`: what a record of the list shows, in place of its columns' names and values.
- `variant: DataTableVariant`: how much is drawn around the rows.
- `striped: Boolean`: whether every other row is laid on a faint fill, to keep the eye on its line.
- `layout: DataTableLayout`: whether this is a table, a list, or whichever its width has room for.
- `headerTextStyle: TextStyle`: what the columns' names are written in: the control label's type, a little heavier. A table whose headers are small capitals set apart gives that type here, and writes its headers in capitals.
- `state: DataTableState`: where the rows and the columns are scrolled to and the widths the columns were dragged to.
- `style: DataTableStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: DataTableColors?`: this table's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the table's automation key: the table is `DataTable_<tagKey>`, and in it a header is `Header_<column>`, a row `Row_<row>`, a cell `Cell_<row>/<column>`, a row's box `Select_<row>`, its chevron `Toggle_<row>` and what it opens `Detail_<row>`. A press is reported as a `DataTable` event: `sort`, `select`, `selectAll`, `expand`, `collapse` and `open`.

### DataTablePin

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.datatable.DataTablePin`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class DataTablePin
```

Where a column of a `PantrixDataTable` stands while the others scroll sideways.

Entries:

- `None`: With the others: it scrolls sideways where the columns do not fit the table.
- `Start`: At the table's start, before every column that scrolls: the column that names a row. It stays there while the others scroll under its edge. The right edge in a right-to-left layout.
- `End`: At the table's end, after every column that scrolls: a row's actions.

### DataTableColumn

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.datatable.DataTableColumn`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class DataTableColumn<T>(
    public val key: String,
    public val header: String,
    public val width: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val weight: Float = 1f,
    public val minWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val alignment: Alignment.Horizontal = Alignment.Start,
    public val sortable: Boolean = false,
    public val comparator: Comparator<T>? = null,
    public val pin: DataTablePin = DataTablePin.None,
    public val resizable: Boolean = false,
    public val showInList: Boolean = true,
    public val tone: DataTableTone? = null,
    public val cell: @Composable (row: T) -> Unit
)
```

One column of a `PantrixDataTable`: its header, how wide it is, and what a row shows in it.

```kotlin
DataTableColumn(key = "state", header = stringResource(Res.string.state), width = 120.dp) { order ->
    PantrixBadge(text = order.state.label)
}
```

A column of plain text is written shorter with `DataTableColumn.text`, which cuts a long text with an ellipsis and orders the rows by it.

**Width.** A column given a `width` is that wide. One given none shares what the fixed columns leave, by its `weight`, and is no narrower than `minWidth`. Where the columns do not fit the table at their least widths, they keep those and the table scrolls sideways.

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What tells this column from the others, the same in every language: what a `DataTableSort` names, and the column's automation key. No two columns of a table have one key.
- `header: String`: The column's name, written once over the rows and before each value in the list a narrow table becomes. It is written as given: a header is a word of a language before it is a style, and the table does not turn it to capitals.
- `width: Dp`: A fixed width, or `Dp.Unspecified` for a share of what is left.
- `weight: Float`: This column's share of what the fixed columns leave, where `width` is unspecified.
- `minWidth: Dp`: The least width of a column that shares, or `Dp.Unspecified` for the style's `columnMinWidth`.
- `alignment: Alignment.Horizontal`: Where the header and what a row shows stand in the column. Numbers end at its end, so that their digits line up.
- `sortable: Boolean`: Whether a press on the header asks for the rows in this column's order. A column with a `comparator` is sortable without it. The header of a column that sorts keeps the place of the order's arrow beside its name, whether the rows are in its order or not: a `width` that just fits the name cuts it.
- `comparator: Comparator<T>?`: How two rows compare by this column, smallest first, for a screen that holds all its rows and orders them itself with comparator. A table whose order is made elsewhere, as by a server, names none.
- `pin: DataTablePin`: Whether the column stays at an edge while the others scroll sideways.
- `resizable: Boolean`: Whether the column's width can be dragged at the end of its header with a pointer. The table keeps the width it was dragged to.
- `showInList: Boolean`: Whether the column is in the list a narrow table becomes: one of a record's lines, and, where it sorts, one of the names over the list that order it. A column that is there for the table's shape, as a row's actions are, is left out. So is one that a record drawn its own way does not show: it sorts in the table, and the list is not ordered by what it does not show.
- `tone: DataTableTone?`: What the column's header is tinted with, or null for a header like the others: the soft fill of one of the theme's roles behind the column's name, which is written in the colour the theme pairs with it. It marks the header alone. What the rows show under it is `cell`'s to colour.
- `cell: @Composable (row: T) -> Unit`: What a row shows in this column.

On the type:

- `DataTableColumn.<T> text(key: String, header: String, width: Dp = Dp.Unspecified, weight: Float = 1f, minWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified, alignment: Alignment.Horizontal = Alignment.Start, sortable: Boolean = false, comparator: Comparator<T>? = null, pin: DataTablePin = DataTablePin.None, resizable: Boolean = false, showInList: Boolean = true, tone: DataTableTone? = null, maxLines: Int = 1, textOrder: Comparator<String>? = null, text: (row: T) -> String): DataTableColumn<T>`: A column of plain text: `text` says what a row shows, on `maxLines` lines at the most, cut with an ellipsis where it is longer, in the control label's type.

  ```kotlin
  DataTableColumn.text(key = "customer", header = stringResource(Res.string.customer)) { it.customer }
  ```

  Given `sortable = true` and no `comparator`, it orders the rows by that text, without regard to case. A column of numbers written as text names its own `comparator`: as texts, `10` comes before `9`.

  Unless told, the texts are compared letter by letter as Unicode numbers the letters: the same on every platform, and not as any language's alphabet has them, so that `ç` comes after `z`. Names that a reader looks up by their alphabet are given the language's own order with `textOrder`:

  ```kotlin
  val order = rememberTextOrder()
  val columns = remember(order) {
      listOf(
          DataTableColumn.text<Order>(key = "name", header = name, sortable = true, textOrder = order) {
              it.customer
          }
      )
  }
  ```

  `key`: what tells this column from the others, the same in every language: what a `DataTableSort` names, and the column's automation key. No two columns of a table have one key.

  `header`: the column's name, written once over the rows and before each value in the list a narrow table becomes. It is written as given: the table does not turn it to capitals.

  `width`: a fixed width, or `Dp.Unspecified` for a share of what is left.

  `weight`: this column's share of what the fixed columns leave, where `width` is unspecified.

  `minWidth`: the least width of a column that shares, or `Dp.Unspecified` for the style's `columnMinWidth`.

  `alignment`: where the header and what a row shows stand in the column. Numbers end at its end, so that their digits line up.

  `sortable`: whether a press on the header asks for the rows in this column's order. A column with a `comparator` is sortable without it. The header of a column that sorts keeps the place of the order's arrow beside its name: a `width` that just fits the name cuts it.

  `pin`: whether the column stays at an edge while the others scroll sideways.

  `resizable`: whether the column's width can be dragged at the end of its header with a pointer. The table keeps the width it was dragged to.

  `showInList`: whether the column is in the list a narrow table becomes: one of a record's lines, and, where it sorts, one of the names over the list that order it.

  `tone`: what the column's header is tinted with, or null for a header like the others: the soft fill of one of the theme's roles behind the column's name, which is written in the colour the theme pairs with it. It marks the header alone.

  `maxLines`: how many lines a row's text has at the most.

  `textOrder`: how two texts compare, for a column that orders the rows by its text: the order of a language, as `PantrixLocale.textOrder` and `rememberTextOrder` give it.

  `text`: what a row shows in this column.

```kotlin
fun <T> List<DataTableSort>.comparator(columns: List<DataTableColumn<T>>): Comparator<T>
```

How two rows compare in this order: by the first column named, and where that says they are equal by the next. Each column compares by its own `DataTableColumn.comparator`, turned round where the order is descending; a column that has none, or that is not among `columns`, says nothing. With no order at all every two rows are equal, and a sort that keeps equal rows as they were, as `sortedWith` does, leaves the list as it is.

### DataTableState

`import com.pantrixui.components.data.datatable.DataTableState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class DataTableState(public val listState: LazyListState = LazyListState())
```

What a `PantrixDataTable` holds from one composition to the next, for a screen that reads it, keeps it or changes it: where the rows are scrolled to, how far the columns are scrolled sideways, and the widths the columns were given by a drag.

```kotlin
val table = rememberDataTableState()
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
PantrixDataTable(rows = orders, columns = columns, state = table)
PantrixButton(text = total, onClick = { scope.launch { table.animateScrollToColumn("total") } })
PantrixButton(text = reset, onClick = { table.columnWidths = emptyMap() })
```

One state is one table's: two tables given the same one would scroll each other's columns.

Parameters:

- `listState: LazyListState`: The state of the list the rows scroll in, where the table is told a height.

Members:

- `columnWidths: Map<String, Dp>`: The widths columns were given after the table laid them out, by their keys: by a drag at the end of a resizable column's header, by the arrow keys there, or by the screen itself, which may write them. A width kept from the last visit goes in here, and an empty map gives every column back the width the table makes it. A column that is not named is as wide as the table makes it.
- `columnScroll: Float`: How far the columns are scrolled from their start, in pixels: nought at rest. Their start is at the right where the table is read from there.
- `columnScrollRange: Float`: How far the columns can be scrolled, in pixels: nought while every column fits the table.
- `suspend fun scrollColumnsBy(pixels: Float): Float`: Scrolls the columns `pixels` further from their start at once, or back towards it by a negative distance, no further than their two ends. Returns how far they went.
- `suspend fun animateScrollColumnsBy(pixels: Float): Float`: Scrolls the columns as `scrollColumnsBy` does, with the motion a wheel's turn has.

  `pixels`: how far the columns scroll, in pixels: further from their start, or back towards it where it is less than nought.
- `suspend fun scrollToColumn(columnKey: String)`: Brings the column with `columnKey` into view at once, by the shorter way, and no further than it has to go. Nothing happens for a column that is in view already, one that is pinned, or one the table does not have.
- `suspend fun animateScrollToColumn(columnKey: String)`: Brings the column with `columnKey` into view as `scrollToColumn` does, with a motion.

On the type:

- `DataTableState.saver(listState: LazyListState): Saver<DataTableState, Any>`: Keeps how far the columns are scrolled and the widths they were given, for a state that is to come back as it was: `rememberSaveable(saver = DataTableState.saver(listState)) { DataTableState(listState) }`. Where the rows are is `listState`'s own to keep.
