## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.datefilledtextfield

### PantrixDateFilledTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datefilledtextfield.PantrixDateFilledTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDateFilledTextField(
    value: PantrixDate?,
    onValueChange: (PantrixDate?) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    format: DateFieldFormat = DateFieldFormat.of(PantrixTheme.locale),
    presentation: DatePickerPresentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    pickerStyle: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    pickerColors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A filled text field for a day: the day is typed in digits, or chosen from a calendar that a button at the box's end opens. It is `PantrixDateTextField` in a filled box.

It is drawn as `PantrixFilledTextField` is, the label inside the box where it rests in the text's place while the field is empty and without the focus, and the pattern shows once the label has moved up. It takes digits alone: the `format`'s mark comes in by itself as each part of the day is whole, so `18102026` shows as `18.10.2026` in Turkish and `10182026` as `10/18/2026` in American English. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `GG.AA.YYYY` in Turkish and `MM/DD/YYYY` in American English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A day pasted written out is read as it is written, in the `format`'s order and else with the year first as ISO 8601 has it: `2026-10-18` pasted in Turkish shows as `18.10.2026`, and a year of two digits is the one of the hundred years around `today` that ends in them.

`onValueChange` is told the day the field holds each time it changes: a whole day the calendar takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no day or a day it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed day stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a day other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a day.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole day, once the user has left the field; a day the calendar has not, the 31st of February; a day before `minDate` or after `maxDate`; and a day `isDateEnabled` turns down. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The calendar opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a day from the calendar alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A day pressed in it is the field's at once and closes it; Escape and a press outside close it and change nothing. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen day, or to today, and comes back to the field as it closes.

Parameters:

- `value: PantrixDate?`: the day the field shows, or null.
- `onValueChange: (PantrixDate?) -> Unit`: told the field's day each time the user changes it: a day, or null for none.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no calendar.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the day can only be chosen from the calendar, and not typed.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its calendar's.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the caller finds the day wrong, as a day already taken: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day the field takes, or null for no first. Not after `maxDate`.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day the field takes, or null for no last.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether the field takes a day between the two, or null for every day: a weekday, a day not yet booked.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the calendar's weeks start on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday as ISO 8601 numbers them, or null for the language's.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day the calendar marks as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight.
- `format: DateFieldFormat`: the order the parts are typed in and the mark between them: the theme's language's and region's by default. `of`: The role of the theme this tone is drawn in.
- `presentation: DatePickerPresentation`: what the calendar opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.
- `pickerStyle: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style of the calendar.
- `pickerColors: DatePickerColors?`: this call's own colours of the calendar.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `DateFilledTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `DateFilledTextFieldCalendar_<tagKey>`, its clear button `DateFilledTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its calendar `DatePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the calendar opened and that a day was chosen in it, and never the day.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

Documented on: [Date Filled Text Field](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/date-filled-text-field.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker

### PantrixDatePicker

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDatePicker(
    selected: PantrixDate?,
    onSelect: (PantrixDate) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    style: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A calendar to choose a day from, a month at a time: the month's title between the arrows that turn it, the days of the week over its columns, and its days.

The calendar is the choice itself, and stands where it is put: in the page, or in a `PantrixPopover`, a `PantrixDialog` or a `PantrixSheet` that a button or a field opens. It paints no ground of its own and holds nothing of the choice: `selected` is the caller's, and a press on a day hands it to `onSelect`. What it keeps is the month on show, which starts at the chosen day's, or today's, and goes to the chosen day's month when the caller chooses one that is not on show.

The days a calendar cannot take are drawn faint and cannot be chosen: those before `minDate` and after `maxDate`, which the arrows do not turn to either, and those between that `isDateEnabled` leaves out, a weekend, a day that is full. Pressing the title shows the years in place of the days, and choosing one turns the calendar to the same month of that year.

The calendar is one stop for Tab, on the chosen day, today or the month's first, and its keys walk the days as a calendar's do: the arrows a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month, with Shift a year, Home and End the week's first and last day; Enter and Space choose. A screen reader hears each day in full, with the day of the week, and is told politely when the month changes.

Days are `PantrixDate`s, with no library of dates: docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md turns them into an app's own.

```kotlin
var due by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
PantrixDatePicker(
    selected = due,
    onSelect = { due = it },
    minDate = PantrixDate.today(),
    tagKey = "due"
)
```

Parameters:

- `selected: PantrixDate?`: the chosen day, or null while none is.
- `onSelect: (PantrixDate) -> Unit`: handed the day a press chose: one that can be chosen.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the calendar's modifier. The calendar is seven days wide, and narrower where it is given less room. Given a width, as `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` gives it the width of a sheet, it fills it: its columns grow as far as `DatePickerStyle.maxCellWidth`, and past that it stands in the middle.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day that can be chosen, or null for none so early.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day that can be chosen, or null for none so late.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether a day between them can be chosen, or null where every one can.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the weeks start on, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Null is the language's, `PantrixLocale.firstDayOfWeek`: Sunday in English, Monday in Turkish, Saturday in Arabic.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a day can be chosen at all. A calendar that takes no choice is drawn faint.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day marked as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight. A test gives a day of its own.
- `style: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: DatePickerColors?`: this calendar's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the calendar's automation key: it is `DatePicker_<tagKey>`, and its days are `DatePicker_<tagKey>.Day_2026_10_17`.

Documented on: [Date Picker](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/date-picker.md)

### PantrixDatePicker

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDatePicker(
    selectedRange: PantrixDateRange?,
    onRangeSelect: (PantrixDateRange) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    style: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A calendar to choose a stretch of days from: a stay, a leave, the days a report is of. It is the calendar that chooses a day, pressed twice: its first press chooses the first day of the stretch and its second the last.

The second press ends the stretch on its day, or on the first day again for a stretch of one day, and `onRangeSelect` is handed the stretch; one before the first day starts the stretch again from there. Between the two presses the first day is the calendar's own, and under a pointer the stretch it would make is drawn lighter. A stretch may run over days that cannot be chosen; its first and its last day are ones that can.

`selectedRange` is the caller's: the calendar draws it with its first and last day marked and a band under the days between, and goes to its first day's month when the caller chooses one of which no day is on show.

Parameters:

- `selectedRange: PantrixDateRange?`: the chosen stretch, or null while none is.
- `onRangeSelect: (PantrixDateRange) -> Unit`: handed the stretch two presses chose.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the calendar's modifier. The calendar is seven days wide, and narrower where it is given less room; given a width, it fills it as far as `DatePickerStyle.maxCellWidth` lets its columns grow.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day that can be chosen, or null for none so early.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day that can be chosen, or null for none so late.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether a day between them can be the first or the last day of a stretch, or null where every one can.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the weeks start on, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Null is the language's, `PantrixLocale.firstDayOfWeek`.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a stretch can be chosen at all. A calendar that takes no choice is drawn faint.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day marked as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight. A test gives a day of its own.
- `style: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: DatePickerColors?`: this calendar's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the calendar's automation key: it is `DatePicker_<tagKey>`, and its days are `DatePicker_<tagKey>.Day_2026_10_17`.

Documented on: [Date Picker](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/date-picker.md)

### DatePickerStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.DatePickerStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class DatePickerStyle(
    public val cellSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val daySize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val padding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxCellWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<DatePickerStyle>
```

`PantrixDatePicker`'s geometry: the room of a day, the round mark a chosen day is drawn in, and the room around the month.

A day's room is as wide as a column of the week and as tall as a row of it, and the days touch: a press anywhere in the room is the day's. On a phone it is the platform's least touch target, 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS, so that a month is seven targets wide, 360dp across on Android as a Material calendar is. Under a pointer it is 36dp. A place too narrow for the month makes every day's room narrower, and its mark with it, by the same share. A calendar given more width than that, as a sheet gives it with `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`, widens its columns to fill it, up to `maxCellWidth`, and stands in the middle of what is left; its rows and its marks keep their size.

The room around the month and the gap under its title follow the density; a day's room, its widest and its mark do not, as a touch target does not.

Parameters:

- `cellSize: Dp`: The width and the height of a day's room: the column and the row. The title and the year's rooms are as tall.
- `daySize: Dp`: The width and the height of the round mark a chosen day, today and the day under a pointer are drawn in, in the middle of its room. A stretch of days is a band as tall.
- `padding: Dp`: The room between the calendar's edge and what it holds.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the title and the days of the week over the month.
- `maxCellWidth: Dp`: The widest a column grows to where the calendar is given more width than seven days' rooms: half as wide again as `cellSize`.

Documented on: [Date Picker](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/date-picker.md)

### DatePickerColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.DatePickerColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class DatePickerColors(
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val weekday: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContainer: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val rangeContainer: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val rangeContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val today: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val hover: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val disabled: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixDatePicker` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `selectedContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the chosen day's number, unless `selectedContent` is given too, and a `rangeContainer` brings its pair for the days of a stretch, unless `rangeContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

The calendar paints no ground of its own: it stands on what is under it, a popover's, a dialog's, a sheet's or a page's, and its words are the theme's for its grounds.

Parameters:

- `content: Color`: The days' numbers, the title and the arrows. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `weekday: Color`: The days of the week over the columns. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `selectedContainer: Color`: The round mark of a chosen day, and of a stretch's first and last. The primary role's `color`.
- `selectedContent: Color`: The number on it. The primary role's `onColor`, or the colour a role's fill given as `selectedContainer` gives what stands on it.
- `rangeContainer: Color`: The band under the days between a stretch's first and last. The primary role's `container`. While the last is being chosen under a pointer, the band to the day under it is drawn in half of it.
- `rangeContent: Color`: The numbers on the band. The primary role's `onContainer`.
- `today: Color`: The ring around today, and its number. The primary role's `color`.
- `hover: Color`: The round mark under a pointer: which day a press would choose. A share of `content`.
- `disabled: Color`: The numbers of the days that cannot be chosen, and everything of a calendar that takes no choice. The theme's `textDisabled`.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield

### PantrixDateTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDateTextField(
    value: PantrixDate?,
    onValueChange: (PantrixDate?) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    format: DateFieldFormat = DateFieldFormat.of(PantrixTheme.locale),
    presentation: DatePickerPresentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    pickerStyle: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    pickerColors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field for a day: the day is typed in digits, or chosen from a calendar that a button at the box's end opens.

It is drawn as `PantrixTextField` is, the label above the box, and takes digits alone: the `format`'s mark comes in by itself as each part of the day is whole, so `18102026` shows as `18.10.2026` in Turkish and `10182026` as `10/18/2026` in American English. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `GG.AA.YYYY` in Turkish and `MM/DD/YYYY` in American English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A day pasted written out is read as it is written, in the `format`'s order and else with the year first as ISO 8601 has it: `2026-10-18` pasted in Turkish shows as `18.10.2026`, and a year of two digits is the one of the hundred years around `today` that ends in them.

`onValueChange` is told the day the field holds each time it changes: a whole day the calendar takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no day or a day it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed day stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a day other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a day.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole day, once the user has left the field; a day the calendar has not, the 31st of February; a day before `minDate` or after `maxDate`; and a day `isDateEnabled` turns down. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The calendar opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a day from the calendar alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A day pressed in it is the field's at once and closes it; Escape and a press outside close it and change nothing. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen day, or to today, and comes back to the field as it closes.

Parameters:

- `value: PantrixDate?`: the day the field shows, or null.
- `onValueChange: (PantrixDate?) -> Unit`: told the field's day each time the user changes it: a day, or null for none.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no calendar.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the day can only be chosen from the calendar, and not typed.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its calendar's.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the caller finds the day wrong, as a day already taken: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day the field takes, or null for no first. Not after `maxDate`.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day the field takes, or null for no last.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether the field takes a day between the two, or null for every day: a weekday, a day not yet booked.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the calendar's weeks start on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday as ISO 8601 numbers them, or null for the language's.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day the calendar marks as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight.
- `format: DateFieldFormat`: the order the parts are typed in and the mark between them: the theme's language's and region's by default. `of`: The role of the theme this tone is drawn in.
- `presentation: DatePickerPresentation`: what the calendar opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.
- `style: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: TextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.
- `pickerStyle: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style of the calendar.
- `pickerColors: DatePickerColors?`: this call's own colours of the calendar.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `DateTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `DateTextFieldCalendar_<tagKey>`, its clear button `DateTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its calendar `DatePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the calendar opened and that a day was chosen in it, and never the day.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

Documented on: [Date Text Field](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/date-text-field.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.elasticdatepicker

### PantrixAutoRefresh

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.elasticdatepicker.PantrixAutoRefresh`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class PantrixAutoRefresh(
    public val every: Int,
    public val unit: AutoRefreshUnit = AutoRefreshUnit.Seconds,
    public val paused: Boolean = true
)
```

How often an elastic date picker reads its range again by itself, as Elastic UI's refresh interval: every `every` `unit`s while it is not `paused`. The picker counts the time and does what Refresh does at each turn: `onRefresh`, which is waited for before the next turn is counted, or the same range handed over where it has none.

Parameters:

- `every: Int`: how many `unit`s come between two refreshes; one at least.
- `unit: AutoRefreshUnit`: what `every` counts.
- `paused: Boolean`: whether it waits: the picker counts nothing.

Members:

- `interval: Duration`: How long the picker waits between two refreshes.

### PantrixElasticDatePicker

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.elasticdatepicker.PantrixElasticDatePicker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixElasticDatePicker(
    range: PantrixTimeRange,
    onRangeChange: (PantrixTimeRange) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    commonlyUsed: List<PantrixQuickRange> = PantrixQuickRange.commonlyUsed(PantrixTheme.strings),
    recentlyUsed: PantrixRecentRanges? = null,
    updateButton: ElasticDatePickerUpdateButton = ElasticDatePickerUpdateButton.Text,
    presentation: DatePickerPresentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
    loading: Boolean = false,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    onRefresh: (suspend () -> Unit)? = null,
    roundRelativeUnits: Boolean = true,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    is24Hour: Boolean = true,
    style: ElasticDatePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: ElasticDatePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    autoRefresh: PantrixAutoRefresh? = null,
    onAutoRefreshChange: ((PantrixAutoRefresh) -> Unit)? = null,
    minAutoRefresh: Duration = Duration.ZERO,
    layout: ElasticDatePickerLayout = ElasticDatePickerLayout.Full,
    timeWindowButtons: ElasticTimeWindowButtons? = null,
    customQuickPanels: List<ElasticQuickPanel> = emptyList(),
    quickMenu: (@Composable ElasticQuickMenuScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    timeZoneName: String? = null,
    utcOffset: ((Instant) -> Duration)? = null,
    disabledText: String? = null
)
```

A range of time that can move with the clock, as a dashboard is filtered by: "the last 15 minutes" is still the last 15 minutes at the next refresh. Elastic UI's `EuiSuperDatePicker`, built again on Pantrix.

A field holds the range and a button beside it refreshes it or takes an edit. Every part opens a panel, a popover by default, or a sheet or a dialog where `presentation` asks for one, on every platform alike:

- **The quick menu's button**, the calendar at the field's start, opens the last or the next amount of a unit, ‹ and › to move the range by its own length, the ranges `commonlyUsed` offers by name, and those `recentlyUsed` holds. A choice there is handed over at once.

- **The range's name**, "Last 15 minutes" or "Today", stands in the field while the range has one. A press on it shows the two ends, start → end, and opens the start's panel.

- **An end** opens its tabs: a moment on a calendar, with the times of the day by the half hour and the moment to type; an amount of time from now, with the moment it falls on and a switch that rounds it; or now itself. Moving to a tab makes the end what that tab shows. An edit waits: the field is painted in the success colour with a mark at its end, and the button beside it says Update, which hands the range over. An end before the start paints the field in the danger colour, and Update takes nothing. With `updateButton` `None` each edit is handed over at once. Apply at the end of the moment's field on the calendar's and the relative tab takes the edit and closes the panel, and the button of now's tab makes the end now and does the same.

- **Refresh** reads the range again where no edit waits: `onRefresh` where it is given, and `onRangeChange` with the same range where not.

A press outside an open popover goes on to what it lands on, as in Elastic UI: one press on the other end opens that end's panel, one on Update takes the edit, and one on the open end's button closes its panel. A sheet and a dialog stand over a scrim, and a press on it closes them alone.

The panels are set close, as Elastic UI's are: an end's popover is as wide as its calendar and the times beside it, the quick menu's 400dp, and the text fields, selects, tabs and buttons in them are 8 lower than a form's, 40dp on Android, 36pt on iOS and 32dp on the desktop and the web.

The range is the caller's: a new `range` drops an edit that waits. Where the field has less room than its words and its button need, the button beside it is its icon alone.

```kotlin
val lastQuarterHour = PantrixTimeRange(PantrixTimePoint.Relative(-15, PantrixTimeUnit.Minutes), PantrixTimePoint.Now)
var range by remember { mutableStateOf(lastQuarterHour) }
PantrixElasticDatePicker(range = range, onRangeChange = { range = it }, recentlyUsed = rememberRecentRanges())
```

Parameters:

- `range: PantrixTimeRange`: the range on show. Its ends can be relative to now.
- `onRangeChange: (PantrixTimeRange) -> Unit`: handed the range the reader chose from the quick menu or updated after an edit, or the same range on a refresh without `onRefresh`.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the picker's modifier. The picker fills the width it is given, up to the style's `maxWidth`.
- `commonlyUsed: List<PantrixQuickRange>`: the ranges the quick menu offers by name: by default Elastic UI's eight, in the theme's language. A range on show that is one of these is called by its name.
- `recentlyUsed: PantrixRecentRanges?`: the ranges the reader chose lately, which the quick menu lists and each range the reader applies is recorded in; null for none. `rememberRecentRanges()` keeps them across a configuration change.
- `updateButton: ElasticDatePickerUpdateButton`: the button beside the field: its words and icon, its icon alone, or none, every edit then handed over at once.
- `presentation: DatePickerPresentation`: what the panels open in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover beside the part pressed in a wider one, chosen as a panel opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog. The same on every platform.
- `loading: Boolean`: whether what the range filters loads: the button beside the field spins and takes no press.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the picker takes a choice at all. One that takes none is drawn faint and opens nothing.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day an end's calendar offers, or null for none so early.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day it offers, or null for none so late.
- `onRefresh: (suspend () -> Unit)?`: what Refresh does where no edit waits, the button spinning while it runs; null to hand the same range to `onRangeChange`. What it throws stops the spinning and goes no further: what went wrong is the caller's to tell, as it is when a turn of `autoRefresh` fails.
- `roundRelativeUnits: Boolean`: whether an end that is an amount from now is put in the unit that reads best, "~ 2 hours ago" for 90 minutes, or keeps its own.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the calendar's weeks start on and a week is rounded to, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday. Null is the language's, `PantrixLocale.firstDayOfWeek`.
- `is24Hour: Boolean`: whether a moment is written and chosen by a clock of twenty-four hours, `22:00`, or of twelve, `10:00 PM`.
- `style: ElasticDatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: ElasticDatePickerColors?`: the field's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the picker's automation key: it is `ElasticDatePicker_<tagKey>`, its parts `.Button_quick_menu`, `.Button_name`, `.Button_start`, `.Button_end`, `.Button_auto_refresh`, the time window buttons `.Button_window_previous`, `.Button_window_zoom_in`, `.Button_window_zoom_out` and `.Button_window_next`, and the button beside the field `Button_<tagKey>_update`.
- `autoRefresh: PantrixAutoRefresh?`: how often the range is read again by itself, or null for never. While it is not paused the field ends in how often, written short, and Refresh is done at each turn: `onRefresh`, waited for before the next turn is counted, or the same range handed to `onRangeChange`. An `onRefresh` that fails pauses it, and says so through `onAutoRefreshChange`.
- `onAutoRefreshChange: ((PantrixAutoRefresh) -> Unit)?`: handed the refresh by itself as the reader sets it in the quick menu, where it has a part of its own; null for no such part.
- `minAutoRefresh: Duration`: the shortest refresh by itself the reader can set: a shorter one draws its amount as wrong.
- `layout: ElasticDatePickerLayout`: what the field shows: the range, the quick menu's button alone, or the refresh by itself alone.
- `timeWindowButtons: ElasticTimeWindowButtons?`: Elastic UI's buttons beside the field that move the range by its length and zoom it, or null for none.
- `customQuickPanels: List<ElasticQuickPanel>`: panels of the caller's own in the quick menu, after the ranges used lately.
- `quickMenu: (@Composable ElasticQuickMenuScope.() -> Unit)?`: the quick menu's parts in an order of the caller's own, some left out or panels of its own put in among them; null for Elastic UI's order.
- `timeZoneName: String?`: the time zone the moments are in, named in the ends' panels with its difference from UTC: "Time zone: Europe/Istanbul (UTC+03:00)". It names, and changes nothing; null for no such line.
- `utcOffset: ((Instant) -> Duration)?`: the difference from UTC the moments are read and written in at a moment; null for the screen's clock's (`LocalPantrixClock`), the device's unless a test or a preview gives another.
- `disabledText: String?`: what a picker that takes no choice shows in the place of its range; null for the range.

### ElasticDatePickerStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.elasticdatepicker.ElasticDatePickerStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ElasticDatePickerStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val padding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ElasticDatePickerStyle>
```

`PantrixElasticDatePicker`'s field: how tall it is, its corners, the room inside it, the gap between it and the button beside it, and how wide it gets.

The field is as tall as a text field on each platform and has its corners, 48dp on Android, 44pt on iOS and 40dp on the desktop and the web, since it stands beside a form's fields and a screen's search box. It fills the width it is given up to `maxWidth`, room for both ends of a range written as moments: Elastic UI's restricted width. What it opens is drawn with the styles of a popover, a sheet, a calendar and tabs.

The height, the room and the gap follow the density, as a text field's do; the corners and the width do not.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: How tall the field is.
- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The field's corners.
- `padding: Dp`: The room between the field's edge and what is in it, at either end.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the field and the button beside it, and between the parts in the field.
- `maxWidth: Dp`: The widest the field and its button get; `Dp.Infinity` for as wide as they are given.

### ElasticQuickMenuScope

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.elasticdatepicker.ElasticQuickMenuScope`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
interface ElasticQuickMenuScope
```

The parts of a picker's quick menu, for a menu in an order of the caller's own, after Elastic UI's custom quick select render. Each part stands where it is called, and the menu draws a line between each two; a part with nothing to show, the ranges used lately where there are none, takes no room and no line. A part left out is not in the menu.

Members:

- `@Composable fun QuickSelect()`: The last or the next amount of a unit, ‹ and › to move the range by its length, and Apply.
- `@Composable fun CommonlyUsed()`: The ranges the picker offers by name, in two columns.
- `@Composable fun RecentlyUsed()`: The ranges used lately, the latest first, where there are any.
- `@Composable fun CustomPanels()`: The picker's own panels, `customQuickPanels`, each a part of its own.
- `@Composable fun AutoRefresh()`: The refresh by itself, where the picker takes a change of it.
- `@Composable fun Panel(title: String, content: @Composable () -> Unit)`: A panel of the caller's own: `title` over `content`.

### ElasticTimeWindowButtons

```kotlin
    public val zoomIn: Boolean = false,

)
```

Elastic UI's time window buttons, beside a picker's field and its button: ‹ and › move the range back and on by its own length, zoom out widens it by `zoomFactor` of its length and zoom in narrows it by as much, half of it at each end. The range they hand over is of moments, as the quick menu's ‹ and › hand over.

‹, › and zoom in take nothing while the range has no length, and none of them while its ends are out of order. A range of no length is widened by half a second at each end.

- `zoomIn: Boolean`: whether zoom in is there: Elastic UI leaves it out unless it is asked for.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.timefilledtextfield

### PantrixTimeFilledTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.timefilledtextfield.PantrixTimeFilledTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTimeFilledTextField(
    value: PantrixTime?,
    onValueChange: (PantrixTime?) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    maxTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    minuteStep: Int = 1,
    is24Hour: Boolean = true,
    presentation: DatePickerPresentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    pickerStyle: TimePickerStyle? = null,
    pickerColors: TimePickerColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A filled text field for a time of day: the time is typed in digits, or chosen from a time picker that a button at the box's end opens. It is `PantrixTimeTextField` in a filled box.

It is drawn as `PantrixFilledTextField` is, the label inside the box where it rests in the text's place while the field is empty and without the focus, and the pattern shows once the label has moved up. It takes digits alone, four at most: the colon comes in by itself once the hour is whole, so `1430` shows as `14:30`, and a first digit that cannot start an hour is an hour of one digit, so `930` shows as `09:30`. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `SS:DD` in Turkish and `HH:MM` in English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A time pasted written out is read as it is written: `14:30`, `14.30`, `1430`, or `2:30 PM` with a half of the day; a second written after the minute is let go.

By a clock of twelve hours, `is24Hour` false, the hours are typed 01 to 12 and the half of the day stands in the box beside them, as a button: a press on it, or Space while it holds the focus, turns it, and A and P typed in the field set it.

`onValueChange` is told the time the field holds each time it changes: a whole time the field takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no time or a time it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed time stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a time other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a time. A `value`'s second is kept while its hour and minute are not typed over; a time typed has none.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole time, once the user has left the field; a time the clock has not, 25 o'clock; and a time before `minTime` or after `maxTime`. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The picker opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a time from the picker alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A value pressed in it is the field's at once and leaves it open, so that the minute can be chosen after the hour; Enter on a value, Escape and a press outside close it. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen hour, or to the hour it is now, and comes back to the field as it closes.

Parameters:

- `value: PantrixTime?`: the time the field shows, or null.
- `onValueChange: (PantrixTime?) -> Unit`: told the field's time each time the user changes it: a time, or null for none.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no picker.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the time can only be chosen from the picker, and not typed.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its picker's.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the caller finds the time wrong, as a time already booked: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `minTime: PantrixTime?`: the first time the field takes, or null for no first. Where it is after `maxTime`, the times run past midnight, as a night's do.
- `maxTime: PantrixTime?`: the last time the field takes, or null for no last.
- `minuteStep: Int`: how many minutes apart the picker's minutes are, 1 to 60. A minute typed between them is taken.
- `is24Hour: Boolean`: whether the field and its picker count the hours of a day, 00 to 23, or by a clock of twelve hours.
- `presentation: DatePickerPresentation`: what the picker opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.
- `pickerStyle: TimePickerStyle?`: this call's own style of the picker.
- `pickerColors: TimePickerColors?`: this call's own colours of the picker.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `TimeFilledTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `TimeFilledTextFieldClock_<tagKey>`, its half of the day `TimeFilledTextFieldPeriod_<tagKey>`, its clear button `TimeFilledTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its picker `TimePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the picker opened and that a value was chosen in it, and never the time.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

Documented on: [Time Filled Text Field](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/time-filled-text-field.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.timepicker

### PantrixTimePicker

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.timepicker.PantrixTimePicker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTimePicker(
    selected: PantrixTime?,
    onSelect: (PantrixTime) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    maxTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    minuteStep: Int = 1,
    is24Hour: Boolean = true,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: TimePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: TimePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A time of day to choose from columns: the hours, the minutes, and by a clock of twelve hours the half of the day, each a column of five rows that scrolls through the rest, the chosen value filled in the middle of it.

`is24Hour` gives it its shape: by twenty-four hours, two columns, the hours 00 to 23 and the minutes, that choose `22:00`; by twelve, the hours 12 to 11, the minutes and a third column of the half of the day, that choose `10:00 PM`. It is twenty-four hours in every language unless the call asks for twelve.

The picker is the choice itself, and stands where it is put: in the page, or in a `PantrixPopover`, a `PantrixDialog` or a `PantrixSheet` that a button or a field opens. It paints no ground of its own and holds nothing of the choice: `selected` is the caller's, and a press on a value hands `onSelect` the whole time it makes, the other columns kept as they are. With nothing chosen, an hour comes with its first minute, and a minute with the first hour the picker takes. A time it shows that is to be taken only on a press of OK is the caller's draft.

The values a picker cannot take are drawn faint and cannot be pressed: the minutes before `minTime` and after `maxTime`, and the hours none of whose minutes are between them. The minutes are `minuteStep` apart.

Each column is one stop for Tab, on its chosen value, and its keys choose as they walk: the arrows the value below and above, Home and End the first and the last, Page Down and Page Up six hours or fifteen minutes on, and typed digits the value they write, `1` then `4` the fourteenth hour; the arrows across go to the column beside. A screen reader hears each column by its name and each value as a button, and is told politely the time a press or a key chose.

Times are `PantrixTime`s, with no library of dates: docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md turns them into an app's own, and a day and a time into a moment.

```kotlin
var at by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixTime?>(null) }
PantrixTimePicker(
    selected = at,
    onSelect = { at = it },
    minuteStep = 15,
    tagKey = "at"
)
```

Parameters:

- `selected: PantrixTime?`: the chosen time, or null while none is. Its seconds are kept in every time a press makes of it.
- `onSelect: (PantrixTime) -> Unit`: handed the time a press or a key chose: one the picker takes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the picker's modifier. The picker is as wide as its columns; given more room, it stands in the middle of it.
- `minTime: PantrixTime?`: the first time that can be chosen, or null for none so early: its hour and minute.
- `maxTime: PantrixTime?`: the last time that can be chosen, or null for none so late. Where it comes before `minTime`, the times that can be chosen run past midnight, from `minTime` to `maxTime` of the next day: a night's. By a clock of 24 hours the column of the hours then starts at `minTime`'s, so that the night's hours stand together: 22, 23, 00.
- `minuteStep: Int`: how far apart the minutes in their column are, 1 to 60: 15 offers the hour's first, a quarter past, half past and a quarter to. A chosen minute between them is shown all the same.
- `is24Hour: Boolean`: whether the hours are counted by twenty-four, and so the picker's shape: two columns that choose `22:00`; or by twelve, with a third column of the half of the day, `10:00 PM`. Twenty-four by default, in every language. Either way the time chosen is a `PantrixTime` of twenty-four hours; a screen writes it by the same clock with `PantrixStrings.time(hour, minute, is24Hour = …)`.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a time can be chosen at all. A picker that takes no choice is drawn faint.
- `style: TimePickerStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TimePickerColors?`: this picker's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the picker's automation key: it is `TimePicker_<tagKey>`, and its values are `TimePicker_<tagKey>.Hour_14`, `.Minute_30` and `.Period_pm`.

Documented on: [Time Picker](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/time-picker.md)

### TimePickerStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.timepicker.TimePickerStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TimePickerStyle(
    public val cellSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val columnWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val padding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<TimePickerStyle>
```

`PantrixTimePicker`'s geometry: the room of a value in a column, the pill a chosen value is drawn in, how wide a column is, and the room around the columns.

A value's room is as wide as its column and as tall as a row, and the rows touch: a press anywhere in the room is the value's. On a phone a row is the platform's least touch target, 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS, as a calendar's day is; under a pointer it is 36dp. A column shows five rows and scrolls through the rest.

The room around the columns and the gap under their names follow the density; a row, its pill and a column's width do not, as a touch target does not.

Parameters:

- `cellSize: Dp`: The height of a value's room: a row.
- `markHeight: Dp`: The height of the pill a chosen value and the value under a pointer are drawn in, in the middle of its room. It is most of the column wide.
- `columnWidth: Dp`: The width of a column of values.
- `padding: Dp`: The room between the picker's edge and its columns.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the columns' names and their values.

Documented on: [Time Picker](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/time-picker.md)

### TimePickerColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.timepicker.TimePickerColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class TimePickerColors(
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val heading: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContainer: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val hover: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val disabled: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixTimePicker` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `selectedContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the chosen value's number, unless `selectedContent` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

The picker paints no ground of its own: it stands on what is under it, a popover's, a dialog's, a sheet's or a page's.

Parameters:

- `content: Color`: The values' numbers and the mark between the hours and the minutes. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `heading: Color`: The columns' names over them. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `selectedContainer: Color`: The pill of a chosen value. The primary role's `color`.
- `selectedContent: Color`: The number on it. The primary role's `onColor`, or the colour a role's fill given as `selectedContainer` gives what stands on it.
- `hover: Color`: The pill under a pointer: which value a press would choose. A share of `content`.
- `disabled: Color`: The values that cannot be chosen, and everything of a picker that takes no choice. The theme's `textDisabled`.

Documented on: [Time Picker](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/time-picker.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.date.timetextfield

### PantrixTimeTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.timetextfield.PantrixTimeTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTimeTextField(
    value: PantrixTime?,
    onValueChange: (PantrixTime?) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    maxTime: PantrixTime? = null,
    minuteStep: Int = 1,
    is24Hour: Boolean = true,
    presentation: DatePickerPresentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    pickerStyle: TimePickerStyle? = null,
    pickerColors: TimePickerColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field for a time of day: the time is typed in digits, or chosen from a time picker that a button at the box's end opens.

It is drawn as `PantrixTextField` is, the label above the box, and takes digits alone, four at most: the colon comes in by itself once the hour is whole, so `1430` shows as `14:30`, and a first digit that cannot start an hour is an hour of one digit, so `930` shows as `09:30`. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `SS:DD` in Turkish and `HH:MM` in English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A time pasted written out is read as it is written: `14:30`, `14.30`, `1430`, or `2:30 PM` with a half of the day; a second written after the minute is let go.

By a clock of twelve hours, `is24Hour` false, the hours are typed 01 to 12 and the half of the day stands in the box beside them, as a button: a press on it, or Space while it holds the focus, turns it, and A and P typed in the field set it.

`onValueChange` is told the time the field holds each time it changes: a whole time the field takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no time or a time it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed time stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a time other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a time. A `value`'s second is kept while its hour and minute are not typed over; a time typed has none.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole time, once the user has left the field; a time the clock has not, 25 o'clock; and a time before `minTime` or after `maxTime`. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The picker opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a time from the picker alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A value pressed in it is the field's at once and leaves it open, so that the minute can be chosen after the hour; Enter on a value, Escape and a press outside close it. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen hour, or to the hour it is now, and comes back to the field as it closes.

Parameters:

- `value: PantrixTime?`: the time the field shows, or null.
- `onValueChange: (PantrixTime?) -> Unit`: told the field's time each time the user changes it: a time, or null for none.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no picker.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the time can only be chosen from the picker, and not typed.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its picker's.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the caller finds the time wrong, as a time already booked: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `minTime: PantrixTime?`: the first time the field takes, or null for no first. Where it is after `maxTime`, the times run past midnight, as a night's do.
- `maxTime: PantrixTime?`: the last time the field takes, or null for no last.
- `minuteStep: Int`: how many minutes apart the picker's minutes are, 1 to 60. A minute typed between them is taken.
- `is24Hour: Boolean`: whether the field and its picker count the hours of a day, 00 to 23, or by a clock of twelve hours.
- `presentation: DatePickerPresentation`: what the picker opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.
- `style: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: TextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.
- `pickerStyle: TimePickerStyle?`: this call's own style of the picker.
- `pickerColors: TimePickerColors?`: this call's own colours of the picker.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `TimeTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `TimeTextFieldClock_<tagKey>`, its half of the day `TimeTextFieldPeriod_<tagKey>`, its clear button `TimeTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its picker `TimePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the picker opened and that a value was chosen in it, and never the time.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

Documented on: [Time Text Field](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/time-text-field.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.autotext

### PantrixAutoText

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.autotext.PantrixAutoText`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAutoText(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    style: TextStyle = LocalPantrixTextStyle.current,
    minFontSize: TextUnit = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote.fontSize,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    textAlign: TextAlign? = null,
    maxLines: Int = 1,
    minLines: Int = 1,
    overflow: TextOverflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
    softWrap: Boolean = true,
    role: TextRole = TextRole.Paragraph,
    selectable: Boolean = false,
    onTextLayout: ((TextLayoutResult) -> Unit)? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Text that gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a title or a name that is read whole in the room it has.

The text is as large as its `style` says while it fits. A text too long for its room is set in a smaller size, the largest in which all of it is in view: no wider than the width it is given, no taller than the height, and on no more than `maxLines` lines. It is one line unless told. With more lines the text wraps first, and is set smaller when its lines run out. At `minFontSize` it stops shrinking, and what still does not fit is cut as `overflow` says.

It needs a room to fit: a width from its parent or its `modifier`, and a height too where it may take any number of lines. A text that is offered all the width there is has room for any line, and is never set smaller.

The lines of a text that is set smaller are as much closer: the style's line height follows the size. So do the sizes its spans give in em, and one given in sp is kept. In everything else it is `PantrixText`: the theme's type, the colour of where it sits, and what a screen reader is told of it. The size is found while the text is laid out, so the first frame shows it fitted, and so does every frame in which its room gets narrower, wider or lower. A room that only gets taller is followed a frame later.

Parameters:

- `text: String`: the text.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the text's modifier: `fillMaxWidth()`, a `weight` or a size gives it the room it is fitted to.
- `style: TextStyle`: the style of the text at its largest: a role of the theme's typography, and the base text unless given, `LocalPantrixTextStyle`, as a `PantrixText`'s is. A style whose size is not in sp has no smaller size to be set in, and its text is not shrunk.
- `minFontSize: TextUnit`: the smallest the text gets: a size in sp, or one in em, which is a share of the style's own. It is the theme's footnote size unless told. At the style's own size or above it the text never shrinks, and at zero it shrinks until it fits, as far as a 256th of the style's size.
- `color: Color`: the text's colour. Unset, it is the style's, or the content colour of where the text sits, or the primary text colour.
- `textAlign: TextAlign?`: how the lines are aligned in the text's width.
- `maxLines: Int`: the most lines the text takes: one unless told. `Int.MAX_VALUE` leaves the lines to the height the text is given.
- `minLines: Int`: the least lines the text is tall, at its largest size.
- `overflow: TextOverflow`: how a text that does not fit at its smallest size is cut.
- `softWrap: Boolean`: whether the text wraps where its width ends. A text that does not is fitted to its longest line.
- `role: TextRole`: what the text is, for a screen reader: prose, a heading, a label or decoration.
- `selectable: Boolean`: whether the user can select the text and copy it.
- `onTextLayout: ((TextLayoutResult) -> Unit)?`: called with the text as it is laid out, in the size it is set in.
- `tagKey: String?`: the text's automation key: the text is `AutoText_<tagKey>`. Without one it has no tag.

Documented on: [Auto Text](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/auto-text.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.avatar

### AvatarTone

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.avatar.AvatarTone`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class AvatarTone
```

How an avatar is coloured where no picture covers it: one of the theme's colour roles, so a brand changes every avatar at once.

An avatar is filled in every tone, from the role's `color` and `onColor`, as initials on a solid circle are drawn everywhere else. The role's pale `container` is chosen for an area as wide as the screen, and a circle of it 32dp across is lost on a white page.

A tone says nothing by itself: a screen reader hears the avatar's description and not its colour, so what a colour is to mean has to be in the words beside it.

Entries:

- `Primary`: The brand's colour: the person using the app.
- `Info`: A distinction with no judgement in it: a guest, a group, an account that is not a person.
- `Success`: Someone or something in good standing.
- `Warning`: Someone or something to look at.
- `Danger`: Someone or something that failed or is blocked.
- `Neutral`: No meaning at all: a grey for the initials to sit on. The default.

Documented on: [Avatar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/avatar.md)

### PantrixAvatar

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.avatar.PantrixAvatar`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAvatar(
    contentDescription: String?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    initials: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    tone: AvatarTone = AvatarTone.Neutral,
    colors: AvatarColors? = null,
    style: AvatarStyle? = null,
    size: Dp = PantrixTheme.style(AvatarStyle, style).size,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    image: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null
)
```

The picture of a person or a thing: a photograph, the initials of a name, or an icon standing for either.

The avatar draws its `initials`, or its `icon` where it has none, on its `tone`. With neither it is the plain shape in its tone. A picture is drawn over them, so the initials show while it loads and where it fails, and are covered once it is there. A picture with parts that can be seen through shows what is under them: give such a picture alone, without initials or an icon.

Pantrix loads no pictures. `image` is a slot, so an app draws one with whatever it already uses: an image loader, a `PantrixImage` of a resource, a canvas of its own. The slot is as large as the avatar and cut to its shape. A picture that is not square is fitted by its own rule, so ask for `ContentScale.Crop`.

Initials are drawn as they are written. They are not put in upper case: `i` becomes `İ` in Turkish and `I` everywhere else, and an avatar is not the place to get a name wrong. Pass what should be drawn. Two letters of it are kept, without the spaces between them. How a name is shortened is the app's to say, and its language's.

The initials and the icon are a share of the avatar, so one of any size keeps its proportions, whether the size is given as `size` or by `modifier`. The initials keep that share at every font scale: an avatar does not grow with the text around it, and letters that grew would leave it.

With a `contentDescription` the avatar is announced as an image by that name. Without one it is hidden from screen readers, which is right beside a name they already read. The initials are never read out: they are what the description shortens. An avatar is drawn and not pressed. One that opens a profile goes inside what takes the press, a button or a list's row.

Parameters:

- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the avatar, usually the name it stands for, or null to hide the avatar from it.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the avatar's modifier. A size given here goes over `size`.
- `initials: String?`: the letters to draw, usually one or two. More than two are cut, and none leaves the `icon`.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: what is drawn where there are no initials: a person, a group, a company.
- `tone: AvatarTone`: the colour under the initials or the icon, and theirs. A picture covers it.
- `colors: AvatarColors?`: this avatar's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.
- `style: AvatarStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `size: Dp`: the avatar's width and height: the style's unless given.
- `tagKey: String?`: the avatar's automation key: it is `Avatar_<tagKey>`, and is tagged only when given one.
- `image: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: a picture that fills the avatar, over the initials or the icon. What it says of itself is not read: the avatar's description stands for both.

Documented on: [Avatar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/avatar.md)

### AvatarStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.avatar.AvatarStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class AvatarStyle(
    public val size: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val initialsScale: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val iconScale: Float = Float.NaN
) : PantrixStyle<AvatarStyle>
```

`PantrixAvatar`'s geometry: how large it is, what its corners are, and how much of it the initials or the icon take.

An avatar is a circle on every platform, 40dp across on Android and iOS, as Material 3 has it beside a list's row, and 32dp on the desktop and the web, where a row is shorter. The initials are four tenths of it and the icon six: an icon fills its box less than a capital letter fills its line, and at these shares the two look alike.

The two shares are fractions of the avatar and not sizes of their own, so an avatar given a size, a large one at the top of a profile or a small one in a comment, keeps its proportions without a second style.

None of the four follows the density: an avatar is a row's identity, and a denser row does not make it smaller.

Parameters:

- `size: Dp`: The avatar's width and height.
- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The avatar's corners: the round end of the brand's shape scale, a circle, unless a brand or a theme asks for a step of it or a shape of its own.
- `initialsScale: Float`: The height the initials are set in, as a fraction of the avatar's shorter side.
- `iconScale: Float`: The icon's width and height, as a fraction of the avatar's shorter side.

Documented on: [Avatar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/avatar.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge

### BadgeTone

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.BadgeTone`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class BadgeTone
```

How a badge is coloured: one of the theme's colour roles, so a brand changes every badge at once.

A badge is filled in every tone, from the role's `color` and `onColor`. It is a mark a few millimetres across with no room to be subtle: on the role's pale `container` a number reads as a stray digit and not as a badge, and a dot has nothing on it to hold a contrast with at all.

Entries:

- `Primary`: The brand's colour: a count that is good news, or one to notice without alarm.
- `Info`: Something worth knowing: a count of items, a new entry.
- `Success`: Something that worked or is well: a finished job, someone who is online.
- `Warning`: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.
- `Danger`: Something that needs attention: unread messages, failures. The default, as each platform's own badge is.
- `Neutral`: A count with no urgency at all.

Documented on: [Badge](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/badge.md)

### BadgeOverlap

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.BadgeOverlap`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class BadgeOverlap
```

How a badge lies on what it is the badge of, in a `PantrixBadgedBox`.

Entries:

- `Rectangular`: On the box around it: its corner or its edge. For an icon, a label, a picture with corners. The default.
- `Circular`: On the circle inside that box. For a round avatar, whose own edge is well inside the corners of its box: a badge on the corner would hang beside it and not on it.

Documented on: [Badge](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/badge.md)

### PantrixBadge

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.PantrixBadge`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixBadge(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    count: Int? = null,
    maxCount: Int = 99,
    tone: BadgeTone = BadgeTone.Danger,
    colors: BadgeColors? = null,
    style: BadgeStyle? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A count or a status dot, usually put on another element with `PantrixBadgedBox`.

Without a `count` the badge is a dot. With one it is a pill that grows with its number, and a circle around one digit. Above `maxCount` it reads that number and a plus, `99+` by default, and stops growing. Zero is drawn as `0`: taking a badge away when there is nothing to count is the caller's to do. A count below zero is drawn as `0` too: a number a server got wrong is no reason to bring an app down.

The number is set in the theme's caption type and grows with the font scale, and the pill with it. It is always at least as wide as it is tall.

Without a `contentDescription` the badge is hidden from screen readers. A lone "3" read out after an icon says nothing, so what the badge sits on should say it, "Inbox, 3 unread", and a badge says something of its own only where it stands alone. A badge is not pressed, and has no touch target.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the badge's modifier.
- `count: Int?`: the number to show, or null for a dot.
- `maxCount: Int`: the largest number that is written out. It has to be positive.
- `tone: BadgeTone`: the colour role the badge is filled from.
- `colors: BadgeColors?`: this badge's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.
- `style: BadgeStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the badge, or null to hide the badge from it.
- `tagKey: String?`: the badge's automation key: it is `Badge_<tagKey>`, and is tagged only when given one.

Documented on: [Badge](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/badge.md)

### PantrixBadgedBox

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.PantrixBadgedBox`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixBadgedBox(
    badge: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    alignment: Alignment = Alignment.TopEnd,
    overlap: BadgeOverlap = BadgeOverlap.Rectangular,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)
```

Puts `badge` on `content`, with its middle on a corner of it, and takes no room for it.

The box is as large as `content`. The badge hangs over its edge and pushes nothing aside, so a badge that comes and goes moves nothing around it. A parent that clips cuts what hangs over. The badge is as large as its number, whatever it sits on, and a baseline of `content` is the box's, so a badged label lines up with the text beside it. A badge wider than it is tall has its round end on the corner and grows away from the content, as the badge of a tab does on each platform: three digits cover no more of an icon than one.

`alignment` says which corner, or which edge: the top corner where lines end by default, which is the top left in a right-to-left layout. `overlap` says what the corners are corners of. Put the box around the icon itself: the corner of something larger, such as a button with its touch target, is far from what is drawn.

Parameters:

- `badge: @Composable () -> Unit`: what is put on the content: usually a `PantrixBadge`. Nothing, where there is nothing to show.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the box's modifier.
- `alignment: Alignment`: where on `content` the middle of the badge is.
- `overlap: BadgeOverlap`: whether that is on the box around `content`, or on the circle in it.
- `content: @Composable () -> Unit`: what the badge belongs to.

Documented on: [Badge](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/badge.md)

### BadgeStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.BadgeStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class BadgeStyle(
    public val dotSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val minWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<BadgeStyle>
```

`PantrixBadge`'s geometry: a dot where there is nothing to count, and otherwise a pill that grows with its number.

The pill is 16dp tall and the dot 6dp across, as Material 3 has its large and its small badge, and a little larger on iOS, after the badge of its tab bar. The pill is as wide as it is tall at the least on every platform, so one digit sits in a circle.

The pill's height, its least width and its padding follow the density, since they are the room around the number. The dot does not: it is a mark, and a mark that shrank with a denser screen would be harder to see where there is more to look at.

Parameters:

- `dotSize: Dp`: The dot's width and height.
- `height: Dp`: The pill's height. A number set larger than it has room for, at a large font scale, makes the pill taller.
- `minWidth: Dp`: The pill's least width. The pill is never narrower than it is tall, whatever this says.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room on each side of the number, which is what makes the pill wider than it is tall as the number grows.

Documented on: [Badge](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/badge.md)
