## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.button

### PantrixButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixButton(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Solid,
    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    loading: Boolean = false,
    fullWidth: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ButtonStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(key = ButtonStyle, override = style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: ButtonColors = variant.colors(),
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    form: FormState? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A button with a text label, the form most buttons take.

`variant` picks the colours and `size` the height, padding and label type. `style` overrides the theme's `ButtonStyle` for this button alone: its shape, pressed scale and per-size geometry. The height is the least the button is tall: where a reader's larger type makes the label taller than that, the button grows with it. A pointer over the button lays a light cover of its content colour on it, and a press a stronger one, so that a mouse shows what a click would press.

`loading` shows a spinner in place of `leadingIcon` and stops clicks, as a submitting `form` does. Given a `form`, a click validates it first: while a field is invalid, `onClick` is not called, and that field takes focus with an error haptic.

`contentDescription` is read in place of `text`, and not after it: give one only where the label alone does not say what the button does, as a "+" does not.

Parameters:

- `text: String`
- `onClick: () -> Unit`
- `modifier: Modifier`: the button's modifier.
- `variant: ButtonVariant`
- `size: ButtonSize`
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the button can be pressed: one that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and does nothing.
- `loading: Boolean`
- `fullWidth: Boolean`: true stretches the button across the width it is given, its content in the middle.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the label: an arrow, or a count.
- `style: ButtonStyle?`
- `shape: Shape`: the button's corners: by default the resolved style's. Given here, it wins over `style`'s.
- `colors: ButtonColors`: this call's own colours, in place of `variant`'s.
- `contentDescription: String?`
- `form: FormState?`
- `tagKey: String?`: the button's automation key: the button is `Button_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the button's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

Documented on: [Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/button.md)

### PantrixButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixButton(
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    contentDescription: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,

    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
```

Slot form, for content a string cannot express.

`contentDescription` is required here rather than optional, because without the text parameter there is nothing left for a screen reader to fall back on. It is all a screen reader hears of the button: what is in `content` is drawn, and not read after it. `style` is the text form's.

Parameters:

- `onClick: () -> Unit`: what a press does. Given a `form`, it is called once the form is valid.
- `contentDescription: String`

- `size: ButtonSize`: the button's height, its padding and the type its label is set in.

- `loading: Boolean`: whether the button takes no press while what it began is under way, and tells a screen reader it is loading. What `content` shows meanwhile is the caller's.
- `fullWidth: Boolean`: true stretches the button across the width it is given, its content in the middle.
- `style: ButtonStyle?`
- `shape: Shape`: the button's corners: by default the resolved style's. Given here, it wins over `style`'s.
- `colors: ButtonColors`: this call's own colours, in place of `variant`'s.
- `form: FormState?`: the form the button submits: a press validates it first, and the button takes no press while it is submitting.
- `tagKey: String?`: the button's automation key: the button is `Button_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the button's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `content: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit`

### ButtonVariant

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ButtonVariant
```

How prominent a button is.

Four of them are a ladder rather than a menu, each one quieter than the one above it: `Solid` is filled in the role's colour, `Soft` in the role's pale container, `Outline` has no fill and an edge, and `Text` has neither. Reading them in that order, which is not the order they are declared in, is how to pick one: go down until the button stops competing with what is around it.

`Subtle` stands on `Soft`'s rung: the same pale fill, with a faint edge in its content colour that keeps the button's shape where the fill alone barely parts from the background.

`Destructive` is not a rung. It says what the button *does*, which is why it is the only variant that changes the colour role, and why it sits at the bottom out of the ladder's reach.

Entries:

- `Solid`: The one primary action on a screen. The default.
- `Outline`: Secondary on a busy surface, where a filled shape would compete.
- `Soft`: Secondary, still clearly a button: a pale fill in the role's container colour.
- `Subtle`: `Soft` with a faint edge, so the shape still shows where the pale fill alone would fade into what is around it.
- `Text`: Tertiary: toolbar actions, "cancel". No surface at all.
- `Destructive`: Destructive and irreversible. Never the only action in a dialog.

Documented on: [Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/button.md), [Icon Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/icon-button.md), [Button Group](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/button-group.md)

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonSize`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ButtonSize
```

Five heights, stepping by 8dp from 24 to 56.

`Medium` is the default and the one to reach for. The two ends are for the places a default would be wrong rather than for a general sense of scale: `ExtraSmall` inside a dense table row or beside a field, `ExtraLarge` as the single action a phone screen is built around.

Entries:

- `ExtraSmall`: 24dp tall: inside a dense table row, or beside a field.
- `Small`: 32dp tall.
- `Medium`: 40dp tall: the default, and the one to reach for.
- `Large`: 48dp tall.
- `ExtraLarge`: 56dp tall: the single action a phone screen is built around.

### PantrixColor.buttonColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.buttonColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
fun PantrixColor.buttonColors(variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Solid): ButtonColors
```

The same prominences, drawn from any role instead of from `primary`.

`ButtonVariant.Destructive.colors()` stays the way to say "this deletes something", and it keeps its own meaning: a variant is what the button *is*. This is only what it is *painted with*, for a button that carries a status — "Mark as paid" in `success`, "Retry" in `warning` — so `ButtonVariant.Destructive` here paints exactly like `ButtonVariant.Solid` rather than quietly ignoring the role it was handed.

`ButtonVariant.Subtle` is `ButtonVariant.Soft` with an edge here too, and the edge is all that tells the two apart. It is drawn in the role's own colour at full strength, where the default draws `primary.onContainer` at 30%.

```kotlin
PantrixButton(
    text = stringResource(Res.string.mark_paid),
    onClick = onMarkPaid,
    colors = PantrixTheme.colors.success.buttonColors(),
    tagKey = "mark_paid"
)
```

Parameters:

- `variant: ButtonVariant`: the prominence the colours are for: `ButtonVariant.Solid` unless told.

The sizes are the same on every platform; the shape and the press scale are not.

### PantrixButtonGroup

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.buttongroup.PantrixButtonGroup`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixButtonGroup(
    buttons: List<GroupButton>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Horizontal,
    attached: Boolean = true,
    equalWidth: Boolean = false,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: ButtonGroupStyle? = null,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.style(ButtonGroupStyle, style).shape.toShape(),
    colors: ButtonColors = variant.colors(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A group of buttons: a few actions of the same rank, drawn as one control or set apart at one distance.

Attached, which it is unless told otherwise, the buttons touch: the group has one shape, of which each button keeps the corners at its own end, one edge around it where its colours have one, and a line between each two buttons. Apart, they are the same buttons a gap from each other, each with its own shape and edge, as the actions under a dialog are.

Each button is a button like any other: it is one stop for Tab, says its own name and role to a screen reader, shows its own focus ring, and reports its own press, as a `Button` or an `IconButton` event. The group reports nothing and chooses nothing: no button stays selected. For a choice of one among several, where one stays chosen, use a segment button, which says which one is.

In a row the buttons are as wide as what they say. In a room too narrow for that the short ones stay whole and the long ones share what is left; with `equalWidth` they all share the width the group is given. In a column they are all as wide as the widest of them.

An attached group keeps the platform's touch target around itself, and each of its buttons is at least as long as that along the group: beside its neighbours, a button has no room of its own to be reached in.

Parameters:

- `buttons: List<GroupButton>`: the buttons, in order. An empty list draws nothing.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the group's modifier, outside the touch target an attached group reserves.
- `variant: ButtonVariant`: the variant of every button that has none of its own.
- `size: ButtonSize`: the size of every button, so that they line up.
- `orientation: Orientation`: `Orientation.Horizontal` for a row, `Orientation.Vertical` for a column of actions.
- `attached: Boolean`: true draws the buttons as one control. False sets them the style's gap apart.
- `equalWidth: Boolean`: true gives every button of a row the same share of the width the group is given; in a room without an end, the width of the widest. A column's buttons are as wide as each other whatever this says.
- `enabled: Boolean`: false disables every button.
- `style: ButtonGroupStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform. The buttons keep the button's own style for their sizes.
- `shape: Shape`: the group's shape: attached, the shape of the whole group; apart, of each button.
- `colors: ButtonColors`: what the buttons are painted with, each one that has neither colours nor a variant of its own. Attached, the border's colour is the group's one edge, and the colour of the lines between the buttons.
- `tagKey: String?`: the group's automation key: the group is `ButtonGroup_<tagKey>`, and its buttons are named inside it, `ButtonGroup_<tagKey>.Button_<key>`, so that two groups with the same actions are told apart.

Documented on: [Button Group](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/button-group.md)

### ButtonGroupStyle

```kotlin

    public val dividerWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
```

`PantrixButtonGroup`'s geometry: the shape of the group, the line between two buttons that are attached, and the room between two that are not.

The shape is the button's own on every platform, so that a group and a button beside it have the same corners: a pill on Android, on desktop and on the web, a rounded rectangle on iOS. Attached, it is the shape of the whole group, and each button keeps the corners at its own end of it. Apart, every button has it whole.

Only the gap follows the density, since it is the room between the buttons. The line and the shape do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The group's shape: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `dividerWidth: Dp`: The width of the line between two attached buttons.
- `gap: Dp`: The room between two buttons that are not attached.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox

### PantrixCheckbox

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox.PantrixCheckbox`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCheckbox(
    checked: Boolean,
    onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: CheckboxStyle? = null,
    colors: CheckboxColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
```

A checkbox: a box that is checked or not, and the label it is the box of.

The box, the label and the supporting text are one target. A press anywhere on them toggles the box, since on a phone the words are most of what a finger can hit, and a screen reader hears one checkbox, named by its label, that says whether it is checked. The box stands on the label's first line, however many lines the label and the supporting text run to. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the box is.

Without `onCheckedChange` the checkbox is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and still says its name and its state. `error` turns the box and the supporting text to the danger role and is announced. Checking and unchecking draw the tick on and off while the fill fades in and out: at once under reduced motion.

Parameters:

- `checked: Boolean`: whether the box is checked.
- `onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?`: called with the value the user asks for, the opposite of `checked`. The checkbox changes nothing by itself: it is checked when `checked` says so. Null makes it read-only.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the checkbox can be toggled. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `label: String?`: the text beside the box: part of the target, and the checkbox's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the label, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the value is wrong: the box and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.
- `style: CheckboxStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: CheckboxColors?`: this checkbox's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled box and one in error keep the theme's.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the checkbox: its name where it has no `label`, as in a table's row, or in place of the label.
- `tagKey: String?`: the checkbox's automation key: the row is `Checkbox_<tagKey>`. A toggle is reported as a `Checkbox` event that carries the state the box had, and never its label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the checkbox's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where the box stands: before the label, as a list of choices has it, or after it. After it, the box is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the box leaves.

Documented on: [Checkbox](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/checkbox.md)

### PantrixCheckbox

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox.PantrixCheckbox`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCheckbox(
    field: FormField<Boolean>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    style: CheckboxStyle? = null,
    colors: CheckboxColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
```

A checkbox bound to a form's field: its value, its error and its name come from `field`.

A toggle changes the field and marks it touched, so a rule's message shows after the first toggle, or when the form is submitted, and not on a form nobody has touched. While the field is in error the message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the checkbox's automation key, `Checkbox_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a value and a field cannot both be given.

Parameters:

- `field: FormField<Boolean>`: the field the checkbox shows and changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the checkbox can be toggled.
- `label: String?`: the text beside the box: part of the target, and the checkbox's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the label, while the field has no error to show there.
- `style: CheckboxStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: CheckboxColors?`: this checkbox's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled box and one in error keep the theme's.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the checkbox where it has no `label`, or in place of it.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where the box stands: before the label, as a list of choices has it, or after it. After it, the box is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the box leaves.

### CheckboxStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox.CheckboxStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class CheckboxStyle(
    public val size: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val strokeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
```

`PantrixCheckbox`'s box: its size, its corners and its edge.

The box is a square with the small step of the shape scale for its corners, 4dp by default, on every platform. It is 18dp, as Material 3 has it, and 22dp on iOS. iOS has no checkbox of its own, and its box is not round there either: a circle is a radio button, and an empty one would say that only one of the boxes can be chosen.

None of the three follows the density: a box, its corners and its edge are not air. The space between the box and its label does, since it comes from the theme's spacing. A checkbox's colours are not part of its style: they come from its state, and from `CheckboxColors` where a checkbox has its own.

Parameters:

- `size: Dp`: The box's width and height, its edge included.
- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The box's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, so a brand with square corners has square boxes.
- `strokeWidth: Dp`: How thick the box's edge is, and the tick's and the dash's line.

### CheckboxColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.checkbox.CheckboxColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class CheckboxColors(
    public val checked: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val checkmark: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val border: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What `PantrixCheckbox` is painted with, for a checkbox that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role. A product gives the colours it changes and no others:

```kotlin
PantrixCheckbox(
    checked = accepted,
    onCheckedChange = { accepted = it },
    label = stringResource(Res.string.accept_terms),
    colors = CheckboxColors(checked = brand, checkmark = onBrand)
)
```

They are the colours of a checkbox that can be toggled and is not in error. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled roles and one in error in its danger role, whatever is given here, so that both look the same across a product.

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `checked: Color`: The box's fill when it is checked or indeterminate. The theme's `primary`.
- `checkmark: Color`: The tick and the dash on the fill: the colour that reads on `checked`. The primary role's `onColor`.
- `border: Color`: The box's edge when it is not checked. The theme's `borderStrong`: an empty box is nothing but its edge.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.chip

### PantrixChip

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.chip.PantrixChip`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixChip(
    label: String,
    onClick: (() -> Unit)?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    leadingIcon: ImageVector? = null,
    onRemove: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: ChipStyle? = null,
    colors: ChipColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A chip: a compact action, or an item the user put in and can take out again, such as a recipient, a tag or an applied filter.

It is as tall as its style says and as wide as its icon, its label and its remove button need, with the platform's touch target reserved around it. A label too long for the room the chip is given ends in an ellipsis, and the remove button stays whole beside it. A label set larger than the chip, at a large font scale, makes the chip taller. In a chip made wider than it needs, the icon and the label are in the middle, as a button's are, and the remove button is at the end.

With `onClick` the chip is a button, named by its label. Without, it only shows a value: one item for a screen reader, which takes no press and no focus, and keeps its remove button when `onRemove` is given.

`onRemove` puts a remove button at the chip's end: a target of its own, as tall as the chip, that a screen reader hears with the label, "Remove Kotlin", so that the buttons of a row can be told apart. The chip does not take itself out: the callback does.

Parameters:

- `label: String`: the chip's text, and its name for a screen reader.
- `onClick: (() -> Unit)?`: called when the chip is pressed. Null makes a chip that only shows a value.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the chip's modifier, outside the touch target it reserves.
- `leadingIcon: ImageVector?`: an icon before the label, in the style's icon size.
- `onRemove: (() -> Unit)?`: called when the remove button is pressed. Null leaves the button out.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the chip and its remove button can be pressed. A chip that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `style: ChipStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: ChipColors?`: this chip's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled chip keeps the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the chip's automation key: the chip is `Chip_<tagKey>` and its remove button `ChipRemove_<tagKey>`. A press is reported as a `Chip` event, `click` or `remove`, which never carries the label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the chip's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null, and the remove button always has its own.

Documented on: [Chip](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/chip.md)

A filter: a chip that is on or off.

Selected, it is filled in the primary role's container and shows a tick in place of `leadingIcon`. The tick, and not the fill alone, says it is on, for whoever cannot tell the two colours apart. A screen reader hears a checkbox that is selected or not. A change is felt, as a switch's is.

Without `onSelectedChange` the filter is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and still says its name and whether it is on.

- `label: String`: the chip's text, and its name for a screen reader.
- `selected: Boolean`: whether the filter is on.
- `onSelectedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?`: called with the value the user asks for, the opposite of `selected`. The chip changes nothing by itself: it is on when `selected` says so. Null makes it read-only.

- `leadingIcon: ImageVector?`: an icon before the label, in the style's icon size. A selected chip shows a tick in its place.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the chip can be pressed. A chip that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `style: ChipStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: ChipColors?`: this chip's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled chip keeps the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the chip's automation key: the chip is `Chip_<tagKey>`. A change is reported as a `Chip` event, `toggle`, which carries the value asked for and never the label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the chip's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

### ChipStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.chip.ChipStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChipStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val borderWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ChipStyle>
```

`PantrixChip`'s geometry.

An icon stands nearer the chip's edge than text does: on a side that has one, `iconPadding` is the room to the edge in place of `horizontalPadding`. It is Material 3's rule, kept on every platform.

On Android the numbers are Material 3's: 32dp tall with corners of 8dp, the medium step of the shape scale. iOS has no chip of its own; it takes the height of a small button, so the two line up in a row, and the pill a Pantrix control has. Desktop and the web are a step tighter, for a pointer.

An icon goes by the buttons': a small button's 20dp on Android and on iOS, where the chip is as tall as one, and 18dp in the chip of 30dp that the desktop and the web have. On every platform that is the largest the chip has room for: the remove button's focus ring goes around the cross, inside the chip, and in high contrast it reaches 6dp past it.

The height and the two paddings follow the density, since they are the room around the label. The icon's size, the edge's width and the shape do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The chip's shape: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `height: Dp`: The chip's height. A label set larger than it has room for, at a large font scale, makes the chip taller.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the label and the chip's edge, on a side that has no icon.
- `iconPadding: Dp`: The room between an icon and the chip's edge, and between an icon and the label.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.filedrop

### PantrixFileDrop

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.filedrop.PantrixFileDrop`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFileDrop(
    onFiles: (List<PantrixFile>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    accept: List<PantrixFileType> = listOf(PantrixFileType.Any),
    multiple: Boolean = false,
    maxSize: Long? = null,
    onRejected: (List<RejectedFile>) -> Unit = {},
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    error: Boolean = false,
    picker: FilePicker = rememberFilePicker(),
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    style: FileDropStyle? = null,
    colors: FileDropColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Somewhere to give the app a file: a zone with a dashed edge that opens the platform's picker when it is pressed, and takes the files dropped on it from the platform's files, another app or another window.

The press is the way in on every platform, and the only one where nothing is dragged in: a phone, a keyboard, a screen reader. The zone says so in its words, which put the drop first under a pointer, on the desktop and the web, and the picker first on a phone. Where only pictures are taken (`PantrixFileType.Images`), Android and iOS open their photo picker.

What is chosen or dropped is screened before the app is handed it: a file of a kind not in `accept`, one larger than `maxSize`, and, where only one is taken, every one after the first go to `onRejected` with the reason, and the rest to `onFiles`. The zone keeps nothing: what was taken is the app's to list, with `PantrixFileItem`s under the zone, and what was not is the app's to say, in `supportingText` with `error`. A screen reader is told politely how many files the zone took and how many it did not.

Nothing is read here: a `PantrixFile` reads its bytes when the app asks it to, which a large file should be read for off the screen's work, and sent where it goes as it is read.

```kotlin
PantrixFileDrop(
    onFiles = { files -> attachments += files },
    accept = listOf(PantrixFileType.Pdf),
    multiple = true,
    maxSize = 10_000_000,
    onRejected = { refused = it },
    supportingText = stringResource(Res.string.pdf_up_to_10_mb),
    tagKey = "attachments"
)
```

Parameters:

- `onFiles: (List<PantrixFile>) -> Unit`: handed the files the zone took, at least one, in the order they came.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the zone's modifier, with its supporting text. The zone fills the width it is given.
- `accept: List<PantrixFileType>`: the kinds of file the zone takes. The picker shows only these, where the platform's can filter.
- `multiple: Boolean`: whether the zone takes more than one file at a time.
- `maxSize: Long?`: the most bytes a file the zone takes may have, or null for any size.
- `onRejected: (List<RejectedFile>) -> Unit`: handed the files the zone did not take, each with why, at least one.
- `label: String?`: what the zone says first, in place of the platform's words.
- `supportingText: String?`: a line under the zone: what it takes and how large, or what was wrong.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the zone takes anything: a press or a drop. A zone that does not is drawn faint.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the zone shows that what it was given was not right: its edge and its supporting text in the danger colour. A screen reader hears the supporting text as the error.
- `picker: FilePicker`: what a press opens: the platform's own picker, or a test's.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the zone's interactions: its press, its hover and its focus.
- `style: FileDropStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FileDropColors?`: this zone's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the zone's automation key: it is `FileDrop_<tagKey>`.

Documented on: [File Drop](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/file-drop.md)

### FileDropStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.filedrop.FileDropStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class FileDropStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val minHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val padding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val borderWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val dashLength: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val dashGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<FileDropStyle>
```

`PantrixFileDrop`'s geometry: the zone, its dashed edge and what stands in it.

No platform has a drop zone of its own. The zone is tall enough to be a target from across a screen, taller on a phone, where a thumb presses it, than under a pointer; its corners are a card's, and its edge is dashed: a solid edge reads as a card, a dashed one as a place to put something.

The least height, the room inside, the gaps and the dashes' gaps follow the density. The edge's width, the dashes' length, the corners and the icon do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The zone's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `minHeight: Dp`: The least height of the zone. A larger type makes it taller.
- `padding: Dp`: The room between the zone's edge and what stands in it.
- `borderWidth: Dp`: The width of the dashed edge.
- `dashLength: Dp`: The length of each of the edge's dashes.
- `dashGap: Dp`: The room between two dashes.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The width and height of the icon over the zone's words.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the icon and the words, and between the two lines of words.

### PantrixFileItem

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.filedrop.PantrixFileItem`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFileItem(
    name: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    size: Long? = null,
    onRemove: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    progress: Float? = null,
    error: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector = PantrixIcons.File,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: FileItemStyle? = null,
```

A file the app took, in a row: its icon, its name, its size or what went wrong with it, how far it is sent, and the button that takes it away. The rows stand under a `PantrixFileDrop`, each for a file the app keeps.

A long name is cut in its middle, so that its start and its extension both show: `Quarterly rep….pdf`. The size is written as the language writes one, `1,2 MB` in Turkish; an `error` stands in its place, in the danger colour, and the row's edge turns that colour too. A `progress` draws a bar under the words, filled from the start of the reading direction, and a screen reader hears it as one.

A screen reader hears the row as one thing, its name and its size or error, and the button apart from it, named for what it removes: `Remove report.pdf`.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.form

### FormField

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.FormField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class FormField<T>
```

One field in a form: its value, its rules, and whether it is currently in error.

`id` doubles as the component's automation tag, so a form-bound component needs no `tagKey` — the field already carries a stable, locale-independent name.

`@Stable` for the same reason as `FormState`: `value`, `error` and `touched` are snapshot state, and `isAttached` is bookkeeping that composition never reads.

Parameters:

- `id: String`: The field's name in its form, and the automation tag of the component bound to it.

Members:

- `value: T`: What the field holds now: its first value until the user gives another, and that value again after a reset.
- `error: String?`: The message to show, or null.

  Stays null until the field has been `touched` or the form has been submitted. Showing "Required" the instant a form opens tells the user they have done something wrong before they have done anything at all.
- `touched: Boolean`: True once the user has interacted with this field.
- `focusRequester: FocusRequester`: What the field is focused by: the component bound to it attaches it, and a submit that finds the field in error moves the focus there.
- `fun onValueChange(newValue: T)`: Called by components on change. Re-validates only once the field has been touched.

  `newValue`: the value the user has given the field.
- `fun onFocusLost()`: Called by components on blur. Marks touched and validates, which is the usual moment to show an error.
- `fun validate(): Boolean`: Runs every rule and publishes the first failure. Returns true when the field is valid.
- `fun isValid(): Boolean`: Whether the field would pass, without publishing an error the user has not earned yet.
- `fun reset(newValue: T)`: Puts the field back as it was before the user touched it: `newValue` as its value, and no error.

Documented on: [Form](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/form.md)

### FormState

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.FormState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class FormState
```

A form's fields and its submission lifecycle.

Holds three things components would otherwise each reinvent, differently: which field to focus when validation fails, whether a submission is in flight, and what Enter does.

`@Stable` is a claim the compiler cannot prove but the class honours: everything a composable reads is snapshot state, and the one plain field — the submit handler — is never read during composition. Without it the compiler reports the class unstable, and the compiler-metrics gate rejects every component that takes a `form`.

Members:

- `fields: List<FormField<*>>`: The form's fields, in the order they were declared: the first one in error takes the focus on a submit.
- `isSubmitting: Boolean`: True while `submit` is running.

  `PantrixButton(form = ...)` reads this for its loading state, so a form cannot be submitted twice by an impatient second tap — the disabled state comes from the same source of truth as the spinner rather than from a separate flag someone has to remember to set.
- `isValid: Boolean`: Whether every field currently passes, without marking anything touched.
- `fun validateAll(): Boolean`: Validates everything and marks every field touched, so errors become visible.

  Touching on submit is what makes "press submit on an empty form" show all the errors at once rather than one per attempt.
- `fun focusFirstError(): Boolean`: Moves focus to the first field in error. Returns false when there is nothing to focus.

  Scrolling a long form to the problem is the difference between a fixable error and a user staring at a submit button that does nothing. Skips fields whose component is not currently composed — requesting focus on a detached FocusRequester throws.
- `suspend fun submit(block: suspend () -> Unit)`: Validates, then runs `block` if everything passed.

  Owns `isSubmitting` around the call so the flag cannot be left stuck on by an early return or an exception — the single most common bug in hand-written form submission.
- `fun reset()`: Starts the form over. Every field on screen goes back to its initial value, untouched and without an error, and is still validated. Fields that have left the screen are forgotten; one that comes back registers again.
- `fun requestSubmit()`: Invoked when a field reports that Enter was pressed.

Documented on: [Form](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/form.md)

### FormState.field

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.field`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin

    id: String,
```

Declares a field.

Remembered by `id`, so the value survives recomposition but a genuinely different field — a different row of a dynamic list — gets its own state.

Parameters:

### Rule

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rule`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
fun interface Rule<in T>
```

A validation rule. Returns the error message, or null when the value is acceptable.

Rules carry their own message rather than an error code because the message has to be translated by whoever wrote the form — the library cannot know that a field called `code` wants "Enter the 6-digit code" rather than "Invalid input".

Members:

- `fun check(value: T): String?`: The error message for `value`, or null when `value` is acceptable.

Documented on: [Form](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/form.md)

### Rules

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rules`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
object Rules
```

The rules that come up in nearly every form.

Members:

- `fun notBlank(message: String): Rule<String>`: For non-null text. Rejects whitespace-only input, which `isEmpty` would let through.

  `message`: what the field says while its text is blank.
- `fun <T : Any> required(message: String): Rule<T?>`: For nullable values — a select with nothing chosen, an unset date.

  `message`: what the field says while nothing is chosen.
- `fun mustBeTrue(message: String): Rule<Boolean>`: Consent checkboxes: "accept the terms" is not satisfied by merely having a value.

  `message`: what the field says while it is not ticked.
- `fun minLength(length: Int, message: String): Rule<String>`: At least `length` characters, not counting leading and trailing whitespace.

  `message`: what the field says while its text is shorter than `length`.
- `fun maxLength(length: Int, message: String): Rule<String>`: At most `length` characters, whitespace included.

  `message`: what the field says while its text is longer than `length`.
- `fun matches(pattern: Regex, message: String): Rule<String>`: The whole value matches `pattern`; matching part of it is not enough.

  `message`: what the field says while its text does not match `pattern`.
- `fun <T> satisfies(message: String, predicate: (T) -> Boolean): Rule<T>`: Escape hatch for rules that depend on something outside the field — a password confirmation, a date range, a server-side uniqueness check already performed.

  `message`: what the field says while `predicate` does not accept its value.

  `predicate`: whether a value is accepted.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.iconbutton

### PantrixIconButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.iconbutton.PantrixIconButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixIconButton(
    imageVector: ImageVector,
    contentDescription: String?,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: ButtonVariant = ButtonVariant.Text,
    size: ButtonSize = ButtonSize.Medium,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    shape: Shape = PantrixTheme.shapes.full,
    colors: ButtonColors = variant.colors(),
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    style: ButtonStyle? = null
)
```

A button that shows only an icon: square, as tall as a `size` button, round by default, with the platform's minimum touch target around it. `variant` picks its colours; `ButtonVariant.Text`, the default, has no container, disabled or not. `contentDescription` names the action for screen readers, "Close" rather than "X". A pointer over the button lays a light cover of its icon's colour on it, and a press a stronger one.

Pass null only for a button that repeats what something a screen reader and the keyboard already reach does: an arrow at the end of a row that is pressed as a whole. Such a button is hidden from screen readers, and is no stop for the keyboard either, since focus would land on something that is never announced; a pointer still presses it. A button that is the only way to its action always has a description.

Parameters:

- `imageVector: ImageVector`: the icon the button shows.
- `contentDescription: String?`
- `onClick: () -> Unit`: what a press does.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the button's modifier.
- `variant: ButtonVariant`
- `size: ButtonSize`
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the button can be pressed: one that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and does nothing.
- `shape: Shape`: the button's corners: fully round unless told.
- `colors: ButtonColors`: this call's own colours, in place of `variant`'s.
- `tagKey: String?`: the button's automation key: the button is `IconButton_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the button's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `style: ButtonStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change.

Documented on: [Icon Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/icon-button.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.link

### PantrixLink

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.link.PantrixLink`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixLink(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    style: TextStyle = LocalPantrixTextStyle.current,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    underline: LinkUnderline = LinkUnderline.Always
)
```

A link on its own that runs `onClick`: `text` underlined in the primary colour, in a row as tall as the platform's minimum touch target, so that a touch above or under the text reaches it. The click is reported to the theme's analytics as a `Link` `click` event. When it is not `enabled`, it keeps its underline, in the disabled text colour, so that it still reads as a link, and does nothing.

`color` is the link's own colour where it is not the theme's `primary`: its text, and the tint under a pointer and a press. A disabled link keeps the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given. `style` is the base text unless given, `LocalPantrixTextStyle`, the type a `PantrixText` has by itself: a link beside a text is as large as the text.

Parameters:

- `text: String`
- `onClick: () -> Unit`
- `modifier: Modifier`: the link's modifier.
- `style: TextStyle`
- `color: Color`
- `enabled: Boolean`
- `tagKey: String?`: the link's automation key: the link is `Link_<tagKey>`, and without one a key of where it is called. Visible text is never the key.
- `underline: LinkUnderline`: when the link is underlined: always unless told; `OnHover` for a link that stands apart from any sentence, underlined under a pointer and the keyboard's focus, and always where the platform is used by touch.

Documented on: [Link](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/link.md)

### LinkUnderline

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.link.LinkUnderline`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class LinkUnderline
```

When a link is underlined: what tells it from the text around it besides its colour.

A link inside a sentence is underlined always: told apart by colour alone, it is lost on whoever cannot tell the two colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1). A link that stands apart, in a row of links or a breadcrumb's trail, is told apart by where it is, and may be underlined only under a pointer or the keyboard's focus. Where the platform is used by touch there is neither to show it, and it is underlined always.

Entries:

- `Always`: Underlined always: the default, and what a link in a sentence needs.
- `OnHover`: Underlined under a pointer and while it holds the keyboard's focus, and always where the platform is used by touch: for a link that stands apart from any sentence.

Documented on: [Link](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/link.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton

### PantrixRadioButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixRadioButton(
    selected: Boolean,
    onClick: (() -> Unit)?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: RadioStyle? = null,
    colors: RadioColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
```

A radio button: a ring that is selected or not, and the label it is the ring of. One of several, of which one is chosen.

It is almost always used through `PantrixRadioGroup`, which lays the options out, moves the selection with the arrow keys and binds it to a form's field. On its own it is for options in a layout a group cannot make, such as a card for each: wrap them in `Modifier.selectableGroup()`, so that a screen reader hears them as one choice.

The ring, the label and the supporting text are one target. A press anywhere on them asks for the option, since on a phone the words are most of what a finger can hit, and a screen reader hears one radio button, named by its label, that says whether it is selected. The ring stands on the label's first line, however many lines the label and the supporting text run to. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the ring is.

Without `onClick` the radio button is read-only: it takes no press and no focus, and still says its name and whether it is selected. `error` turns the ring and the supporting text to the danger role and is announced. Selecting grows the dot and turns the ring to the primary role's colour together, and unselecting takes both back: at once under reduced motion.

Parameters:

- `selected: Boolean`: whether this is the option chosen.
- `onClick: (() -> Unit)?`: called when the user presses the radio button, selected already or not. The radio button changes nothing by itself: it is selected when `selected` says so. Null makes it read-only.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the radio button can be selected. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `label: String?`: the text beside the ring: part of the target, and the radio button's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the label, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the choice is wrong or missing: the ring and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.
- `style: RadioStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: RadioColors?`: this radio button's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled ring and one in error keep the theme's.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the radio button: its name where it has no `label`, as in a card that is the option, or in place of the label.
- `tagKey: String?`: the radio button's automation key: the row is `RadioButton_<tagKey>`. A press is reported as a `RadioButton` event, and never by its label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the radio button's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where the ring stands: before the label, as a list of choices has it, or after it. After it, the ring is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the ring leaves.

Documented on: [Radio Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/radio-button.md)

### RadioOption

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.RadioOption`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class RadioOption<out T>(
    public val value: T,
    public val label: String,
    public val supportingText: String? = null,
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
    public val tagKey: String? = null
)
```

One option of `PantrixRadioGroup`: the value it stands for, its label, and a key for automation.

Parameters:

- `value: T`: What the group gives to its `onSelect` when the option is chosen, and compares with its `selected` by `==`.
- `label: String`: The visible text, and the option's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: Written under the label in a smaller type, to say what the option is: a price, how long a delivery takes. It is part of the option's target and of what a screen reader says for it, and keeps its colour when the group is in error.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the option can be selected. A press does nothing on one that cannot, and the arrow keys skip it.
- `tagKey: String?`: The option's automation key, the same in every language: the option is `RadioButton_<tagKey>`, or `RadioButton_<index>` without one, inside the tag of a group that has a key: `RadioGroup_plan.RadioButton_pro`.

Documented on: [Radio Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/radio-button.md)

### PantrixRadioGroup

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioGroup`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixRadioGroup(
    options: List<RadioOption<T>>,
    selected: T?,
    onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Vertical,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    style: RadioStyle? = null,
    colors: RadioColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
```

A group of radio buttons: a choice of one among `options`, under a label, with help or an error's message below.

The options stand one under another, or side by side with `Orientation.Horizontal`: as many on a line as the width takes, and the rest on the next. Each is a `PantrixRadioButton`, with the ring on the first line of its label.

The group is one stop for Tab, on the selected option, as the radio group pattern of WAI-ARIA has it: the first option that can be selected, while none is. The arrow keys choose the next and the previous option, left and right the other way round in a right-to-left layout, wrapping around and skipping an option that is disabled. They choose and do not only move: while an option has the focus, the focus goes with the selection, whoever makes it, so that the option a screen reader is on is the one chosen. A press on an option takes the focus to it, where a press can.

For a screen reader each option is a radio button that says whether it is selected, in one group named by `label`. `error` is announced by the group, once, and turns every ring and the group's message to the danger role.

Parameters:

- `options: List<RadioOption<T>>`: the options, in order.
- `selected: T?`: the value of the selected option. Null, or a value no option has, selects none.
- `onSelect: (T) -> Unit`: called with the value of the option the user chose, by a press or by the keys. The group selects nothing by itself: an option is selected when `selected` says so. A press on the option that is selected asks again, and an arrow key only ever asks for another option.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the group's modifier.
- `orientation: Orientation`: `Orientation.Vertical` for one option under another, `Orientation.Horizontal` for side by side.
- `enabled: Boolean`: false disables every option, and writes the label and the supporting text in the disabled text colour.
- `label: String?`: what the choice is, written over the options: the group's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the options, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the choice is wrong or missing: the rings and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.
- `style: RadioStyle?`: this call's own style, the one every option is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: RadioColors?`: the colours every option is drawn in, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled option and a group in error keep the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the group's automation key: the group is `RadioGroup_<tagKey>`, and its options are named inside it, `RadioGroup_<tagKey>.RadioButton_<key>`, so that two groups with the same options are told apart. A choice is reported once, as a `RadioGroup` event that carries the option's index, and never its value or its label.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where each option's ring stands: before its label, or after it. After it, one under another, every option spans the group and the rings line up at its end; side by side, each ring follows its label.

Documented on: [Radio Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/radio-button.md)

### PantrixRadioGroup

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.PantrixRadioGroup`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixRadioGroup(
    field: FormField<T>,
    options: List<RadioOption<T>>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Vertical,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    style: RadioStyle? = null,
    colors: RadioColors? = null,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
```

A radio group bound to a form's field: its selection, its error and its name come from `field`.

A choice changes the field and marks it touched, so a rule's message shows after the first choice, or when the form is submitted, and not on a form nobody has touched. While the field is in error the message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the group's automation key, `RadioGroup_<id>`, with its options inside it, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error: it goes to the group's one stop.

A choice that has to be made is a field of a nullable value that starts at null, with `Rules.required`. Its options are options of the value itself: a `RadioOption<String>` is an option of a `FormField<String?>`.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a selection and a field cannot both be given.

Parameters:

- `field: FormField<T>`: the field the group shows and changes.
- `options: List<RadioOption<T>>`: the options, in order.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the group's modifier.
- `orientation: Orientation`: `Orientation.Vertical` for one option under another, `Orientation.Horizontal` for side by side.
- `enabled: Boolean`: false disables every option.
- `label: String?`: what the choice is, written over the options: the group's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the options, while the field has no error to show there.
- `style: RadioStyle?`: this call's own style, the one every option is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: RadioColors?`: the colours every option is drawn in, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled option and a group in error keep the theme's.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where each option's ring stands: before its label, or after it. After it, one under another, every option spans the group and the rings line up at its end; side by side, each ring follows its label.

Documented on: [Radio Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/radio-button.md)

### RadioStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.radiobutton.RadioStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class RadioStyle(
    public val size: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val dotSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val strokeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<RadioStyle>
```

`PantrixRadioButton`'s ring and the dot in it: how large each is, and how thick the ring.

The ring is 20dp around a 10dp dot, as Material 3 has it, and 22dp around a 12dp dot on iOS, where a checkbox is 22dp too. iOS has no radio button of its own: it marks the one chosen row of a list with a tick. Pantrix draws the same ring on every platform, so that a choice of one looks like one wherever it is made.

None of the three follows the density: a ring, its dot and its line are not air. The space between the ring and its label does, since it comes from the theme's spacing. A radio button's colours are not part of its style: they come from its state, and from `RadioColors` where a radio button has its own.

Parameters:

- `size: Dp`: The ring's width and height, its line included.
- `dotSize: Dp`: The width and height of the dot in a selected ring.
- `strokeWidth: Dp`: How thick the ring's line is.

Documented on: [Radio Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/radio-button.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.scrollbar

### Modifier.pantrixVerticalScroll

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.scrollbar.pantrixVerticalScroll`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun Modifier.pantrixVerticalScroll(
    state: ScrollState,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified
): Modifier
```

Scrolls this content up and down by `state`, as `Modifier.verticalScroll` does, with Pantrix's scroll bar along its side: a page of text, a form, a settings screen that is taller than its window.

The bar is the one Pantrix's own views of documents draw. Its thumb is as long as the share of the content on the screen, and stands where that share is. Where the reader has a pointer it is there while there is something to scroll, darker under the pointer, and a mouse can drag it; under a finger it shows while the content moves and fades after, since a finger scrolls the content itself. It stands at the end of the content, at the left where the layout is read from the right, and is drawn over the content rather than beside it: the content keeps its width.

The scroll and the bar come together, so that the bar stands over the window the content scrolls in, not on the content that scrolls under it:

```kotlin
val scroll = rememberScrollState()
Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize().pantrixVerticalScroll(scroll)) {
    Article()
}
```

A lazy list scrolls by itself, and takes its bar with `pantrixScrollBar`.

Parameters:

- `state: ScrollState`: how far the content is scrolled, as `rememberScrollState()` gives it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a drag, the wheel and the bar scroll the content: the bar is drawn either way, while there is something to scroll.
- `color: Color`: what the thumb is drawn in, at a share of its strength: the theme's `textSecondary` where it is not given. On a fill, the colour written on it.

Documented on: [Building blocks](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/building-blocks.md)

### Modifier.pantrixScrollBar

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.scrollbar.pantrixScrollBar`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun Modifier.pantrixScrollBar(
    state: LazyListState,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified
): Modifier
```

Pantrix's scroll bar along the side of a lazy list, which scrolls by its own `state`: the one `pantrixVerticalScroll` draws, on the list's own modifier.

A lazy list knows the rows on the screen and how many there are, not how tall the others are: the thumb takes them to be as tall as the ones it sees, which the rows of a list mostly are. Where they are not, the thumb's length changes a little as they come by.

```kotlin
val list = rememberLazyListState()
LazyColumn(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().pantrixScrollBar(list), state = list) {
    items(orders, key = { it.id }) { order -> OrderRow(order) }
}
```

Parameters:

- `state: LazyListState`: the list's state, the one the list is given.
- `color: Color`: what the thumb is drawn in, at a share of its strength: the theme's `textSecondary` where it is not given.

Documented on: [Building blocks](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/building-blocks.md)

- `label: String`: The visible text, and the segment's name for a screen reader.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: Drawn before the label, in the label's colour, or null for none. A screen reader passes over it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the segment can be chosen. A press does nothing on one that cannot, and the arrow keys skip it.

Documented on: [Segment Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/segment-button.md)

### PantrixSegmentButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixSegmentButton(
    options: List<SegmentOption<T>>,
    selected: T?,
    onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    fullWidth: Boolean = true,
    style: SegmentButtonStyle? = null,
    colors: SegmentButtonColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    labelStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label
)
```

A segment button: a small set of choices side by side in one control, one of them chosen.

It is a radio group drawn as one control. A screen reader hears a group of radio buttons, one of them selected, and a choice changes what is on the screen around it at once: a list's order, a chart's span, a map's layer. A pill slides to the chosen segment, and its label takes the primary colour. Choosing the segment that is chosen already does nothing.

The control is one stop for Tab, on the chosen segment. The arrow keys choose the next or the previous segment, the other way round in a right-to-left layout, round from the last to the first, and skip a segment that cannot be chosen. A press takes the focus to the control where a press can.

The track is as tall as the style says, with the platform's touch target reserved around it. A label set larger than the track, at a large font scale, makes it taller. Use it for two to five choices of a word or two: for more, or for longer ones, a radio group; for actions rather than a choice, buttons.

Parameters:

- `options: List<SegmentOption<T>>`: the choices, in order. An empty list draws nothing.
- `selected: T?`: the value of the chosen segment, compared with each option's by `==`. A value no option has, null among them, chooses none: no segment is selected and no pill is drawn.
- `onSelect: (T) -> Unit`: called with the value of the segment the user chose, by a press or by a key, when it is not the chosen one already. The control chooses nothing by itself: a segment is chosen when `selected` says so.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the control's modifier, outside the touch target it reserves.
- `enabled: Boolean`: false disables every segment. The pill stays where it is, so that the choice can still be read.
- `fullWidth: Boolean`: true spans the control across the width it is given, each segment taking an equal share, so that the segments stay where they are whatever their labels say in another language. False makes each segment as wide as its label; in a room too narrow for that, the short labels stay whole and the long ones share what is left.
- `style: SegmentButtonStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SegmentButtonColors?`: this control's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled control's track and a segment that cannot be chosen keep the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the control's automation key: the control is `SegmentButton_<tagKey>`, and its segments are named inside it, `SegmentButton_<tagKey>.Segment_<key>`, so that two controls with the same options are told apart. A choice is reported as a `SegmentButton` event, `select`, which carries the segment's key, or its place without one, and never its label.
- `labelStyle: TextStyle`: the type the labels are set in: the theme's `label` unless given. A label set larger than the track makes it taller, as a large font scale does.

Documented on: [Segment Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/segment-button.md)

### SegmentButtonStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentButtonStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SegmentButtonStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val trackPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val segmentPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<SegmentButtonStyle>
```

`PantrixSegmentButton`'s geometry: the track, the pill that slides inside it, and the room each segment gives its label.

The pill has no shape of its own: it is the track's shape with each corner smaller by `trackPadding`, so the two curve around the same centres on every brand's shape scale. A pill as round as the track would look rounder than the room it is in.

On Android the control is Material 3's segmented button: 40dp tall, a pill throughout. On iOS it is `UISegmentedControl`: 32pt tall, a rounded rectangle with the pill close to its edge. The desktop's is lower, 30dp, for a pointer, and the web's 34dp.

An icon goes by the buttons': 20dp on Android, where the pill is as tall as a small button, and 18dp in the lower pills of the other platforms, between a small button's icon and an extra small one's.

The height, the two paddings and the gap follow the density, since they are the room around the labels. The icon's size and the shape do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The track's shape: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `height: Dp`: The track's height. A label set larger than it has room for, at a large font scale, makes the track taller.
- `trackPadding: Dp`: The room between the track's edge and the pill.
- `segmentPadding: Dp`: The room on each side of a segment's label.
- `iconGap: Dp`: Between a segment's icon and its label.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The width and height of a segment's icon.

Documented on: [Segment Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/segment-button.md)

### SegmentButtonColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentButtonColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class SegmentButtonColors(
    public val track: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val pill: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val unselectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What `PantrixSegmentButton` is painted with, for a control that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```kotlin
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = sorts,
    selected = sort,
    onSelect = { sort = it },
    colors = SegmentButtonColors(pill = brand, selectedContent = onBrand)
)
```

They are the colours of segments that can be chosen. A disabled control's track and a segment that cannot be chosen are drawn in the theme's disabled roles whatever is given here; the pill keeps its colour, so that the choice can still be read.

A fill given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is drawn on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `track: Color`: The track the segments stand on. The neutral role's `container`.
- `pill: Color`: The pill under the chosen segment. The theme's `surface`.
- `selectedContent: Color`: The label and the icon of the chosen segment: the colour that reads on `pill`. The theme's `primary`.
- `unselectedContent: Color`: The label and the icon of the other segments: the colour that reads on `track`. The theme's `textSecondary`.

Documented on: [Segment Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/segment-button.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.selection

### ControlPosition

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.selection.ControlPosition`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ControlPosition
```

Where a checkbox's box, a radio button's ring or a switch's track stands against its label: before it, as a list of choices has it, or after it, at the end of the row, as a settings screen has a switch.

Entries:

- `Start`: Before the label, at the row's start: at the left, or at the right where the layout is read from the right.
- `End`: After the label: at the end of the width the row is given, or right after the label where it is given none. The label and its help wrap in what the control leaves, and never push it on.

```kotlin
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    labelStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label,
    controlPosition: ControlPosition = ControlPosition.Start
)
```

A switch: a setting that is on or off and takes effect at once, and the label it is the switch of.

The track, the label and the supporting text are one target. A press anywhere on them turns the switch, since on a phone the words are most of what a finger can hit, and a screen reader hears one switch, named by its label, that says whether it is on. The track stands on the label's first line, however many lines the label and the supporting text run to. The row takes the platform's touch target, small as the track is.

The thumb can be dragged as well. Let go past the middle of the track, it turns the switch on, and short of the middle it turns it off: a thumb let go on the side it started from settles back and nothing is reported. The drag runs with the reading direction, so right to left the on end is the left one, the end a press sends the thumb to. A press, a key and a drag change the switch in one way, with one haptic and one event.

The thumb slides, and the track turns to the primary role's colour with it, wherever the thumb is: under a finger that drags it too. Both happen at once under reduced motion.

Without `onCheckedChange` the switch is read-only: it takes no press, no drag and no focus, and still says its name and its state. `error` turns the supporting text to the danger role and is announced. The switch itself keeps its colours: a switch is a setting, and an answer that can be wrong belongs to a checkbox.

Parameters:

- `checked: Boolean`: whether the switch is on.
- `onCheckedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)?`: called with the value the user asks for, the opposite of `checked`. The switch changes nothing by itself: it is on when `checked` says so. Null makes it read-only.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the switch can be turned. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `label: String?`: the text beside the track: part of the target, and the switch's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the label, in a smaller type: the message, while `error` is true.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the value is wrong: the supporting text turns to the danger role, and a screen reader is told the input is invalid.
- `style: SwitchStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SwitchColors?`: this switch's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled switch keeps the theme's.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the switch: its name where it has no `label`, as in a row of the app's own that has the words elsewhere, or in place of the label.
- `tagKey: String?`: the switch's automation key: the row is `SwitchButton_<tagKey>`. A change is reported as a `SwitchButton` event that carries the new value, and never its label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the switch's interactions, hoisted: its presses, its drags and its focus. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `labelStyle: TextStyle`: the type the label is set in: the theme's `label` unless given. The track stands on its first line at any size. A colour in it is the label's while the switch is enabled; a disabled switch writes it in the disabled colour.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where the track stands: before the label, or after it, as a settings screen has it. After it, the track is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the track leaves.

Documented on: [Switch Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/switch-button.md)

### PantrixSwitchButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSwitchButton(
    field: FormField<Boolean>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,

```

A switch bound to a form's field: its value, its error and its name come from `field`.

A change sets the field and marks it touched, so a rule's message shows after the first change, or when the form is submitted, and not on a form nobody has touched. While the field is in error the message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the switch's automation key, `SwitchButton_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a value and a field cannot both be given.

Parameters:

- `field: FormField<Boolean>`: the field the switch shows and changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the switch can be turned.
- `label: String?`: the text beside the track: part of the target, and the switch's name for a screen reader.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the label, while the field has no error to show there.
- `style: SwitchStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SwitchColors?`: this switch's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled switch keeps the theme's.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the switch where it has no `label`, or in place of it.
- `labelStyle: TextStyle`: the type the label is set in: the theme's `label` unless given.
- `controlPosition: ControlPosition`: where the track stands: before the label, or after it, as a settings screen has it. After it, the track is at the end of the width the row is given, `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` lining it up with the others, or right after the label where the row is given none; the label wraps in what the track leaves.
