### SwitchStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.SwitchStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SwitchStyle(
    public val trackWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val trackHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val thumbSizeOff: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val thumbSizeOn: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val thumbSizePressed: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val strokeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val thumbAlwaysLight: Boolean? = null,
    public val thumbShadow: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<SwitchStyle>
```

`PantrixSwitchButton`'s track and its thumb: how large each is, the track's edge, and what the thumb looks like.

The thumb has three sizes. On Material 3 it grows from off to on, and further while it is held: that change is the switch's own motion, so Android's preset has three sizes. iOS's switch never resizes its thumb, and under a pointer a thumb that changes size is noise, so on iOS, the desktop and the web the three are one size. The component never asks which platform it is on.

The thumb sits in the middle of the track's round end, as far from the end as from the sides, at every size: the room around it is what the track's height leaves, and no value of its own.

`strokeWidth` is the edge of a track that is off, in the border colour, which marks where the control is at 3:1 against what it sits on. Material 3 draws one, and so does Windows: Android's preset has Material's, and the desktop's and the web's a thinner one, since their track is smaller. iOS draws none and leaves a pale track with a white thumb and its shadow, which Pantrix keeps there.

None of it follows the density: a track, its thumb and its edge are not air. The space between the track and its label does, since it comes from the theme's spacing. A switch's colours are not part of its style: they come from its state, and from `SwitchColors` where a switch has its own.

Parameters:

- `trackWidth: Dp`: The track's width, its edge included.
- `trackHeight: Dp`: The track's height, its edge included. The track's ends are as round as it is tall.
- `thumbSizeOff: Dp`: The thumb's width and height while the switch is off.
- `thumbSizeOn: Dp`: The thumb's width and height while the switch is on.
- `thumbSizePressed: Dp`: The thumb's width and height while it is pressed or dragged.
- `strokeWidth: Dp`: How thick the edge of a track that is off is. Zero draws none.
- `thumbAlwaysLight: Boolean?`: True keeps the thumb white whatever the theme and the state, as iOS has it. False draws it in the border colour when off and in the colour paired with the track's fill when on, as Material has it. Null is unspecified.
- `thumbShadow: Dp`: How far the thumb stands above the track: the size of the shadow under it. Zero draws none.

Documented on: [Switch Button](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/switch-button.md)

### SwitchColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.SwitchColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class SwitchColors(
    public val checkedTrack: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val checkedThumb: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val uncheckedTrack: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val uncheckedThumb: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val border: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What `PantrixSwitchButton` is painted with, for a switch that does not take the theme's: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's role.

```kotlin
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = notifications,
    onCheckedChange = { notifications = it },
    label = stringResource(Res.string.notifications),
    colors = SwitchColors(checkedTrack = brand)
)
```

They are the colours of a switch that can be turned. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled roles whatever is given here. Between off and on the track and the thumb turn from one colour to the other as the thumb moves.

A track given here that is one of the theme's own colours brings the thumb the theme pairs with it, unless the thumb is given too or the style keeps it light. A track no role has does not: the thumb on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `checkedTrack: Color`: The track's fill when the switch is on. The theme's `primary`.
- `checkedThumb: Color`: The thumb when the switch is on: the colour that stands out on `checkedTrack`. The primary role's `onColor`, or white where the style keeps the thumb light.
- `uncheckedTrack: Color`: The track's fill when the switch is off. A tint of the theme's `borderStrong`.
- `uncheckedThumb: Color`: The thumb when the switch is off: the colour that stands out on `uncheckedTrack`. The theme's `borderStrong`, or white where the style keeps the thumb light.
- `border: Color`: The edge of a track that is off, where the style draws one. The theme's `borderStrong`: a switch that is off is seen by its edge and its thumb.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.elements.text

### TextRole

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.TextRole`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
sealed interface TextRole
```

What a piece of text *is*, which decides how a screen reader treats it.

A visual style is not a substitute: text styled like a heading but not marked as one is invisible to the heading-navigation every screen reader user relies on to skim a page.

#### TextRole.Paragraph

```kotlin
data object Paragraph : TextRole
```

Ordinary prose.

#### TextRole.Heading

```kotlin
data class Heading(val level: Int) : TextRole
```

A heading at `level` (1 = page title). Enables heading navigation.

Parameters:

- `level: Int`: The heading's depth: 1 for the page's title, 2 for its sections, and so on down.

#### TextRole.Label

```kotlin
data object Label : TextRole
```

Names a control or a value.

#### TextRole.Decorative

```kotlin
data object Decorative : TextRole
```

Purely visual — hidden from assistive technology.

For text already announced by something else: the letter inside an avatar whose content description is the person's full name. Its words are left out of the semantics tree, so a parent heard as one does not read them with its own: a test finds it by its tag.

Documented on: [Text](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/text.md), [Auto Text](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/auto-text.md)

### PantrixText

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixText(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    style: TextStyle = LocalPantrixTextStyle.current,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    textAlign: TextAlign? = null,
    maxLines: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE,
    minLines: Int = 1,
    overflow: TextOverflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
    softWrap: Boolean = true,
    role: TextRole = TextRole.Paragraph,
    selectable: Boolean = false,
    onTextLayout: ((TextLayoutResult) -> Unit)? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Text in the theme's type. `style` is the base text unless given, `LocalPantrixTextStyle`: the label role, or what a part of the screen around it provides. `role` tells a screen reader what the text is: a heading, a label, decoration. `selectable` lets the user select and copy it.

The colour is `color`, or else the style's, or else the theme's `textPrimary`: on the theme's own grounds, the page, a surface and a card, a text is drawn in the primary text colour. Only a fill says otherwise: on a solid button, a card filled with a role's colour or anything else that gives its content a colour, a text takes that colour, which is the one that reads there.

The text is set in the size its style says, and what does not fit is cut as `overflow` says. A text that is to get smaller to fit its room is `PantrixAutoText`.

Parameters:

- `text: String`: the text.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the text's modifier.
- `style: TextStyle`
- `color: Color`
- `textAlign: TextAlign?`: how the lines are aligned in the text's width.
- `maxLines: Int`: the most lines the text takes; what goes past them is cut as `overflow` says.
- `minLines: Int`: the least lines the text is tall.
- `overflow: TextOverflow`
- `softWrap: Boolean`: whether the text wraps where its width ends.
- `role: TextRole`
- `selectable: Boolean`
- `onTextLayout: ((TextLayoutResult) -> Unit)?`: called with the text as it is laid out.
- `tagKey: String?`: the text's automation key: the text is `Text_<tagKey>`. Without one it has no tag.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.inputs.autoresizetextfield

### PantrixAutoResizeTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.autoresizetextfield.PantrixAutoResizeTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    state: TextFieldState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null,
    minFontSize: TextUnit = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote.fontSize,
    lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field whose text gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a card's number, a short note, anything that is read whole.

The text is as large as its style says while it fits. A text too long for the box is set in a smaller size, as small as it takes to fit, and grows back as it is shortened. The box does not grow wider with its text: its width is its style's least or the one its caller gave it. At `minFontSize` the text stops shrinking and scrolls, as the text of any field does.

The field holds one line unless told: a line that is fitted to the box's width, in a box that keeps its height. With `lineLimits` of several lines the text wraps, and the box grows with it from the least of its lines to the most, as a text field's does. From there the box keeps its height and the text is set smaller, its lines as much closer, so that all of it stays in the box.

A height the field is given comes before its lines. The box fills what the label and the supporting text leave of it, and the text is fitted to that: it is set smaller where the height holds fewer lines than the field may take, and keeps its size for as many lines as a taller one holds. One line is set smaller in a box too low for it.

What is fitted is the text as it is shown: after an output transformation, and with what the keyboard is still composing. It is the text's size that changes, and nothing is drawn smaller than it is laid out: the caret, a selection and its handles are those of the size the text is in, and that size is what a test reads from the text's layout. The placeholder is set as the text would be, in a smaller size where it is too long. A box whose size changes has its text fitted again a frame later. A text that is too long for its box when the field is first shown is drawn a frame later too, fitted, and is never seen in a size too large.

It is the label, the box and the supporting text of `PantrixTextField`, and takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its text fields restyles this one with them. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

Parameters:

- `state: TextFieldState`: the text and the selection. Create it with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent, and a height is one the text is fitted to as it is to the width.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the text's own style.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the border, the label, the supporting text and the caret turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(TextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, and after the clear button: a currency's sign after an amount.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `textStyle: TextStyle?`: the style of the text at its largest: a role of the theme's typography, such as `PantrixTheme.typography.headline` for an amount. What it leaves unset is the body's, which is what the text is set in without it. A box too short for the style grows to hold a line of it.
- `minFontSize: TextUnit`: the smallest the text gets: a size in sp, or one in em, which is a share of the style's own. It is the theme's footnote size unless told. A text that does not fit at this size scrolls, and at the style's own size or above it the text never shrinks.
- `lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits`: one line, or `TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine`, in which the text wraps and Enter starts a new line. The box is as tall as its lines are at the text's largest size: it grows from `minHeightInLines` to `maxHeightInLines`, and past the most of them the text is set smaller. With no most lines the box grows with its text for as long as it may, and the text is set smaller only where the field is given a height. Tab moves the focus on from either.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key.
- `onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler?`: called for the keyboard's action key, for the action `keyboardOptions` names. Null keeps what the platform does: `Next` moves the focus on, and `Done` closes the keyboard.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.
- `outputTransformation: OutputTransformation?`: how the text is shown, without changing it: an amount's separators. The text is fitted as it is shown.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in: `ContentType.CreditCardNumber` and the like.
- `style: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `AutoResizeTextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `AutoResizeTextFieldClear_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus and that it was cleared, and never its text.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

Documented on: [Auto Resize Text Field](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/auto-resize-text-field.md)

### PantrixAutoResizeTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.autoresizetextfield.PantrixAutoResizeTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin

fun PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    value: String,
    onValueChange: (String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null,
    minFontSize: TextUnit = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote.fontSize,
    singleLine: Boolean = true,
    minLines: Int = 1,
    maxLines: Int = if (singleLine) 1 else Int.MAX_VALUE,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default,
    visualTransformation: VisualTransformation = VisualTransformation.None,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field whose text shrinks to fit, and whose text is a `String` its caller holds: `value` is what it shows, and `onValueChange` is asked for every change the user makes.

It looks, measures and shrinks its text as the field on a `TextFieldState` does, and underneath it is Foundation's text field of a value and a callback. The text the callback is given has to come back as `value` by the next frame, or the field shows the old text again and the caret jumps: keep the text in state that the callback writes at once, and take the `TextFieldState` overload when the text lives in a flow. What comes back may differ from what was asked for, which is how this overload filters: a change the callback does not take is not shown.

It speaks the vocabulary of the text field underneath: `singleLine`, `minLines` and `maxLines` for its lines.

Parameters:

- `value: String`: the text the field shows.
- `onValueChange: (String) -> Unit`: asked for each change the user makes, with the whole new text, and by the clear button with an empty one.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the text's own style.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the border, the label, the supporting text and the caret turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.

### PantrixAutoResizeTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.autoresizetextfield.PantrixAutoResizeTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAutoResizeTextField(
    field: FormField<String>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    form: FormState? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null,
    minFontSize: TextUnit = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote.fontSize,
    lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field whose text shrinks to fit, bound to a form's field: its text, its error and its name come from `field`.

The field's value and the text on screen stay in step both ways: typing changes the field, and a change made to the field in code, such as a reset, replaces the text. When the focus leaves, the field is marked touched and checked, which is when an error first shows. While the field is in error its message takes the place of `supportingText`. The field's id is the automation key, `AutoResizeTextField_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

Parameters:

- `field: FormField<String>`: the field the text field shows and changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field.
- `form: FormState?`: given, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the button registered with it. An action of `Next` or `Previous` moves the focus as it always does. A field of one line that names no action gets `ImeAction.Done`, since the default action never reaches a handler. A field of several lines is left alone: there Enter starts a new line. An `onKeyboardAction` of the caller's own takes the place of the submit.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the text's own style.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, while the field has no error to show there.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, and after the clear button.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `textStyle: TextStyle?`: the style of the text at its largest. What it leaves unset is the body's.
- `minFontSize: TextUnit`: the smallest the text gets, in sp or in em: the theme's footnote size unless told.
- `lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits`: one line, or `TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine`, whose text is set smaller past the most of its lines. Tab moves the focus on from either.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key.
- `onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler?`: called for the keyboard's action key, in place of the form's submit.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it.
- `outputTransformation: OutputTransformation?`: how the text is shown, without changing it. The text is fitted as it is shown.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in.
- `style: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.inputs.common

### TextLimit

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.common.TextLimit`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class TextLimit
```

What a text area does with an edit that takes its text past its `maxLength`: takes it and shows that the text is too long, or turns it down.

Entries:

- `Allow`: The edit is taken, and the field shows that the text is too long: the count says in words how far past the limit it is, and the border and the count turn to the error's colour. A paste is kept whole, for the user to cut where they choose, rather than cut where the limit falls. A form the field is bound to is not submitted while its text is past the limit.
- `Block`: The edit is turned down whole, as a text field's limit turns it down: typing stops at the limit, and a paste that does not fit is not put in.

Documented on: [Text Area](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/text-area.md), [Filled Text Area](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/filled-text-area.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledautoresizetextfield

### PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledautoresizetextfield.PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField(
    state: TextFieldState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    textStyle: TextStyle? = null,
    minFontSize: TextUnit = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote.fontSize,
    lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field whose label is inside its box and whose text gets smaller to stay in view: an amount, a card's number, a short note, anything that is read whole, in the filled box of `PantrixFilledTextField`.

The text is as large as its style says while it fits. A text too long for the box is set in a smaller size, as small as it takes to fit, and grows back as it is shortened. The box does not grow wider with its text: its width is its style's least or the one its caller gave it. At `minFontSize` the text stops shrinking and scrolls, as the text of any field does.

The field holds one line unless told: a line that is fitted to the box's width, in a box that keeps its height. With `lineLimits` of several lines the text wraps, and the box grows with it from the least of its lines to the most, as a filled text field's does. From there the box keeps its height and the text is set smaller, its lines as much closer, so that all of it stays in the box.

A height the field is given comes before its lines. The box fills what the supporting text leaves of it, and the text is fitted to that: it is set smaller where the height holds fewer lines than the field may take, and keeps its size for as many lines as a taller one holds. One line is set smaller in a box too low for it.

What is fitted is the text as it is shown: after an output transformation, and with what the keyboard is still composing. It is the text's size that changes, and nothing is drawn smaller than it is laid out: the caret, a selection and its handles are those of the size the text is in, and that size is what a test reads from the text's layout. The placeholder is set in the text's size, and in a smaller one where it is too long. A box whose size changes has its text fitted again a frame later. A text that is too long for its box when the field is first shown is drawn a frame later too, fitted, and is never seen in a size too large.

The label rests where the text will be, in the body's size whatever the text's own, and moves up to its own line above the text when the field takes the focus or holds a text. The box is filled and has no outline at rest, and is outlined with the focus and in error. It is that filled box around the text that `PantrixAutoResizeTextField` shrinks, and takes the filled text field's `style` and `colors`: the filled fields are restyled together, and the two fields that shrink their text can stand in for each other. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

Parameters:

- `state: TextFieldState`: the text and the selection. Create it with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent, and a height is one the text is fitted to as it is to the width.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn without its fill in the disabled colours, and says so.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader. Without one the text stands in the middle of the box, and the `placeholder` shows whenever the field is empty.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown where the text goes while the field is empty and its label is out of the way: while it has the focus, or always where it has no label. It is set in the text's style, without the weight a filled field adds to what is typed.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the box is outlined in the danger role's colour, the supporting text and the caret turn to it, and a screen reader is told.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the label and the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, and after the clear button: a currency's sign after an amount.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `textStyle: TextStyle?`: the style of the text at its largest: a role of the theme's typography, such as `PantrixTheme.typography.title` for an amount. What it leaves unset is the body's in the medium weight, which is what a filled field's text is set in without it. A box too short for the style grows to hold its label and a line of it.
- `minFontSize: TextUnit`: the smallest the text gets: a size in sp, or one in em, which is a share of the style's own. It is the theme's footnote size unless told. A text that does not fit at this size scrolls, and at the style's own size or above it the text never shrinks.
- `lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits`: one line, or `TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine`, in which the text wraps and Enter starts a new line. The box is as tall as its lines are at the text's largest size: it grows from `minHeightInLines` to `maxHeightInLines`, and past the most of them the text is set smaller. With no most lines the box grows with its text for as long as it may, and the text is set smaller only where the field is given a height. Tab moves the focus on from either.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key.
- `onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler?`: called for the keyboard's action key, for the action `keyboardOptions` names. Null keeps what the platform does.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.
- `outputTransformation: OutputTransformation?`: how the text is shown, without changing it: an amount's separators. The text is fitted as it is shown.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in: `ContentType.CreditCardNumber` and the like.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledAutoResizeTextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `FilledAutoResizeTextFieldClear_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus and that it was cleared, and never its text.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

It looks, measures and shrinks its text as the field on a `TextFieldState` does, and underneath it is Foundation's text field of a value and a callback. The text the callback is given has to come back as `value` by the next frame, or the field shows the old text again and the caret jumps: keep the text in state that the callback writes at once, and take the `TextFieldState` overload when the text lives in a flow. What comes back may differ from what was asked for, which is how this overload filters: a change the callback does not take is not shown.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledsecuretextfield

### PantrixFilledSecureTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledsecuretextfield.PantrixFilledSecureTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    state: TextFieldState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    showRevealButton: Boolean = true,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    textObfuscationMode: TextObfuscationMode = TextObfuscationMode.System,
    textObfuscationCharacter: Char = '•',
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A secure text field whose label is inside its box: a password, a PIN or a card's security code in the filled box of `PantrixFilledTextField`.

What is typed is drawn as dots, and cannot be cut, copied or dragged out of the field. The platform is told that the field holds a password, and while the text is hidden it is given the dots for the text: a screen reader reads no password out, and a password manager still fills the field and saves it. The field holds one line.

A button at the box's end shows the text and hides it again. With a keyboard it is a Tab stop of its own, after the field, and the keyboard's `Next` goes past it to the next field. A press on it with a pointer leaves the caret where it is. That the text was shown is not saved: it is hidden again when the field is made anew, as it is after the screen turns.

The label rests where the text will be, and moves up to its own line above the text when the field takes the focus or holds a text. The box is filled and has no outline at rest, and is outlined with the focus and in error. It is that filled box around the secure text field that `PantrixSecureTextField` is underneath, and takes the filled text field's `style` and `colors`: the two filled fields are restyled together, and the two secure fields can stand in for each other. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload for a form's field: the text is read from the state, where it is used or as it changes.

Parameters:

- `state: TextFieldState`: the text and the selection. Create it with `remember { TextFieldState() }`, or keep it in a view model: `rememberTextFieldState()` puts what is typed into the saved state, which the platform holds after the app's process has gone and may write to its disk. A remembered state goes when the screen is made anew, as it is after the screen turns, and the field is empty again. Read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn without its fill in the disabled colours, has no button to show its text and says so.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, and shown by the button.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader. Without one the text stands in the middle of the box, and the `placeholder` shows whenever the field is empty.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown where the text goes while the field is empty and its label is out of the way: while it has the focus, or always where it has no label.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the box is outlined in the danger role's colour, the supporting text and the caret turn to it, and a screen reader is told.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the label and the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, after the clear button and the button that shows the text.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.
- `showRevealButton: Boolean`: shows the button that shows the text and hides it again, while the field is enabled. Without it the text stays as `textObfuscationMode` draws it: for a text that is never to be shown, and for a caller that shows it another way.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `textObfuscationMode: TextObfuscationMode`: how the text is drawn while it is hidden. `TextObfuscationMode.System` does as the platform does: on Android the last character typed shows for a moment where the system's own setting says so, and nowhere else does anything show. `Hidden` shows nothing on any platform, and `RevealLastTyped` the last character for a moment on every one.
- `textObfuscationCharacter: Char`: what is drawn in place of a hidden character.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key. What these leave unset is a password's, the password keyboard and no corrections, so that naming an action does not bring back a keyboard that learns what is typed. `KeyboardType.NumberPassword` is a PIN's.
- `onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler?`: called for the keyboard's action key, for the action `keyboardOptions` names. Null keeps what the platform does.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in. Left out, the field holds `ContentType.Password`, as Foundation's secure field says for itself: `ContentType.NewPassword` is one that is being chosen.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledSecureTextField_<tagKey>`, its clear button `FilledSecureTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and the button that shows its text `FilledSecureTextFieldReveal_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus, that it was cleared and that its text was shown or hidden, and never its text.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

Documented on: [Filled Secure Text Field](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/filled-secure-text-field.md)

### PantrixFilledSecureTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledsecuretextfield.PantrixFilledSecureTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledSecureTextField(
    field: FormField<String>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    form: FormState? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    showRevealButton: Boolean = true,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    textObfuscationMode: TextObfuscationMode = TextObfuscationMode.System,
    textObfuscationCharacter: Char = '•',
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A filled secure text field bound to a form's field: its text, its error and its name come from `field`.

The field's value and the text on screen stay in step both ways: typing changes the field, and a change made to the field in code, such as a reset, replaces the text. When the focus leaves the field and its buttons, the field is marked touched and checked, which is when an error first shows. While the field is in error its message takes the place of `supportingText`. The field's id is the automation key, `FilledSecureTextField_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

Parameters:

- `field: FormField<String>`: the field the text field shows and changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field.
- `form: FormState?`: given, the keyboard's action key submits the form through the button registered with it. An action of `Next` or `Previous` moves the focus as it always does. A field that names no action gets `ImeAction.Done`, since the default action never reaches a handler. An `onKeyboardAction` of the caller's own takes the place of the submit.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown where the text goes while the field is empty and its label is out of the way.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, while the field has no error to show there.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the label and the text.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, after the clear button and the button that shows the text.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `showRevealButton: Boolean`: shows the button that shows the text and hides it again, while the field is enabled.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `textObfuscationMode: TextObfuscationMode`: how the text is drawn while it is hidden.
- `textObfuscationCharacter: Char`: what is drawn in place of a hidden character.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key. What these leave unset is a password's.
- `onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler?`: called for the keyboard's action key, in place of the form's submit.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in. Left out, it is `ContentType.Password`.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledtextarea

### PantrixFilledTextArea

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledtextarea.PantrixFilledTextArea`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledTextArea(
    state: TextFieldState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minLines: Int = 3,
    maxLines: Int = 8,
    resizable: Boolean = true,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    overLimit: TextLimit = TextLimit.Allow,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    onSubmit: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences),
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A filled text area: a field for text of several lines, a comment, a message or a note, on a filled box that grows with what is typed and then scrolls, with its label inside the box, and help or an error's message below it and a count of its characters.

The label rests in the place of the first line while the field is empty and without the focus, and rises above the text as the field takes the focus or holds text, as a filled text field's does.

The box is `minLines` lines tall while it is empty and grows a line at a time with its text, up to `maxLines`. Past them the text scrolls in the box, and a thin bar at the box's end shows how far. Where the platform is used with a pointer, a handle in the box's bottom corner drags it taller or shorter, and the box then keeps the height it was left at whatever its text, down to its least lines.

Enter starts a new line on every keyboard: a software keyboard always shows its key for one, and never an action in its place. A text that is sent takes `onSubmit`, which Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, call from a hardware keyboard; a screen gives it a button as well, since a software keyboard has no such keys. Tab moves the focus on, and does not type a tab, which would leave a keyboard no way forward out of the field.

A `maxLength` is soft unless told otherwise: the text may pass it, and the count then says how far past it the text is, in words, with the border in the error's colour. A paste that does not fit is kept whole, for the user to cut where they choose. `TextLimit.Block` turns an edit past the limit down instead, as a text field's limit does.

On iOS a field of several lines has no key that puts the keyboard away: `Modifier.clearFocusOnTap()` on the screen puts it away when the user taps outside the field.

It is the box and the supporting text of `PantrixFilledTextField`, and takes that component's `style` and `colors`: a product that restyles its filled text fields restyles its filled text areas with them. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

Parameters:

- `state: TextFieldState`: the text and the selection. Create it with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent. A height is the whole field's as well, in place of its lines: the box fills what the supporting text leaves of it, and its text scrolls in it. The handle moves the box only within such a height, so a field that is to be dragged is given `heightIn` and not `height`.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours, has no handle and says so.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected, copied, scrolled and dragged taller.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, inside the box: in the place of the first line while the field is empty and without the focus, and above the text otherwise. It is the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty. It is no label: it goes as soon as the user types.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the outline, the supporting text and the caret turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told. A text past a soft `maxLength` is drawn in error as well.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text, at its first line, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text at its first line, and after the clear button.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button at the first line that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field. It is no stop for Tab, and a screen reader still reaches it as a button.
- `minLines: Int`: how many lines tall the box is at the least: while it is empty, and when it is dragged its shortest. At least one.
- `maxLines: Int`: how many lines tall the box grows to with its text before the text scrolls in it. No fewer than `minLines`: the two the same give a box that keeps its height.
- `resizable: Boolean`: whether a handle in the box's bottom corner drags it taller or shorter. Only where the platform is used with a pointer, a desktop's or a browser's: on a phone a finger on the box scrolls its text.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the text should hold, counted as `String.length` counts them, so that an emoji can count as two. What an edit past it does is `overLimit`'s. It has to be positive.
- `overLimit: TextLimit`: what an edit past `maxLength` does: `TextLimit.Allow` takes it and shows that the text is too long, and `TextLimit.Block` turns it down whole.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows the count under the box while `maxLength` is set: `120/500`, and past the limit how far past it, `12 over the limit`. A screen reader is told it once typing pauses, at the limit and past it.
- `onSubmit: (() -> Unit)?`: called for Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, on a hardware keyboard: the text is sent. Null leaves both keys to the field. It is reported, and the text never is.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals and its corrections: a sentence starts with a capital unless told otherwise. The keyboard's action is always the new line, whatever is named here.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it. With a `maxLength` that blocks, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.
- `outputTransformation: OutputTransformation?`: how the text is shown, without changing it.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style, the filled text field's: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, the filled text field's, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye, so that the field is not named twice while it is empty.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledTextArea_<tagKey>`, its clear button `FilledTextAreaClear_<tagKey>` and its handle `FilledTextAreaResize_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus, that it was cleared and that it was submitted, and never its text.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

Documented on: [Filled Text Area](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/filled-text-area.md)

### PantrixFilledTextArea

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledtextarea.PantrixFilledTextArea`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledTextArea(
    value: String,
    onValueChange: (String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minLines: Int = 3,
    maxLines: Int = 8,
    resizable: Boolean = true,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    overLimit: TextLimit = TextLimit.Allow,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    onSubmit: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences),
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text area whose text is a `String` its caller holds: `value` is what it shows, and `onValueChange` is asked for every change the user makes.

It looks, measures and behaves as the text area on a `TextFieldState` does, and underneath it is Foundation's text field of a value and a callback, with what that brings. The text the callback is given has to come back as `value` by the next frame, or the field shows the old text again and the caret jumps: keep the text in state that the callback writes at once, and take the `TextFieldState` overload when the text lives in a flow or is changed away from the screen. That text field does not tell how far its text is scrolled, so its box has no bar that shows it.

Parameters:

- `value: String`: the text the field shows.
- `onValueChange: (String) -> Unit`: asked for each change the user makes, with the whole new text, and by the clear button with an empty one.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it. A height is the whole field's, in place of its lines.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours, has no handle and says so.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, inside the box: in the place of the first line while the field is empty and without the focus, and above the text otherwise. It is the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, once the label has risen above it.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the outline, the supporting text and the caret turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told. A text past a soft `maxLength` is drawn in error as well.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text, at its first line.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text at its first line, and after the clear button.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button at the first line that asks for an empty text, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.
- `minLines: Int`: how many lines tall the box is at the least. At least one.
- `maxLines: Int`: how many lines tall the box grows to with its text before the text scrolls in it. No fewer than `minLines`.
- `resizable: Boolean`: whether a handle in the box's bottom corner drags it taller or shorter, where the platform is used with a pointer.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the text should hold, counted as `String.length` counts them. What an edit past it does is `overLimit`'s. It has to be positive.
- `overLimit: TextLimit`: what an edit past `maxLength` does: `TextLimit.Allow` asks for it and shows that the text is too long, and `TextLimit.Block` turns it down before `onValueChange` is asked.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows the count under the box while `maxLength` is set, and past the limit how far past it.
- `onSubmit: (() -> Unit)?`: called for Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, on a hardware keyboard. Null leaves both keys to the field.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals and its corrections. The keyboard's action is always the new line, whatever is named here.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style, the filled text field's: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, the filled text field's, in place of the theme's roles. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledTextArea_<tagKey>`, its clear button `FilledTextAreaClear_<tagKey>` and its handle `FilledTextAreaResize_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus, that it was cleared and that it was submitted, and never its text.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledTextArea(
    field: FormField<String>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    form: FormState? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minLines: Int = 3,
    maxLines: Int = 8,
    resizable: Boolean = true,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    overLimit: TextLimit = TextLimit.Allow,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    onSubmit: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences),
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null

```

A text area bound to a form's field: its text, its error and its name come from `field`.

The field's value and the text on screen stay in step both ways: typing changes the field, and a change made to the field in code, such as a reset, replaces the text. When the focus leaves, the field is marked touched and checked, which is when an error first shows. While the field is in error its message takes the place of `supportingText`. A text past a soft `maxLength` puts the field in error as well, so that the form is not submitted with it: the message is `PantrixStrings.tooLong`, and the count says how far past the limit the text is. The field's id is the automation key, `FilledTextArea_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

Parameters:

- `field: FormField<String>`: the field the text area shows and changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field.
- `form: FormState?`: given, Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, submit the form through the button registered with it: the form is checked, and then submitted or the focus sent to its first field in error. Enter alone starts a new line. An `onSubmit` of the caller's own takes the place of the form's submit.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, while the field has no error to show there.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text, at its first line.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text at its first line, and after the clear button.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `minLines: Int`: how many lines tall the box is at the least. At least one.
- `maxLines: Int`: how many lines tall the box grows to with its text before the text scrolls in it. No fewer than `minLines`.
- `resizable: Boolean`: whether a handle in the box's bottom corner drags it taller or shorter, where the platform is used with a pointer.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the text should hold. It has to be positive.
- `overLimit: TextLimit`: what an edit past `maxLength` does: `TextLimit.Allow` takes it and puts the field in error, and `TextLimit.Block` turns it down whole.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows the count under the box while `maxLength` is set, and past the limit how far past it.
- `onSubmit: (() -> Unit)?`: called for Ctrl and Enter, or Cmd and Enter, on a hardware keyboard, in place of the form's submit.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals and its corrections. The keyboard's action is always the new line, whatever is named here.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it.
- `outputTransformation: OutputTransformation?`: how the text is shown, without changing it.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style, the filled text field's: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, the filled text field's, in place of the theme's roles. A disabled field is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledtextfield

### PantrixFilledTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledtextfield.PantrixFilledTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledTextField(
    state: TextFieldState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler? = null,
    inputTransformation: InputTransformation? = null,
    outputTransformation: OutputTransformation? = null,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field whose label is inside its box: the label rests where the text will be, and moves up to its own line above the text when the field takes the focus or holds a text.

The box is filled and has no outline at rest. With the focus it is outlined in the primary role's colour, and in error in the danger role's, on the surface's colour both times: the outline is what shows the focus and the error, and a message under the box says what to put right. A box that cannot be typed into has no fill at all.

It holds one line, or several in a box that scrolls its text and shows how far with a bar at its end.

It is the text field `PantrixTextField` is underneath, with another decoration around the text, and takes what that one takes: the two can stand in for each other. It is built on a `TextFieldState`, and has an overload that takes a `value` and an `onValueChange`, and one for a form's field.

Parameters:

- `state: TextFieldState`: the text and the selection. Create it with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and read what was typed from it: `state.text` where the text is used, or `snapshotFlow { state.text.toString() }` to follow it as it changes.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` makes the box as wide as its parent. A height is the whole field's as well: the box fills what the supporting text leaves of it, with one line in its middle and several from its top, and a text too long for the box scrolls in it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into. One that cannot takes no focus, is drawn without its fill in the disabled colours, and says so.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader. Without one the text stands in the middle of the box, and the `placeholder` shows whenever the field is empty.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown where the text goes while the field is empty and its label is out of the way: while it has the focus, or always where it has no label.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box, in a smaller type. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the box is outlined in the danger role's colour, the supporting text and the caret turn to it, and a screen reader is told.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the label and the text, in the secondary text colour. A slot does not size what is put in it: `PantrixIcon(size = PantrixTheme.style(FilledTextFieldStyle).iconSize)` is the platform's size.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, and after the clear button.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while the field can be typed into and is not empty. It leaves the caret in the field, and is no stop for Tab.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter, counted as `String.length` counts them. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole. Text set in code is not cut, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `lineLimits: TextFieldLineLimits`: one line, or `TextFieldLineLimits.MultiLine`: the box is as tall as its least lines, grows to its most, and scrolls from there. Tab moves the focus on from either.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key.
- `onKeyboardAction: KeyboardActionHandler?`: called for the keyboard's action key, for the action `keyboardOptions` names. Null keeps what the platform does.
- `inputTransformation: InputTransformation?`: what is done to the text as the user types it. With `maxLength`, it comes first and the limit applies to what it lets through.
- `outputTransformation: OutputTransformation?`: how the text is shown, without changing it.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in: `ContentType.EmailAddress` and the like.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`. A `placeholder` that says the same is then left to the eye.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledTextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `FilledTextFieldClear_<tagKey>`. The field reports that it took the focus and that it was cleared, and never its text.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

### PantrixFilledTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.filledtextfield.PantrixFilledTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFilledTextField(
    value: String,
    onValueChange: (String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    showCharacterCount: Boolean = true,
    singleLine: Boolean = true,
    minLines: Int = 1,
    maxLines: Int = if (singleLine) 1 else Int.MAX_VALUE,
    keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions.Default,
    keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default,
    visualTransformation: VisualTransformation = VisualTransformation.None,
    contentType: ContentType? = null,
    style: FilledTextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: FilledTextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A filled text field whose text is a `String` its caller holds: `value` is what it shows, and `onValueChange` is asked for every change the user makes.

It looks and measures as the field on a `TextFieldState` does, and underneath it is Foundation's text field of a value and a callback, with what that brings. The text the callback is given has to come back as `value` by the next frame, or the field shows the old text again and the caret jumps: keep the text in state that the callback writes at once, and take the `TextFieldState` overload when the text lives in a flow or is changed away from the screen. What comes back may differ from what was asked for, which is how this overload filters: a change the callback does not take is not shown.

It speaks the vocabulary of the text field underneath: `singleLine`, `minLines` and `maxLines` for its lines, `keyboardActions` for the keyboard's action key, and `visualTransformation` for how the text is shown, a password's dots among them. That text field does not tell how far its text is scrolled, so a box of several lines has no bar here.

Parameters:

- `value: String`: the text the field shows.
- `onValueChange: (String) -> Unit`: asked for each change the user makes, with the whole new text, and by the clear button with an empty one.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be typed into.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the text can only be read: it can still be focused, selected and copied.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written inside the box: the field's name for a screen reader.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown where the text goes while the field is empty and its label is out of the way.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the text is wrong: the box is outlined in the danger role's colour, and a screen reader is told.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the label and the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.
- `trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands after the text, and after the clear button.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that asks for an empty text, while the field can be typed into and is not empty.
- `maxLength: Int?`: the most characters the user can enter. An edit that would pass the limit is turned down whole, before `onValueChange` is asked. A `value` over the limit is shown as it is, and the user can still make it shorter. It has to be positive.
- `showCharacterCount: Boolean`: shows `count/maxLength` under the box while `maxLength` is set.
- `singleLine: Boolean`: whether the field holds one line, which scrolls sideways. It does unless told otherwise. A line break in `value` is then shown as a space, and `value` keeps it.
- `minLines: Int`: the least lines the box is tall, in a field of several.
- `maxLines: Int`: the most lines the box grows to before its text scrolls, in a field of several.
- `keyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions`: the keyboard's type, its capitals, its corrections and its action key.
- `keyboardActions: KeyboardActions`: what the keyboard's action key does, for the action `keyboardOptions` names.
- `visualTransformation: VisualTransformation`: how the text is shown, without changing it: `PasswordVisualTransformation()` draws a dot for each character.
- `contentType: ContentType?`: what the field holds, for the platform to fill it in.
- `style: FilledTextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: FilledTextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. A disabled field has no fill and is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `FilledTextField_<tagKey>`, and its clear button `FilledTextFieldClear_<tagKey>`.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

