## Package com.pantrixui.components.navigation.sidebar

### PantrixSidebar

`import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.sidebar.PantrixSidebar`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSidebar(
    groups: List<SidebarGroup>,
    selected: String?,
    onSelect: (String) -> Unit,
    expanded: Set<String>,
    onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    collapsed: Boolean = false,
    adaptive: Boolean = true,
    flyout: SidebarFlyout = SidebarFlyout.Popup,
    singleExpanded: Boolean = true,
    style: SidebarStyle? = null,
    colors: SidebarColors? = null,
    header: (@Composable SidebarSlotScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    footerItems: List<SidebarItem> = emptyList(),
    footer: (@Composable SidebarSlotScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label,
    titleTextStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.caption.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)
)
```

The column of destinations down the side of an app, with the sections of the app it holds.

A sidebar is two levels deep and no more: sections, and the destinations inside them. A section opens and closes in place, and by default opening one closes whichever was open (`singleExpanded`), so a sidebar of six sections stays the height of six rows and not of everything the app can show. The rows between the header and the pinned destinations scroll when there are more than fit.

`collapsed`, it is a rail of icons. A destination's icon then carries its name, which a tooltip shows, and a section opens what it holds beside the rail (`flyout`): a card, as a pointer rests on the section and at a press where there is no pointer, or a column of its own that moves the page over. Either goes once a destination in it is chosen, and it is where a row's `SidebarItem.detail` is written. A top-level row without an icon is drawn as a chevron on the rail: give every one an icon.

By default the sidebar takes the rail by itself where its column would crowd the page (`adaptive`): an unfolded foldable, a tablet held upright and a narrow window get the rail, a wide window the column. The header and the footer are told which it is, through `SidebarSlotScope.collapsed`.

Which destination is current and which sections are open are both the caller's state: navigation belongs to the app, and a sidebar that kept its own would fight the back button, a deep link and a restored process.

```kotlin
var where by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("crashes") }
var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("quality")) }
PantrixScaffold(
    sideBar = { insets ->
        PantrixSidebar(
            groups = groups,
            selected = where,
            onSelect = { where = it },
            expanded = open,
            onExpandedChange = { open = it },
            insets = insets,
            tagKey = "main"
        )
    }
) { padding -> Page(where, padding) }
```

The current destination is told three ways: its fill, a label a step heavier than the others, and its selected state for a screen reader. The section that holds it is written heavier too, and on the rail it has the fill and the bar on the rail's edge: a closed section still says where the app is. A section says to a screen reader whether it is open, and a closed one composes nothing of what it holds. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target, and grows with a larger type. Rows that do not fit scroll, with Pantrix's scroll bar along the sidebar's end where the reader has a pointer.

Parameters:

- `groups: List<SidebarGroup>`: the rows, in groups, in order. A line is drawn between one group and the next.
- `selected: String?`: the key of the destination the app is showing, or null where it shows none of them.
- `onSelect: (String) -> Unit`: called with the key of a destination that was pressed. The sidebar changes nothing by itself.
- `expanded: Set<String>`: the keys of the sections that are open in the column. The rail opens a section beside itself and keeps which by itself: nothing of it is the app's to restore.
- `onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit`: called with the keys that are to be open after a section of the column was pressed.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the sidebar's modifier. The sidebar is as wide as its style says, and wider by the `insets` at its sides, and as tall as the room it is given: its rows take what the header, the pinned destinations and the footer leave, and scroll inside it. Where the room has no end, inside a page that scrolls, it needs a height of its own.
- `collapsed: Boolean`: whether the sidebar is drawn as its rail, at any width. The shape changes at once, and the sidebar's width follows it over the theme's motion, the page beside it moving with it.
- `adaptive: Boolean`: whether the sidebar takes the rail by itself where the column would crowd the page: where the width it is offered, less the column's, is under the window's expanded breakpoint, 840dp unless the window's breakpoints say otherwise, below which a page has no room for two panes. False leaves the shape to `collapsed` alone: for a sidebar in a drawer, which covers the page and crowds nothing, or for an app that lets its user pin the column. It measures what it is offered, so it cannot be asked its intrinsic size: turn it off under a parent that is sized by `IntrinsicSize`.
- `flyout: SidebarFlyout`: what a section of the rail opens: `SidebarFlyout.Popup`, a card beside the section, or `SidebarFlyout.Panel`, a column beside the rail that moves the page over. The column opens its sections in place either way.
- `singleExpanded: Boolean`: whether opening a section of the column closes whichever was open.
- `style: SidebarStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SidebarColors?`: this sidebar's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest. What a rail's section opens is drawn in them too.
- `header: (@Composable SidebarSlotScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands above the rows and does not scroll: the app's mark, a workspace switcher. A line sets it off. It lays itself out for the width it has, by `SidebarSlotScope.collapsed`.
- `footerItems: List<SidebarItem>`: destinations pinned under the rows, below a line: settings, help. They are no sections: one that has children is refused.
- `footer: (@Composable SidebarSlotScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands at the very bottom and does not scroll, below `footerItems` and a line: an account, a plan. It lays itself out for the width it has, as the header does.
- `insets: PaddingValues`: the room the sidebar keeps clear at its edges while its fill runs behind it: what a scaffold gives its side bar, so that the rows stand clear of the system bars.
- `tagKey: String?`: the sidebar's automation key: the sidebar is `Sidebar_<tagKey>`, a destination in it `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Item_<key>` wherever it is shown, and a section `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Section_<key>`; what a rail's section opens is `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Flyout_<key>` or `Sidebar_<tagKey>.Panel_<key>`. A press is reported as a `Sidebar` event: `select` with the destination's key and whether the sidebar was its rail, `expand` and `collapse` with the section's.
- `textStyle: TextStyle`: the type a row's name is set in, in the column, in a section's and in what a rail's section opens: the theme's `label` unless given. The current destination and the section that holds it are set a step heavier than it. A colour in it is not a row's, which is the row's state's.
- `titleTextStyle: TextStyle`: the type a group's title is set in, in capitals: the theme's `caption`, bold, unless given. It is written in the sidebar's quiet colour whatever colour it holds.

What a section of a collapsed `PantrixSidebar`, its rail, opens to show its destinations.

Entries:

- `Popup`: A card beside the section, as tall as what it holds. Where there is a pointer it is up while the pointer rests on the section or on the card, so that moving down the rail reads each section in turn; a press without a pointer, a finger's, the keyboard's or a screen reader's, opens it with the keyboard in it, until it is dismissed.
- `Panel`: The section's destinations in a column of their own against the rail, the column's width and the rail's height: a part of the sidebar, which is wider by it, so that the page beside it moves over and is not covered. ### SidebarItem

`import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.sidebar.SidebarItem`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SidebarItem(
    public val key: String,
    public val label: String,
    public val icon: ImageVector? = null,
    public val children: List<SidebarItem> = emptyList(),
    public val detail: String? = null,
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
    public val tagKey: String? = null
)
```

One row of a `PantrixSidebar`: a destination, or a section with the destinations inside it.

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What the sidebar's `selected` holds and its `onSelect` reports, and what its `expanded` holds for a section. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen still knows where it is.
- `label: String`: The visible text, and the row's name for a screen reader.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: Drawn before the label, in the label's colour, or null for none. A screen reader passes over it.
- `children: List<SidebarItem>`: The destinations inside this row. A row that has any is a section and no destination itself: a press opens and closes it. A sidebar is two levels and no more, so a child's own children are not drawn.
- `detail: String?`: A number or a state beside the label, "87 open", "48.2M requests", or null for none. It is drawn in what a rail's section opens, where there is room for it. The column is a list of places to go, and a run of figures down its side would read as data.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the row can be pressed. One that cannot is written in the disabled text's colour. A section that cannot be pressed stays open or closed as the sidebar's `expanded` has it, and each destination inside it follows its own.
- `tagKey: String?`: The row's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: a destination is `Item_<tagKey>` and a section `Section_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a sidebar that has a key, as `Sidebar_main.Item_crashes`.

### SidebarStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.sidebar.SidebarStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SidebarStyle(
    public val width: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val collapsedWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val rowHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val childRowHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val collapsedIconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val childIndent: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val guideWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<SidebarStyle>
```

`PantrixSidebar`'s geometry: its width as a column and as a rail, its rows at both levels, and the line that says a section's destinations are inside it.

The column's width is the same on every platform: what a sidebar holds is the same, and one that changed its width would move the app's whole layout with it. The rows and the room in them follow the density; the widths, the icons, the indent, the corners, the line and the mark do not. A sidebar's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `SidebarColors` where a sidebar has its own.

Parameters:

- `width: Dp`: How wide the sidebar is as a column, and how wide the column a rail's section opens beside it: 248dp.
- `collapsedWidth: Dp`: How wide the sidebar is as a rail of icons: 76dp on Android and iOS, 68dp on desktop, 72dp on the web.
- `rowHeight: Dp`: The least height of a top-level row, a destination's or a section's: 44dp on Android and iOS, 36dp on desktop, 40dp on the web. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target.
- `childRowHeight: Dp`: The least height of a destination inside a section: 40dp on Android and iOS, 32dp on desktop, 36dp on the web. It is never lower than the platform's touch target either.
- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The corners of a row's fill: medium on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the sidebar's edge and a row's fill, and again between the fill's edge and what the row holds: 12dp on Android and iOS, 10dp on desktop and the web.
- `iconSize: Dp`: A row's icon, and a section's chevron: 20dp on Android and iOS, 18dp on desktop and the web.
- `collapsedIconSize: Dp`: A row's icon on the rail, where the icon is the row: 24dp on Android and iOS, 22dp on desktop and the web.
- `iconGap: Dp`: The room between a row's icon and its label: 12dp on Android and iOS, 10dp on desktop and the web.
- `childIndent: Dp`: How far a destination inside a section starts in from where its section does: 32dp on Android and iOS, 28dp on desktop and the web.
- `guideWidth: Dp`: How thick the line down an open section's destinations is: 1dp.
- `markerSize: Dp`: How thick the bar on the rail's edge is, beside the row the app is at: 4dp.

Documented on: [Sidebar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/sidebar.md)


What a `PantrixSidebar` is painted with, for a sidebar that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

A destination that is not the current one, and a section's chevron, are the theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own fill, and this colour on a fill of the caller's.

The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.commandpalette

### PantrixCommandPalette

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.commandpalette.PantrixCommandPalette`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixCommandPalette(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    commands: List<PantrixCommand>,
    onRun: (PantrixCommand) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    emptyText: String? = null,
    style: CommandPaletteStyle? = null,
    colors: CommandPaletteColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Every command of the app, found by its name and run from the keyboard: what Cmd+K or Ctrl+K opens.

The palette is modal, as a dialog is: a scrim over the app, the focus inside, and back, Escape and a click on the scrim asking to close. Whether it is shown is the caller's: give `visible`, and act on `onDismissRequest` and on `onRun`, which is where the palette is closed before the command does its work. It stands at the top of the window, where its field stays while the list under it grows and shrinks.

**Finding.** The field takes the focus as the palette opens, on a phone too, and keeps it while the list is walked. With nothing typed every command is listed, under its group. What is typed narrows the list to the commands whose label, group or keywords hold each word of it, compared in the theme's language; inside a group those whose label starts with it come first, and the letters found are marked. Each time it opens the field is empty.

**Running.** One command is highlighted, at first the first that can be run. The arrows down and up move the highlight over the commands that can be run and stop at the ends, Page Down and Page Up a page at a time, and the pointer moves it to the row it passes over. Enter, the keyboard's action and a press on a row run the command. A command that is not `enabled` is listed, faint, and is not run.

**Shortcuts.** A command's `PantrixCommand.shortcut` is written at its row's end as the system writes it. The palette opens by a shortcut of the app's, and the commands run by theirs, with `commandShortcuts` on the window's root.

**To a screen reader** the palette is announced by the theme's name for a list of commands. The highlighted row is selected, the groups are headings, and as what is typed narrows the list, the number of commands left is said.

```kotlin
var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
Box(Modifier.shortcutRoot().onShortcut(PantrixShortcut(Key.K, command = true)) { open = true }) {
    …
    PantrixCommandPalette(
        visible = open,
        onDismissRequest = { open = false },
        commands = commands,
        onRun = { command ->
            open = false
            run(command.key)
        },
        tagKey = "commands"
    )
}
```

Parameters:

- `visible: Boolean`: whether the palette is shown. It never hides itself.
- `onDismissRequest: () -> Unit`: called for back, Escape and a click on the scrim.
- `commands: List<PantrixCommand>`: every command, in the order they are listed under their groups. No two have one key.
- `onRun: (PantrixCommand) -> Unit`: called with the command run, by Enter, the keyboard's action or a press. Close the palette here.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the panel's modifier.
- `placeholder: String?`: what the empty field shows, or null for the theme's words for searching commands.
- `emptyText: String?`: what stands in the list's place while nothing matches, or null for the theme's words for it.
- `style: CommandPaletteStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: CommandPaletteColors?`: this palette's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the palette's automation key: the panel is `CommandPalette_<tagKey>`, its field `CommandPalette_<tagKey>.TextField_query` and a command's row `CommandPalette_<tagKey>.Command_<key>`. What is done is reported as a `CommandPalette` event: `open`, `dismiss` with `via` (`back` or `scrim`), and `run` with the command's key and `via` (`key` or `click`). What is typed is never reported.

Documented on: [Command Palette](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/command-palette.md)

### CommandPaletteStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.commandpalette.CommandPaletteStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class CommandPaletteStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val maxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val elevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val margin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val topSpace: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val itemHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val itemHorizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<CommandPaletteStyle>
```

`PantrixCommandPalette`'s geometry: the panel, where it stands, and the rows of its list.

No platform has a command palette of its own. The panel is a dialog's, its corners and its shadow as the platform's dialog has them, and the rows are the platform's list rows: 48dp on Android, 44pt on iOS and 36dp under a pointer. A row is never lower than the platform's touch target.

The panel stands at the top of the window, where a field that is typed in stays while the list under it grows and shrinks: below the margin on a phone, and lower on a desktop and the web, by `topSpace`.

The room, the rows' height and the gaps follow the density. The panel's size, its corners, its shadow and the icons do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The panel's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `maxWidth: Dp`: The widest the panel grows in a wide window.
- `maxHeight: Dp`: The tallest the panel grows in a tall window. A narrower window, and the keyboard, make it less.
- `elevation: Dp`: The panel's shadow. iOS sets a panel apart by the dimming alone.
- `margin: Dp`: The least room between the panel and the window's safe area.
- `topSpace: Dp`: The room above the panel, past `margin`.
- `itemHeight: Dp`: The least height of a command's row. A larger type makes it taller.
- `itemHorizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between a row's sides and what it holds, and a heading's.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The width and height of a command's icon.
- `iconGap: Dp`: Between a command's icon, its label and its shortcut.

Documented on: [Command Palette](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/command-palette.md)

### Modifier.commandShortcuts

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.commandpalette.commandShortcuts`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
fun Modifier.commandShortcuts(
    commands: List<PantrixCommand>,
    onRun: (PantrixCommand) -> Unit
): Modifier
```

Runs each command of `commands` that has a shortcut by that shortcut, by `onRun`, while the focus is on this node or inside it: the one list of commands is what the palette shows and what the keyboard runs.

A command that is not `enabled` lets its keys through. Of two commands with one shortcut, the first one runs. Put it on a window's root with `shortcutRoot`, which holds the focus while nothing else does, so that the shortcuts are heard then too:

```kotlin
Box(Modifier.shortcutRoot().commandShortcuts(commands, onRun = { run(it.key) })) { … }
```

While a palette or another modal of Pantrix's is open, the keys are its own, and these shortcuts are not heard.

Parameters:

- `commands: List<PantrixCommand>`: the commands, as the palette is given them.
- `onRun: (PantrixCommand) -> Unit`: called with the command whose shortcut was pressed.

### PantrixCommand

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.commandpalette.PantrixCommand`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PantrixCommand(
    public val key: String,
    public val label: String,
    public val group: String? = null,
    public val icon: ImageVector? = null,
    public val shortcut: PantrixShortcut? = null,
    public val keywords: List<String> = emptyList(),
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
    public val tagKey: String? = null,
    public val supportingText: String? = null
)
```

One command of a `PantrixCommandPalette`: what the user reads, where it is listed, and what else finds it.

```kotlin
PantrixCommand(
    key = "rename",
    label = stringResource(Res.string.rename),
    group = stringResource(Res.string.file),
    shortcut = PantrixShortcut(Key.R, command = true)
)
```

Parameters:

- `key: String`: the command's own key, the same in every language: what `PantrixCommandPalette`'s `onRun` and its `run` event are given, and its row's automation key unless `tagKey` is given. No two commands of a palette have one key.
- `label: String`: what the command does, as the user reads it.
- `group: String?`: the heading the command is listed under, or null for one listed under none.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: drawn before the label.
- `shortcut: PantrixShortcut?`: the keys that run the same thing, written at the row's end as the system writes them. Binding them is `Modifier.commandShortcuts`'s.
- `keywords: List<String>`: other words that find the command: what another app calls it, a word a user types for it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the command can be run now. One that cannot is listed, faint, and the arrows pass it by.
- `tagKey: String?`: the row's automation key, where it is not `key`.
- `supportingText: String?`: a second line under the label, smaller and quieter: what the command opens or where it leads. A screen reader hears it after the label, and a search finds the command by it, as by a keyword.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.common

### OverlayPresentation

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.common.OverlayPresentation`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class OverlayPresentation
```

How an overlay that belongs to a control is shown: beside the control, or as a sheet from the bottom of the window.

A popover beside what was pressed suits a window with room around the control, and a pointer. On a phone the same overlay is small under a finger and hides the screen's middle; a sheet from the bottom edge is within the thumb's reach and as wide as the window.

Entries:

- `Adaptive`: A sheet in a narrow window, the `Compact` width class, and a popover in every wider one. The window is the one the overlay is shown over, not the room of a pane it was opened in, and it is asked as the overlay opens: one that is open stays as it is when the window changes, and the next one is shown by the window as it is then.
- `Popover`: A popover beside the control, in every window.
- `Sheet`: A sheet from the bottom edge of the window, in every window.

Documented on: [Menu](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/menu.md), [Popover](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/popover.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.dialog

### PantrixDialog

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.dialog.PantrixDialog`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDialog(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    title: String? = null,
    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    message: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    dismissible: Boolean = true,
    style: DialogStyle? = null,
    colors: DialogColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null
)
```

A decision or a message that stops the app until the user deals with it.

The dialog sits in the middle of the window, above a scrim, and is modal on every platform: nothing behind it takes a click, Tab never leaves it, and on Android TalkBack stays inside it. It is shown while `visible` is true and enters and leaves with the theme's motion; it never hides itself. Back, Escape and a click on the scrim call `onDismissRequest` unless `dismissible` is false. The actions the caller puts in `actions` call only their own `onClick`: an action that ends the dialog sets `visible` to false there.

A keyboard user starts on the first control, usually the first action, so put the safe choice first: "Cancel" before "Delete". The title is announced when the dialog appears and is its heading. A dialog without one, a `title` that is null or blank, has nothing in its place: what it holds starts at the top.

**Close it to see it leave.** A dialog that has closed composes nothing, so leaving it in the tree with `visible = false` is free, and it leaves with the theme's motion. An open one that is taken out of the composition is gone without it, and that is all it costs: its window is composed at the root of the window around it, so a layout that throws its content away while it measures closes no layer that is still being measured.

It looks the same on every platform; what differs is in `DialogStyle`: the corners, the widths and the shadow. A dialog of a title, a message and actions is as wide as its widest part, between the style's two widths: a short question is narrow, and a long message wraps at the widest. A dialog that holds `content` is as wide as it may be, so that a field or a list in it has room.

Parameters:

- `visible: Boolean`: whether the dialog is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.
- `onDismissRequest: () -> Unit`: called for back, Escape and a click on the scrim while `dismissible`. The dialog stays until `visible` is false.
- `title: String?`: what the dialog is about, as a short question or statement: "Delete this file?". Null or blank for none: no line is kept for it, and a screen reader announces no name when the dialog appears.
- `actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit`: end-aligned buttons, which wrap onto another line when they do not fit. They keep their own test tags.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the dialog itself. The margin it keeps to the window is no part of it.
- `message: String?`: the explanation under the title. It scrolls with `content` when the window is short.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: a decorative icon above the title, which then centres.
- `dismissible: Boolean`: whether back, Escape and a click on the scrim ask to close. Turn it off only when the user must choose one of `actions`.
- `style: DialogStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: DialogColors?`: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the dialog's tag is `Dialog_<tagKey>`, on the dialog as it is drawn.
- `content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)?`: anything else the dialog holds, under the message: a form field, a list of choices.

Documented on: [Dialog](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/dialog.md)

`PantrixDialog`'s geometry.

The padding and the gaps between the title, the message and the actions come from the theme's spacing, so they follow density, and so do the narrowest width and the margin. The widest width, the corners, the shadow and the icon do not. A dialog's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `DialogColors` where a call has its own.

Parameters:

- `elevation: Dp`: How high the dialog floats over the scrim, which is how large its shadow is. None on iOS.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The size of the icon above the title.

Shows over an app what its theme's diagnostics have found: a button with the number of findings, and on its press a sheet that lists them, each with its check, where it was found and what puts it right. A finding chosen in the list is outlined where its node stands, until the screen is next pressed. While nothing has been found, nothing is shown.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.menu

### PantrixMenu

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.menu.PantrixMenu`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixMenu(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    anchor: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    side: PopoverSide = PopoverSide.Bottom,
    alignment: PopoverAlignment = PopoverAlignment.Start,
    style: MenuStyle? = null,
    colors: MenuColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    presentation: OverlayPresentation = OverlayPresentation.Adaptive,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A list of actions for one element, in a panel beside it: what a "more" button opens, or the actions of a row.

It is anchored, not modal: nothing is dimmed, the app stays in view around it, and the panel follows its anchor as the content moves. It sits on `side` of the anchor, lined up as `alignment` says, while the window has room for it there, and takes the opposite side otherwise, never closer than the style's margin to the edges of the window, its system bars or the keyboard. It is as wide as its longest row, between the style's narrowest and widest, and more rows than fit its tallest height scroll.

The menu never hides itself. A press outside it, Escape and back call `onDismissRequest`, and so does the choosing of a row, before the row's own `onClick`: a row says what it does and nothing about the menu. The caller sets `visible` to false. The first press outside only asks to close: what is under it is not pressed.

Opened by the keyboard it takes the focus on its first row. The arrows walk the rows and go round from the last to the first, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Tab walks them as well, the rows being the only stops in the panel. Enter and the space bar choose the row, and Escape closes the menu. Opened by a touch or a click no row shows the focus, and the first of those keys brings the keyboard into use: an arrow down or Home on the first row, an arrow up or End on the last. Once the menu has closed the focus is on the anchor, on the control that opened it. While it is shown the app under it shows no focus, as under a dialog.

It looks the same on every platform; what differs is in `MenuStyle`: the corners, the widths, the shadow and the rows' height.

**In a narrow window it is a sheet** (`presentation`): on a phone a panel beside a button is small under a finger, and a sheet from the bottom edge is within the thumb's reach. The rows are as wide as the sheet and as tall as the platform's touch target, there is no title, and a drag down or a press on the scrim closes it as anything outside the panel does. A destructive row keeps its colour; a shortcut is not written where the platform is used by touch, which has no keys to press. The keyboard walks the rows as in the panel.

Parameters:

- `visible: Boolean`: whether the menu is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.
- `onDismissRequest: () -> Unit`: called for a press outside, Escape, back and a row that is chosen. The menu stays until `visible` is false.
- `anchor: @Composable () -> Unit`: the control the menu belongs to, laid out where this is called and as that place asks: usually the button that opens it.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the panel, inside its layer. Not to the anchor.
- `side: PopoverSide`: the side of the anchor the panel prefers. `PopoverSide.Start` and `PopoverSide.End` follow the layout direction.
- `alignment: PopoverAlignment`: how the panel lines up with the anchor along that side: from its start edge unless told otherwise, as a menu hangs from what opened it.
- `style: MenuStyle?`: this call's own style, which its rows are drawn with too: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: MenuColors?`: this call's own colours, its rows' among them. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the panel's tag is `Menu_<tagKey>`, and its rows are named inside it, `Menu_<tagKey>.MenuItem_<row's key>`. A menu shown as a sheet has the same tags, on the sheet.
- `presentation: OverlayPresentation`: how the menu is shown: a sheet in a narrow window and a panel beside its anchor in a wider one, by default; always the panel, or always the sheet. Chosen as the menu opens, it stays until it has closed.
- `content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit`: the rows: `PantrixMenuItem`s, with a `PantrixDivider` between groups of them. Given no colour, that line is told by the rows' colour on a fill, as the panel's hairline is.

Documented on: [Menu](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/menu.md)

### PantrixMenuItem

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.menu.PantrixMenuItem`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixMenuItem(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    icon: ImageVector? = null,
    shortcut: String? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    destructive: Boolean = false,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    selected: Boolean = false,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    supportingTextStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
)
```

One action in a `PantrixMenu`: a label, an optional icon before it and an optional shortcut after it. Among rows that each choose one thing, a language or an order, the one in effect is `selected`, with a check at its end.

Choosing it asks the menu to close and then calls `onClick`. It is at least as tall as the style's row and as the platform's touch target, and its label is cut at one line where the panel is at its widest.

Parameters:

- `text: String`: what the action does, in a word or two.
- `onClick: () -> Unit`: called when the row is chosen, after the menu has been asked to close.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the row.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: drawn before the label, at the style's icon size and in the label's colour. A picture of what the label says: a screen reader is told the label alone.
- `shortcut: String?`: the keys that do the same thing, such as "Ctrl+K", after the label. It is shown and read out, never bound: binding the keys is the app's.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the row can be chosen. One that cannot takes no press and no focus, and reports nothing.
- `destructive: Boolean`: draws the label and the icon in the menu's destructive colour, for an action that deletes or cannot be undone.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the row's tag is `MenuItem_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of a menu that has a key of its own.
- `selected: Boolean`: whether the row is the choice in effect among rows that each choose one thing: a check stands at its end, in the label's colour, and a screen reader is told it is selected.
- `supportingText: String?`: a second line under the label, smaller and in the shortcut's quieter colour: what the choice leads to, as a language's address under its name. The row grows to hold it, and a screen reader hears it after the label. It is cut at two lines.
- `supportingTextStyle: TextStyle`: the type `supportingText` is set in: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Its colour stays the row's, quieter than the label and the disabled colour on a row that cannot be chosen.

Documented on: [Menu](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/menu.md)

### MenuStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.menu.MenuStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class MenuStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val minWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val elevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val margin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val itemHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val itemHorizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<MenuStyle>
```

`PantrixMenu`'s geometry: the panel it draws, how far that sits from its anchor and from the edges of the window, and the rows in it.

The air follows density: the gap, the margin, the padding above the first row and below the last, a row's height and the padding and the gap inside it, and the narrowest width. The widest width, the tallest height, the corners, the shadow and the icon do not. A row is never shorter than the platform's touch target, whatever the density. A menu's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `MenuColors` where a call has its own.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The panel's corners: medium on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.
- `minWidth: Dp`: The narrowest the panel gets, however short its labels.
- `maxWidth: Dp`: The widest the panel gets: a longer label is cut short.
- `maxHeight: Dp`: The tallest the panel gets: more rows than fit scroll.
- `elevation: Dp`: How high the panel floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the anchor and the panel.
- `margin: Dp`: Kept clear between the panel and the edges of the window, and of what covers the window there: a system bar, a cutout, the keyboard.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: Above the first row and below the last.
- `itemHeight: Dp`: The least a row is tall, where the platform's touch target is not taller.
- `itemHorizontalPadding: Dp`: Inside a row, before its icon and after its shortcut.
- `iconSize: Dp`: A row's icon.
- `iconGap: Dp`: Between a row's icon and its label, and between its label and its shortcut.

Documented on: [Menu](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/menu.md)

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.menu.MenuColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
    public val border: Color = Color.Unspecified
```

What a `PantrixMenu` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.


A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the rows, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give, and so is a `destructive` colour that reads on it.

Parameters:

The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has. A transparent colour draws none.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.modal

### ModalPosition

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.modal.ModalPosition`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ModalPosition
```

Where `PantrixModal`'s content sits in the window, which also says how it enters and leaves.

Entries:

- `Center`: In the middle of the window's safe area, fading and growing in, as a dialog does.
- `Top`: Near the top of the window's safe area, in the middle across, fading and growing in: a search or a palette, whose field stays where it is while what is under it grows and shrinks.

Documented on: [Modal](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/modal.md)

### PantrixModal

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.modal.PantrixModal`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixModal(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    position: ModalPosition = ModalPosition.Center,
    margin: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(PantrixTheme.spacing.xl),
    paneTitle: String? = null,
    dismissOnScrimClick: Boolean = true,
    dismissOnBack: Boolean = true,
    scrimColor: Color = PantrixTheme.colors.scrim,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)
```

A modal layer of the app's own: a scrim over the whole window, and over it content the app draws, with everything a modal of Pantrix does. It is what `PantrixDialog` and `PantrixCommandPalette` stand on, for a layer neither of them draws: a search with filters of its own, a picture shown large, an editor that fills a phone.

```kotlin
var searching by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixModal(
    visible = searching,
    onDismissRequest = { searching = false },
    position = ModalPosition.Top,
    paneTitle = stringResource(Res.string.search)
) {
    PantrixSurface(Modifier.widthIn(max = 640.dp), shape = PantrixTheme.shapes.lg) { SearchPanel() }
}
```

The modal never hides itself. Back, Escape and a press on the scrim call `onDismissRequest`, and the caller sets `visible` to false; the content leaves with the theme's motion, and once it has gone nothing of the modal is composed. It enters a frame after its window has first drawn, so that the motion is seen.

Focus follows the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern. Opened from the keyboard, the modal moves the focus to the first control of the content, and Tab then goes round inside it and never reaches the app under it; opened by touch, the focus stays where it was, so that no software keyboard rises unasked. Once the modal has closed the focus is where it was. Under the modal the app draws no focus ring. A screen reader hears `paneTitle` as the modal appears, then the content, and last the scrim, as one action called by the theme's word for closing where a press on it dismisses.

The modal gives its content no fill, no shape and no width: the content draws itself, as large as it is, in the room `margin` leaves. Where a fold divides the window, the content keeps to the half it was opened from; opened inside a `PantrixWindowFrame`, the modal takes the frame for its window.

Parameters:

- `visible: Boolean`: whether the modal is shown. Set to false, the content leaves with its motion, and then nothing is composed.
- `onDismissRequest: () -> Unit`: called when the user asks to close the modal: back, Escape, or a press on the scrim.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the content, inside `margin`: the node it tags is the content as it is drawn, and a press anywhere on it is the content's, never the scrim's.
- `position: ModalPosition`: where the content sits: in the middle of the window, or near its top.
- `margin: PaddingValues`: the room kept between the content and the window's safe area, side by side. It is part of the scrim: a press in it, right beside the content, dismisses as one anywhere else on the scrim does. None, with content that fills what it is given, makes the content the whole safe area, as an editor on a phone is.
- `paneTitle: String?`: what a screen reader announces as the modal appears: what it is, in a word or two.
- `dismissOnScrimClick: Boolean`: whether a press on the scrim asks to dismiss. Where it does not, the scrim is a fill a screen reader passes over.
- `dismissOnBack: Boolean`: whether back and Escape ask to dismiss.
- `scrimColor: Color`: what is drawn over the app while the modal is shown, fading with the content: the theme's scrim unless given. The theme's background makes the modal a page of its own, the window's bars and all.
- `tagKey: String?`: the modal's automation key: the content is `Modal_<tagKey>`. A dismissal is reported as a `Modal` event, `dismiss`, which says whether it came by the scrim or by back.
- `content: @Composable () -> Unit`: what the modal shows, drawn by the app.

Documented on: [Modal](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/modal.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.multiselect

### PantrixMultiSelect

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.multiselect.PantrixMultiSelect`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixMultiSelect(
    options: List<SelectOption<T>>,
    selected: Set<T>,
    onSelectionChange: (Set<T>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    valueText: String? = null,
    searchable: Boolean = false,
    searchPlaceholder: String? = null,
    style: SelectStyle? = null,
    fieldStyle: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: SelectColors? = null,
    fieldColors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    presentation: OverlayPresentation = OverlayPresentation.Popover
)
```

Several choices out of a list the control opens: the projects a page is narrowed to, the days a shop is open.

It is a `PantrixSelect` whose list takes several choices. The box is a text field's, with a chevron at its end and a field's label, placeholder, error and supporting text, and the list opens under it, as wide as the box. Every option is a check box: a press ticks it or clears it, and the list stays open for the next. A press outside the list, Escape and back close it. What is chosen is its caller's and not the control's: it is given `selected` and asks for another set with `onSelectionChange`.

The box shows the labels of what is chosen, in the options' order with a comma between them and cut at one line, or `valueText` where a caller would rather say it another way: a count, or one word for all of them. With nothing chosen it shows its placeholder. Asked how wide it would be, as `Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max)` asks, it answers as a `PantrixSelect` does, with what the longest of its options needs, whatever is chosen.

The keyboard is a select's. Opened by the keyboard the list takes the focus on the first chosen option, or on its first; the arrows walk the options and go round, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Enter and the space bar tick or clear. With `searchable` the list has a field that narrows the options, at its edge nearest the box: at its top under the box, at its foot where the list opens above it. The focus stays in that field, and the keyboard's action ticks or clears the marked option.

It shares a select's style and colours, `SelectStyle` and `SelectColors`, and a text field's for its box: a product that restyles its selects restyles these with them.

Parameters:

- `options: List<SelectOption<T>>`: the choices, in the order they are shown. With none, the list says so.
- `selected: Set<T>`: the values that are chosen now: every option whose value is among them is ticked.
- `onSelectionChange: (Set<T>) -> Unit`: asked for another set, with the whole of it: the one before with the pressed option's value put in or taken out.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the list can be opened. One that cannot be takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `label: String?`: what the choice is, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and what its list is announced as.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while nothing is chosen.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the choice is wrong: the border, the label and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.
- `valueText: String?`: what the box shows while something is chosen, in place of the chosen labels.
- `searchable: Boolean`: whether the list has a field to search its options by.
- `searchPlaceholder: String?`: what the search field shows while it is empty, and what it is called. The theme's word for a search where it is null.
- `style: SelectStyle?`: this call's own `SelectStyle`, the one its list is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `fieldStyle: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own `TextFieldStyle`, the one its box is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SelectColors?`: its list's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's. The check boxes are the theme's.
- `fieldColors: TextFieldColors?`: its box's own colours, as a text field takes them. A disabled one is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `MultiSelect_<tagKey>`, its list `MultiSelectList_<tagKey>`, the list's search field `MultiSelectSearch_<tagKey>`, and its options are named inside it, `MultiSelect_<tagKey>.MultiSelectOption_<option's key>`. It reports that its list opened and that an option was ticked or cleared, by the option's key and never by its label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `presentation: OverlayPresentation`: how the list is shown: under the field, by default; as a sheet from the bottom of the window, its title the field's label; or the one in a narrow window and the other in a wider one. Chosen as the list opens, it stays until the list has closed.

### PantrixMultiSelect

A multi select bound to a form's field: its choices, its error and its name come from `field`.

A tick or a clearing changes the field and marks it touched, so a rule's message shows after the first of them, or when the form is submitted, and not on a form nobody has touched. While the field is in error the message takes the place of `supportingText`, rather than standing beside it. The field's id is the automation key, `MultiSelect_<id>`, with its options inside it, and the form can send the focus here when it is submitted with this field in error.

It is an overload of its own and not a parameter of the controlled form, so that a set and a field cannot both be given.

- `fieldColors: TextFieldColors?`: its box's own colours, as a text field takes them.

- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover

### PantrixPopover

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PantrixPopover`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixPopover(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    anchor: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    side: PopoverSide = PopoverSide.Bottom,
    alignment: PopoverAlignment = PopoverAlignment.Center,
    title: String? = null,
    dismissible: Boolean = true,
    style: PopoverStyle? = null,
    colors: PopoverColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    presentation: OverlayPresentation = OverlayPresentation.Popover,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A layer beside an element, holding more about it than the element itself can show: what a status means, what a field expects, a few controls for one row.

It is anchored, not modal: nothing is dimmed, the app stays in view around it, and the popover follows its anchor as the content moves. It sits on `side` of the anchor while the window has room for it there and on the opposite side otherwise, lined up as `alignment` says, and never closer than the style's margin to the edges of the window, its system bars or the keyboard. It is no larger than that room either: what it holds wraps, and scrolls under the title.

The popover never hides itself. A press outside it, Escape and back call `onDismissRequest` unless `dismissible` is false, and the caller sets `visible` to false. The first press outside only asks to close: what is under it is not pressed, so a press on the anchor closes the popover and does not open it again. Once it is told to close it is in no one's way: a press while it fades is the app's.

Opened by the keyboard it takes the focus: its first control does, or the popover itself where it holds none, and then the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, the space bar, Home and End scroll what it holds. Opened by a touch or a click it leaves the focus where it was, and takes it once the keyboard comes into use. Tab stays inside it, and once it has closed the focus is on the anchor: on the control that opened it. While it is shown the app under it shows no focus, as under a dialog.

**Close it to see it leave.** A popover that has closed composes nothing but its anchor, so leaving it in the tree with `visible = false` is free, and it leaves with the theme's motion. An open one that is taken out of the composition is gone without it, and that is all it costs: its layer is composed at the root of its window, so a layout that throws its content away while it measures, such as a `BoxWithConstraints` that changes branch, closes no layer that the window is still measuring.

It looks the same on every platform; what differs is in `PopoverStyle`: the corners, the widths and the shadow.

Parameters:

- `visible: Boolean`: whether the popover is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.
- `onDismissRequest: () -> Unit`: called for a press outside, Escape and back while `dismissible`. The popover stays until `visible` is false.
- `anchor: @Composable () -> Unit`: what the popover is placed beside: the control that opens it, laid out where this is called and as that place asks. The popover is placed against its layout box, the room of its touch target included.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the popover itself, inside its layer. Not to the anchor.
- `side: PopoverSide`: the side of the anchor the popover prefers. `PopoverSide.Start` and `PopoverSide.End` follow the layout direction.
- `alignment: PopoverAlignment`: how the popover lines up with the anchor along that side.
- `title: String?`: a heading at the top of the popover, which stays in view while what is under it scrolls, and what a screen reader announces as the popover appears. Give one to a popover of more than a line.
- `dismissible: Boolean`: whether a press outside, Escape, back and a screen reader's dismiss action ask to close. Turn it off only for a popover that something in `content` closes.
- `style: PopoverStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: PopoverColors?`: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the popover's tag is `Popover_<tagKey>`, on the popover as it is drawn, and on the sheet where it is shown as one.
- `presentation: OverlayPresentation`: how the popover is shown: beside its anchor, by default; as a sheet from the bottom of the window, the `title` its heading and `content` under it with the popover's own padding at its sides; or the one in a narrow window and the other in a wider one. Chosen as it opens, it stays until it has closed.
- `content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit`: what the popover holds, in a column under the title.

Documented on: [Popover](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/popover.md)

### PopoverSide

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PopoverSide`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class PopoverSide
```

Which side of its anchor a popover prefers. It takes the opposite side where the window has no room for it.

Entries:

- `Top`: Over the anchor.
- `Bottom`: Under the anchor.
- `Start`: The start edge: the left in a left-to-right layout, the right in a right-to-left one.
- `End`: The end edge: the right in a left-to-right layout, the left in a right-to-left one.

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PopoverAlignment`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class PopoverAlignment
```

How a popover lines up with its anchor along the side it sits on.

Entries:

- `Start`: Their start edges meet, or their top edges where the popover is beside its anchor.
- `Center`: Centred on the anchor.
- `End`: Their end edges meet, or their bottom edges where the popover is beside its anchor.

### PopoverStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PopoverStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PopoverStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val minWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val elevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val margin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<PopoverStyle>
```

`PantrixPopover`'s geometry: how wide and tall it gets, how far it sits from its anchor and how close it comes to the edges of the window.

The padding inside it and the gaps between what it holds come from the theme's spacing, so they follow density, and so do the gap, the margin and the narrowest width. The widest width, the tallest height, the corners and the shadow do not. A popover's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `PopoverColors` where a call has its own.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The popover's corners: medium on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.
- `minWidth: Dp`: The narrowest the popover gets, however little it holds.
- `maxWidth: Dp`: The widest the popover gets: longer text wraps.
- `maxHeight: Dp`: The tallest the popover gets: what it holds scrolls beyond this, under the title.
- `elevation: Dp`: How high the popover floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the anchor and the popover.
- `margin: Dp`: Kept clear between the popover and the edges of the window, and of what covers the window there: a system bar, a cutout, the keyboard.

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PopoverColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val title: Color = Color.Unspecified,
```

What a `PantrixPopover` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.


A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what the popover holds, and for the title unless a title colour is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The popover's fill. The theme's `surface`.
- `title: Color`: The title. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `border: Color`: The hairline around the popover, which tells it from a surface of its own colour under it, as in the dark theme, where a shadow shows little. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `title`: the edge a subtle button has. A transparent colour draws none.

### SelectOption

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.select.SelectOption`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SelectOption<out T>(
    public val value: T,
    public val label: String,
    public val icon: ImageVector? = null,
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
```

One option of a `PantrixSelect`, and of a `PantrixMultiSelect`: the value it stands for, its label, and a key for automation.

Parameters:

- `value: T`: What the select gives to its caller when the option is chosen, and compares with what is chosen by `==`.
- `label: String`: The visible text, the option's name for a screen reader, and what a search looks in.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: Drawn before the label, in the label's colour, or null for none. A screen reader passes over it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the option can be chosen. One that cannot is drawn in the disabled colour, takes no press, and is passed over by the keyboard. It stays in the list: what cannot be chosen is still there to be read.

In a multi select it is `MultiSelectOption_<tagKey>`, inside `MultiSelect_<the control's key>`.

### PantrixSelect

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.select.PantrixSelect`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> PantrixSelect(
    options: List<SelectOption<T>>,
    selected: T?,
    onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    searchable: Boolean = false,
    searchPlaceholder: String? = null,
    style: SelectStyle? = null,
    fieldStyle: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: SelectColors? = null,
    fieldColors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
    presentation: OverlayPresentation = OverlayPresentation.Popover
)
```

One choice out of a list the control opens: a country, a currency, a plan.

It is a text field's box with a chevron at its end, with a field's label, placeholder, error and supporting text, and a list that opens under the box, as wide as the box. What is chosen is its caller's and not the control's: it is given `selected` and asks for another with `onSelect`. A press on the field opens the list, and so do Enter and the space bar while the field has the focus. Choosing an option closes it, and so do a press outside it, Escape and back, which choose nothing. While the list is open the box is drawn as a field with the focus.

By itself the field is as wide as a text field, and its box grows with a choice longer than that. Asked how wide it would be, it answers with what the longest of its options needs, in the box and in a row of the list, with its placeholder and its label: `Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max)` makes a select that is no wider than its options and as wide whichever of them is chosen, as one in a toolbar or in a table's foot is.

The list hangs under the box, over the field's help where it has any, never closer than the style's margin to the edges of the window, its system bars or the keyboard. It opens there where the room holds three of its rows, or all of them where it has fewer, and is as tall as that room at the most, its rows scrolling. With less room than that it opens above the box, and with too little on both sides it lies over the box. Once open it stays on its side while one of its rows has room there: the keyboard, which comes as the list is used, makes it shorter where it is. More options than fit its tallest height scroll, and it opens with the chosen one in view. That option is marked by its row's fill and a tick, and not by a colour alone.

Opened by the keyboard the list takes the focus on the chosen option, or on its first. The arrows walk the options and go round from the last to the first, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Enter and the space bar choose. Opened by a touch or a click no option shows the focus, and the first arrow moves on from the chosen one. Once the list has closed the focus is on the field again.

With `searchable` the list has a field that narrows the options to those whose label holds what is typed, and the list is as short as the options that are left. The field is at the list's edge next to the box, its top, or its bottom where the list is above the box, so that it stays where it is while the list gets shorter. The focus stays in that field: the arrows move a mark among the options that match, and the keyboard's action chooses the marked one, which is the first match as soon as something is typed.

Use it for a list short enough to read, or one worth searching. Two or three choices that should all be in view are a radio group or a segment button, actions are a menu, and several values at once are a `PantrixMultiSelect`.

Parameters:

- `options: List<SelectOption<T>>`: the choices, in the order they are shown. With none, the list says so.
- `selected: T?`: what is chosen now: the first option whose value it equals. A value no option has is nothing chosen, and so is null, unless an option stands for it.
- `onSelect: (T) -> Unit`: asked for another choice, with the option's value. It is asked for the chosen one again too.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it. `fillMaxWidth()` fills a form's column, and `width(IntrinsicSize.Max)` is as wide as the options need.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the list can be opened. A select that cannot be takes no focus, is drawn in the disabled colours and says so.
- `label: String?`: what the choice is, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and what its list is announced as.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while nothing is chosen.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right, which a screen reader announces as the error.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the choice is wrong: the border, the label and the supporting text turn to the danger role, and a screen reader is told.
- `searchable: Boolean`: whether the list has a field to search its options by.
- `searchPlaceholder: String?`: what the search field shows while it is empty, and what it is called. The theme's word for a search where it is null.
- `style: SelectStyle?`: this call's own style, the one its list is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `fieldStyle: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own `TextFieldStyle`, the one its box is drawn with: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SelectColors?`: its list's own colours, in place of the theme's roles: the ones it sets are used, and the rest stay the theme's.
- `fieldColors: TextFieldColors?`: its box's own colours, as a text field takes them. A disabled select is drawn in the theme's disabled colours whatever is given.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field: its name where it has no `label`, as a select in a toolbar has none.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `Select_<tagKey>`, its list `SelectList_<tagKey>`, the list's search field `SelectSearch_<tagKey>`, and its options are named inside it, `Select_<tagKey>.SelectOption_<option's key>`. It reports that its list opened and that an option was chosen, by the option's key and never by its label.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses. It keeps a source of its own when this is null.
- `presentation: OverlayPresentation`: how the list is shown: under the field, by default; as a sheet from the bottom of the window, its title the field's label; or the one in a narrow window and the other in a wider one. Chosen as the list opens, it stays until the list has closed.

### SelectStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.select.SelectStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SelectStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val maxHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val elevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val margin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val itemHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<SelectStyle>
```

The list a `PantrixSelect` opens: the panel it is drawn in, how far that sits from the box it belongs to and from the edges of the window, and its rows.

The box is no part of it: a select's box is a text field's box, and is drawn by `TextFieldStyle`. The list is as wide as the box, whatever this style says, and has the box's corners unless a product gives it its own.

The air follows density: the gap, the margin, the padding above the first row and below the last, a row's height and the padding and the gap inside it. The tallest height, the corners, the shadow and the icon do not. A row is never shorter than the platform's touch target, whatever the density. A list's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `SelectColors` where a call has its own.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The panel's corners: the medium step of the shape scale on every platform, as the box's are.
- `maxHeight: Dp`: The tallest the panel gets: more options than fit scroll.
- `elevation: Dp`: How high the panel floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the box and its list.
- `margin: Dp`: Kept clear between the panel and the edges of the window, and of what covers the window there: a system bar, a cutout, the keyboard.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: Above the first row and below the last.
- `itemHeight: Dp`: The least a row is tall, where the platform's touch target is not taller.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: From the panel's edge to what a row starts with, and from what it ends with to the other edge. Each preset has the text field's own, so that an option's label starts where the box's text does.
- `iconSize: Dp`: An option's icon, and the tick beside the chosen one.
- `iconGap: Dp`: Between a row's parts: its check box, its icon, its label and its tick.

```kotlin
data class SelectColors(

    public val selectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,

```

What the list of a `PantrixSelect` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's. The box's colours are `TextFieldColors`.

```kotlin

```

A `container` or a `selectedContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what is written on it, unless that is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The panel's fill. The theme's `surface`.
- `content: Color`: An option's label and icon. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `selectedContainer: Color`: The fill of the chosen option's row, in a select of one choice. The primary role's container. A select of several marks its choices with check boxes, and fills no row.
- `selectedContent: Color`: The chosen option's label, its icon and the tick beside it, in a select of one choice. The primary role's `onContainer`.
- `border: Color`: The hairline around the panel, which tells it from a surface of its own colour under it, as in the dark theme, where a shadow shows little, and the line between the rows and the field a list is searched by. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has. A transparent colour draws none.
