## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.sheet

### PantrixSheet

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.sheet.PantrixSheet`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSheet(
    visible: Boolean,
    onDismissRequest: () -> Unit,
    title: String? = null,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    edge: SheetEdge = SheetEdge.Bottom,
    dismissible: Boolean = true,
    halfOpen: Boolean = false,
    fullScreen: Boolean = false,
    coverStatusBar: Boolean = false,
    overscrollMovesSheet: Boolean = true,
    scrollContent: Boolean = true,
    style: SheetStyle? = null,
    colors: SheetColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A panel over the app for a short task that belongs to the current screen: choosing how to sort, where to share, a field or two, a list to pick from, the details of what was pressed.

It lies along the `edge` it is given. Along the bottom edge it is as wide as the window up to the style's `maxWidth` and as tall as what it holds, and a drag moves it. Along the end edge it is a side sheet: as tall as the window and the style's `sideWidth` wide, with a button to close it, and a drag towards the edge closes it. It is modal either way: nothing behind it takes a click, Tab never leaves it, and on Android TalkBack stays inside it. It is shown while `visible` is true and enters and leaves with the theme's motion; it never hides itself. Back, Escape, a click on the scrim, a drag towards its edge and the side sheet's close button call `onDismissRequest` unless `dismissible` is false, and so does a screen reader's dismiss action on a full-screen sheet, which can cover the scrim.

The content spans the sheet's width, so the rows of a list reach its edges; give a form its own horizontal padding. It scrolls under the title when the sheet is too short for it. A long list belongs in a `LazyColumn`, with `scrollContent` off.

**Close it to see it leave.** A sheet that has closed composes nothing, so leaving it in the tree with `visible = false` is free, and it leaves with the theme's motion. An open one that is taken out of the composition is gone without it, and that is all it costs: its window is composed at the root of the window around it, so a layout that throws its content away while it measures closes no layer that is still being measured.

Parameters:

- `visible: Boolean`: whether the sheet is shown. It enters and leaves with the theme's motion.
- `onDismissRequest: () -> Unit`: called for back, Escape, a click on the scrim, a drag towards the edge and the side sheet's close button while `dismissible`. The sheet stays until `visible` is false.
- `title: String?`: what the sheet is for, as a short label: "Sort by". It is announced when the sheet appears and is its heading. Null or blank for none: no line is kept for it, the content starts under the handle, and a screen reader announces no name when the sheet appears. A side sheet's close button still stands at its top.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the sheet itself. The strip of scrim kept clear beside it is no part of it.
- `edge: SheetEdge`: the edge of the window the sheet lies along: the bottom, the end, the start, or by the window's width (`SheetEdge.Adaptive`), full screen from the bottom in a narrow one. `halfOpen`, `fullScreen`, `coverStatusBar` and `overscrollMovesSheet` count for an adaptive sheet where it comes from the bottom.
- `dismissible: Boolean`: whether back, Escape, a click on the scrim, a drag towards the edge, the side sheet's close button and a screen reader's dismiss action ask to close. Turn it off only when a control in `content` must close the sheet.
- `halfOpen: Boolean`: whether the sheet first opens half open, its top at the middle of the window, when what it holds is taller than that. A drag up opens it fully, and so does focus moving into it; a drag down from half open closes it. Along the bottom edge only.
- `fullScreen: Boolean`: whether the fully open sheet is as tall as the window under the status bar however short its content, with no scrim above it. Like every sheet along the bottom edge it reaches the window's bottom edge, under the system's navigation bar, and keeps what it holds above that bar. Along the bottom edge only.
- `coverStatusBar: Boolean`: whether a `fullScreen` sheet reaches under the status bar too, fully open as tall as the whole window. Its top corners square off as it slides under the bar, its handle and title stay below the bar, and on Android the bar's icons turn to read against the sheet where it is as wide as the window. Along the bottom edge and with `fullScreen` only.
- `overscrollMovesSheet: Boolean`: whether a drag down on content that is already at its top goes on to move the sheet down: to half open, then closed. Turn it off for a list that should only scroll; the handle and the title still drag the sheet, and a drag up on the content still opens a half-open sheet. Along the bottom edge only.
- `scrollContent: Boolean`: whether the sheet puts `content` in a scroll area under the title. Turn it off for content that scrolls itself, such as a `LazyColumn`, which cannot sit in a scroll area: `content` then gets the height left under the title, and its scrolling still opens a half-open sheet and moves the sheet down past its top. Give a `LazyColumn` `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`: a list is only as wide as the rows on screen, and a drag beside them would not scroll it.
- `style: SheetStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SheetColors?`: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the sheet's tag is `Sheet_<tagKey>`, on the sheet as it is drawn, and the side sheet's close button is `SheetClose_<tagKey>`.
- `content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit`: what the sheet holds, under the title.

Documented on: [Sheet](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/sheet.md)

### SheetEdge

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.sheet.SheetEdge`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SheetEdge
```

The edge of the window a `PantrixSheet` lies along.

Entries:

- `Bottom`: The bottom edge. The sheet is as wide as the window up to the style's `maxWidth` and as tall as what it holds, and a drag down closes it.
- `End`: The end edge, the left one in a right-to-left layout. The sheet is as tall as the window and the style's `sideWidth` wide, and a drag towards the edge closes it.
- `Start`: The start edge, the right one in a right-to-left layout: an app's menu, which a narrow window keeps in a sheet rather than beside its content. The sheet is as tall as the window and the style's `sideWidth` wide, and a drag towards the edge closes it.
- `Adaptive`: The bottom edge in a narrow window, the `Compact` width class, as a full-screen sheet, and the end edge in every wider one: a form or the details of what was pressed, which fill a phone and stand beside the content on a tablet or a desktop. The window is the one the sheet is shown over, and it is asked as the sheet opens: one that is open stays as it is when the window changes.

Documented on: [Sheet](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/sheet.md)

### SheetStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.sheet.SheetStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SheetStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val maxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sideWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val margin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val elevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handleHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val handlePadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<SheetStyle>
```

`PantrixSheet`'s geometry.

The space between the handle, the title and the content comes from the theme's spacing, so it follows density, and so do the margin and the room around the handle. The widths, the corners, the shadow and the handle itself do not. A sheet's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `SheetColors` where a call has its own.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The corners that face the app: the top two of a sheet along the bottom edge, the start two of one along the end edge. The corners at the window's edge are square. Large on Android and iOS, medium on desktop and the web.
- `maxWidth: Dp`: The widest a sheet along the bottom edge gets; in a wider window it stays in the middle of the edge.
- `sideWidth: Dp`: How wide a sheet along the end edge is, where the window leaves it that room.
- `margin: Dp`: Kept clear between the sheet and the far side of the window, so that the scrim still shows there and a tap on it closes the sheet: above a tall sheet along the bottom edge, beside a sheet along the end edge in a narrow window. It is a target for a tap, so it is each platform's smallest touch target.
- `elevation: Dp`: How high the sheet floats over the scrim, which is how large its shadow is. None on iOS.
- `handleWidth: Dp`: How long the drag handle is, which a sheet along the bottom edge draws while a drag can move it.
- `handleHeight: Dp`: How thick the drag handle is: `handleWidth` is how long it is.
- `handlePadding: Dp`: Above and below the handle.

Documented on: [Sheet](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/sheet.md)

### SnackbarTone

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.snackbar.SnackbarTone`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SnackbarTone
```

What a snackbar is telling the user: one of the theme's colour roles, which also decides its icon and how it is announced.

The semantic tones, `Info`, `Success`, `Warning` and `Danger`, reach the user as colour and as an icon, because colour alone fails anyone who cannot see it. `Primary` and `Neutral` carry no meaning of their own, and have no icon.

A snackbar is filled in every tone, from the role's `color` and `onColor` rather than its pale `container`: it floats over the app's own content for a few seconds, and a pale bar would read as one more card on the page. `Primary` takes the brand's `primary` role. `Neutral` takes the `neutral` role, a grey with no hue of its own, which Pantrix's colours keep darker than the page in the light theme and lighter than it in the dark one.

Entries:

- `Info`: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.
- `Success`: Something that worked: saved, sent, uploaded.
- `Warning`: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.
- `Danger`: Something that failed. The one tone announced assertively: it interrupts what a screen reader is saying.
- `Primary`: Something the app wants noticed, in the brand's colour, without an icon: a new version ready to install, a feature to try.
- `Neutral`: Something the app did: a grey bar, without an icon. The default.

Documented on: [Snackbar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/snackbar.md)

### PantrixSnackbarState

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.snackbar.PantrixSnackbarState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PantrixSnackbarState
```

The snackbars an app asks for: one on screen at a time, the others waiting their turn in the order they were asked for.

A `PantrixSnackbarHost` puts them on screen. Keep one state for the part of the app one host covers, usually the whole app, so snackbars from any screen queue behind each other.

Members:

- `current: SnackbarData?`: The snackbar on screen, or null.
- `suspend fun show(message: String, actionLabel: String? = null, duration: SnackbarDuration = if (actionLabel == null) { SnackbarDuration.Short } else { SnackbarDuration.UntilDismissed }, closeButton: Boolean = duration == SnackbarDuration.UntilDismissed, tone: SnackbarTone = SnackbarTone.Neutral, tagKey: String? = null): SnackbarResult`: Shows a snackbar once the snackbars asked for before it have left, and returns how it left.

  Cancelling the coroutine that called it takes the snackbar away, or drops it before its turn.

  `message`: what happened, in a short sentence: "Conversation archived".

  `actionLabel`: a short verb for the one thing the user can do about it: "Undo".

  `duration`: how long the snackbar stays when nobody acts on it. A snackbar with an action stays until the user acts on it or closes it: a few seconds are too few for some people to reach the action.

  `closeButton`: whether the snackbar has a close button. A snackbar that stays until it is dismissed has one.

  `tone`: what the snackbar is telling the user: its colours, an icon for a semantic tone, and for an error an assertive announcement.

  `tagKey`: the snackbar's automation key: the snackbar is `Snackbar_<tagKey>`, its action `SnackbarAction_<tagKey>` and its close button `SnackbarClose_<tagKey>`.

Documented on: [Snackbar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/snackbar.md)

### PantrixSnackbarHost

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.snackbar.PantrixSnackbarHost`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSnackbarHost(
    state: PantrixSnackbarState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    style: SnackbarStyle? = null,
    colors: SnackbarColors? = null
)
```

Puts the snackbars of `state` on screen: short messages about what the app has just done, each with at most one action, in a neutral, primary or semantic tone, one at a time.

Put the host over the app, as the last child of a `Box` that fills the window, so snackbars appear above the content; `PantrixScaffold`, given the state, does that itself, between its bars. The host fills the space it is given and places each snackbar by `SnackbarStyle.placement` inside the window's safe area: in the middle of the bottom edge on Android, at the top on iOS, in the bottom end corner on desktop and the web. A snackbar belongs to the app, not to a dialog or a sheet, and one of those opened over the host covers its snackbars.

Beside an upright fold, a foldable held like a book or a hinge between two screens, a snackbar keeps to a half and never lies across the fold: one in the bottom end corner to the end half, every other one to the start half, in the middle of it or in its corner as it is placed. A snackbar as wide as a phone's window, in a corner too, would reach past the fold otherwise.

A snackbar never takes focus and never blocks the app; a screen reader announces it without interrupting, and one in the `SnackbarTone.Danger` tone assertively. It leaves after its `SnackbarDuration`, which waits while the pointer is over it, focus is inside it or it is being dragged, and then starts again, or when the user presses its action or its close button, swipes it sideways, presses Escape with focus inside it, or uses a screen reader's dismiss action.

Parameters:

- `state: PantrixSnackbarState`: the snackbars to show; `PantrixSnackbarState.show` asks for one.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the host's modifier. The host fills the space it is given.
- `style: SnackbarStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: SnackbarColors?`: the colours of every snackbar this host shows, where they are not their tones': the ones set here, with the tone's for the rest.

Documented on: [Snackbar](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/snackbar.md)

## Package com.pantrixui.components.overlay.tooltip

### PantrixTooltipState

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.tooltip.PantrixTooltipState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PantrixTooltipState
```

Whether a `PantrixTooltip` is up, and the handle that brings it up and puts it away.

A tooltip brings itself up when a pointer rests on what it names, when that takes the keyboard's focus and when a press is held on it, and it goes as the pointer or the focus leaves, on a press and on Escape. Every one of those throws this one switch, so `visible` is the whole truth about the tooltip.

A screen that shows one of its own accord, a hint on the first run or a name beside a control it has just changed, holds the state itself and calls `show` and `dismiss`:

```kotlin
val hint = rememberPantrixTooltipState()
LaunchedEffect(firstRun) { if (firstRun) hint.show() }
PantrixTooltip(text = stringResource(Res.string.refresh), state = hint, tagKey = "refresh") {
    PantrixIconButton(imageVector = PantrixIcons.Refresh, contentDescription = …, onClick = onRefresh)
}
```

Hold it with `rememberPantrixTooltipState`.

Members:

- `visible: Boolean`: Whether the tooltip is up. A tooltip that is turned off, or whose control is under a dialog or another modal layer, is put away, and this is false then.
- `fun show()`: Brings the tooltip up. Showing one that is up changes nothing.
- `fun dismiss()`: Puts the tooltip away. Dismissing one that is away changes nothing.
- `fun toggle()`: Puts the tooltip away where it is up, and brings it up where it is not.

Documented on: [Tooltip](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tooltip.md)

### rememberPantrixTooltipState

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.tooltip.rememberPantrixTooltipState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberPantrixTooltipState(initiallyVisible: Boolean = false): PantrixTooltipState
```

Remembers a `PantrixTooltipState`. Give it to `PantrixTooltip` to show and hide that tooltip from the screen around it.

Parameters:

- `initiallyVisible: Boolean`: whether the tooltip is up the first time it is composed.

### PantrixTooltip

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.tooltip.PantrixTooltip`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTooltip(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    side: PopoverSide = PopoverSide.Top,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    state: PantrixTooltipState = rememberPantrixTooltipState(),
    style: TooltipStyle? = null,
    colors: TooltipColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    anchor: @Composable () -> Unit
)
```

A short label that names the control it is anchored to: an icon button's name, a truncated label in full.

It shows what the control already says. A screen reader reads the control itself and the label is hidden from it: a tooltip is a way of showing a name, not a place for anything new. Give the control the same words, as its `contentDescription` or its text.

It comes up by itself and takes nothing from the app: no focus and no key, and no press but one on the label itself and the one that is held to ask for it. What it names keeps working while it is up, and so does whatever is pressed to put it away.

- **A pointer** brings it up once it has rested on the control for the style's `pointerRestMillis`, and takes it away as it leaves. It may cross onto the label and rest there: the label stays while the pointer is on either. A mouse button on the control puts it away until the pointer has left and come back.

- **The keyboard's focus** brings it up at once, where a focus ring is drawn, and takes it away as it leaves. Escape puts it away while the control keeps the focus.

- **A press that is held**, a finger's long press on the control, brings it up, and it stays until something is pressed: one that left with the finger would never be read. That press asked what the control is and presses nothing as it lifts. A tap is the control's alone and brings nothing up, and a press that travels is the start of a scroll.

`state` is the switch all of these throw, and a screen can throw it too.

It sits on `side` of the control, centred on it, on the opposite side where the window has no room for it, and never closer than the style's margin to the window's edges, its system bars or the keyboard. It is put away while its control is under a dialog, a sheet or an open popover, when its control scrolls out of view, and when the window changes size.

Parameters:

- `text: String`: what the control is called: a few words, and the ones the control itself says.
- `modifier: Modifier`: applied to the control's place, the box the control is laid out in where the tooltip is called: an alignment or a weight there places the control, and the label goes with it.
- `side: PopoverSide`: the side of the control the tooltip prefers. `PopoverSide.Start` and `PopoverSide.End` follow the layout direction.
- `enabled: Boolean`: false puts it away and keeps it away, for a control whose name is already in view.
- `state: PantrixTooltipState`: whether the tooltip is up, and the handle that shows and hides it.
- `style: TooltipStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TooltipColors?`: this call's own colours. Only the ones it sets change; the rest stay the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent key for automation: the label's tag is `Tooltip_<tagKey>`.
- `anchor: @Composable () -> Unit`: the control the tooltip names, laid out where this is called and as that place asks. A control that is pressed, a button or an icon, or a text that is only read: one with a long press of its own, a text field or text that can be selected, would have that press taken from it on a touch screen.

Documented on: [Tooltip](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tooltip.md)

### TooltipStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.tooltip.TooltipStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TooltipStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val margin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val elevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val pointerRestMillis: Int? = null
) : PantrixStyle<TooltipStyle>
```

`PantrixTooltip`'s geometry: how large the label is, how far it sits from what it names, how close it comes to the edges of the window, and how long a pointer rests on a control before its tooltip appears.

The padding around the text, the gap and the margin follow density. The widest width, the corners, the shadow and the pointer's rest do not. A tooltip's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `TooltipColors` where a call has its own.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The label's corners.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: Between the text and the label's start and end edges.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: Between the text and the label's top and bottom edges.
- `maxWidth: Dp`: The widest the label gets: longer text wraps.
- `gap: Dp`: Between what the tooltip names and the tooltip.
- `margin: Dp`: Kept clear between the tooltip and the edges of the window, and of what covers the window there: a system bar, a cutout, the keyboard.
- `elevation: Dp`: How high the label floats over the app, which is how large its shadow is.
- `pointerRestMillis: Int?`: How long a pointer rests on a control before its tooltip appears, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus shows it at once, and a finger's long press as long as the platform takes one to be: this is the pointer's wait alone. `null` leaves the value of the style underneath in place.

Documented on: [Tooltip](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tooltip.md)

### TooltipColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.tooltip.TooltipColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class TooltipColors(
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixTooltip` is painted with, for a call that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
PantrixTooltip(text = name, colors = TooltipColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color)) { … }
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the text, unless a `content` colour is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The label's fill. The theme's `onSurface`: the tone opposite the theme's grounds, so that the label stands out over whatever the page shows under it, in the light theme and the dark.
- `content: Color`: The label's text. The theme's `textInverse`, which is what reads on that tone.

Documented on: [Tooltip](https://develappsancho.github.io/pantrix-ui-cmp-package/pages/tooltip.md)
